comments.title: Overhead Electric Clearance Documentation Missing from Plans
comments.comment: The plans provide no clearance dimensions, profile views, cross-arm exhibits, or clearance envelope exhibits for existing overhead electric facilities along the Valley View Road frontage.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.16.0(2) require comprehensive clearance documentation for all overhead electric facilities. The following are absent from the submitted plan set:
- No clearance dimensions annotated on any sheet for buildings, structures, driveways, or other site features relative to overhead electric lines; when dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not the utility pole centerline
- No electrical section/profile views showing existing pole heights, all conductor elevations, and clearance envelopes (7.5-ft horizontal minimum per UCM § 1.10.3)
- No plan-and-section-view exhibit showing utility poles with cross-arm dimensions (~8 ft wide) and measured distances from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings
- No exhibits documenting AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes (7.5-ft horizontal, 15-ft radial for distribution; greater for transmission) in relation to existing overhead facilities and proposed structures
- No plan-and-profile cross-section views showing vertical separation between overhead conductors and building rooflines
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Southern and western property boundaries where overhead electric (OHE) lines run along Valley View Road frontage; all proposed buildings and site features within proximity of overhead facilities
comments.resolution: Add clearance dimension callouts on Sheets 9 and 21 for all buildings, structures, driveways, and site features relative to the overhead electric lines, with dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not the pole centerline), identified by label. Provide a section-and-plan-view exhibit for each overhead line corridor showing: existing pole heights, all conductor elevations, cross-arm dimensions (~8 ft), and clearance envelopes per AE, NESC, and OSHA standards (minimum 7.5-ft horizontal, 15-ft radial for distribution conductors). Include plan-and-profile cross-sections showing vertical separation between conductor heights and proposed building rooflines.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Sub-items for profile views, cross-arm exhibit, and clearance envelope exhibits were flagged by only 1 of 3 runs each; verify full scope of required clearance exhibits against UCM § 1.10.2 and § 1.10.3 before issuing comment.

perRunFindings.comment: All clearance annotations must be revised to show dimension lines originating at the surveyed outside conductor location (not pole center), with clear identification of which conductor is being measured from, and dimension values showing clearances in feet and inches from the conductor to site features.
applicableAreas: All proposed site features and infrastructure
perRunFindings.observation: Complete review of Sheets 9 (Site Plan), 11 (Grading Plan), and 21 (Electrical Plan) reveals NO dimension annotations showing clearances from buildings, structures, driveways, walls, or other site features to overhead electric lines. The only distances shown are from property lines and internal site features to each other. Sheet 4 shows the existing utility poles with symbols but no dimension annotations from the poles. No dimension lines on any sheet are shown extending from an identified 'outside conductor' location to site features. Applicant has not labeled the location of outside conductors or the measurement reference point for any clearance annotations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: All clearance dimensions (or lack thereof) must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole center or pole structure. No clearance dimensions are provided on the plans at all, and no plans identify the location of the outside conductor for measurement purposes.

perRunFindings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on site plans, measured from outside conductor as required. All clearance dimensions must originate from the actual conductor location, with notation showing measurement source.
applicableAreas: All locations with clearance dimensions shown on overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 shows the OHE line on the southern boundary of the site but includes NO dimension callouts or clearance annotations of any kind. Wherever clearance dimensions should appear (from conductor to buildings, parking, driveways), none are provided. The few dimension lines visible on Sheet 9 relate to building setbacks and site distances, not to overhead line clearances. The critical requirement to show dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location (not pole centerline) is therefore not met—because no dimensions are shown at all.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires clearance dimensions to be measured from the outside conductor, never from the utility pole centerline. On multi-conductor installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center, creating significant measurement errors if pole-based dimensions are used. The applicant has not provided any clearance dimensions from any overhead electric infrastructure. This is a foundational deficiency—without dimension callouts originating from the conductor, the plans cannot communicate or verify clearance compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance dimensions are not shown on any plan sheets. When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. Dimension lines should clearly identify the conductor location and show measurement to the building edge or feature being evaluated.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations on site plan
perRunFindings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows multiple utility poles and overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) on the property. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows the overhead electric line (OHE) running along the Valley View Road frontage. However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on the plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Measurement Methodology section: 'Profile plans must show dimension lines originating at the conductor location, not at the pole. [This is critical.]' The complete absence of clearance dimensions means there is no opportunity to verify that dimensions originate from the conductor rather than the pole.

perRunFindings.comment: Section views showing existing electrical pole heights, all conductor elevations, and required clearance envelopes (minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance) are not provided. Please provide detailed electrical profile/section views showing all existing overhead facilities with heights and clearance demonstrations.
applicableAreas: All elevation/profile views with existing overhead facilities in proximity
perRunFindings.observation: Examined available section and elevation sheets. Sheet 21 references 'See Sheet 19 for Profile' but vision analysis of Sheet 19 found NO profile views present—only plan view with notes. No dedicated section views showing heights, conductor spacing, or clearance envelopes were located on Sheet 19. No profile sheets explicitly showing existing electrical pole heights and all conductors were found in the available plan set. While Sheet 3 contains transmission clearance notes, no graphical cross-sections or elevation views demonstrating pole heights and clearance envelopes are present.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires section views to show 'height of existing electrical poles and all conductors with clearance envelopes.' Although section views exist in the plan set (e.g., storm sewer profiles on other sheets), the electrical profile information referenced on Sheet 21 is not provided.

perRunFindings.comment: No section and plan view exhibit is provided showing utility poles with cross arm dimensions and distances to proposed buildings/structures. Design must provide this exhibit with specific dimensions documenting compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification for proposed buildings near existing utility poles with cross arms
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles and overhead utility lines. The poles are shown with cross arm symbols (approximately 8 feet wide for standard distribution poles). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations. However, no section or plan view exhibit is provided that shows the utility poles with cross arms (8 feet width) and dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a 'section and plan view exhibit showing utility poles with cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide) and dimensions from outer conductor to outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.' This exhibit is a fundamental documentation requirement for verifying compliance with the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance requirements from overhead distribution lines.

perRunFindings.comment: No clearance exhibits are provided showing AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes in relation to existing overhead facilities and proposed buildings. Exhibits must be provided documenting the clearance envelopes required by applicable standards (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial for distribution; larger for transmission).
applicableAreas: Clearance verification areas where proposed buildings are near overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Existing overhead distribution poles and lines are documented on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey). No clearance exhibits are provided in the site plan set. The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed underground equipment but does not address existing overhead facilities or clearance envelopes.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.10.2 require that clearance exhibits document AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes. These envelopes define the three-dimensional space that must be maintained clear of obstructions around energized conductors for safety. The applicant has not provided any exhibits showing these clearance envelopes in relation to proposed structures.

perRunFindings.comment: Plan and profile views not submitted to verify required clearances between existing overhead electric lines and proposed buildings. Provide plan and profile cross-sections showing vertical separation between overhead conductors and building structures, with dimensions confirming 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Proposed buildings 1-8 relative to existing overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheets 9, 21, and 31 show the locations of the proposed buildings relative to these overhead facilities in plan view. However, NO PLAN AND PROFILE VIEWS have been provided that show the vertical (profile) relationship between the existing overhead electric lines and the proposed buildings.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Plan view alone is insufficient to verify clearance compliance between overhead conductors and building structures. Profile views are required to show the vertical separation between conductor height and building height/roofline. Without these profile views with dimensions, the clearance requirement of 7.5 feet horizontal and 15-foot radial separation cannot be verified.

comments.title: Underground Electric Facilities Lack Required 5-Foot Clearance from Building Foundations
comments.comment: Proposed underground electric conduit routed to wall-mounted meters on all 8 buildings necessarily enters the required 5-foot exclusion zone at every meter connection, no clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheet, and the plans do not confirm that underground lines avoid routing beneath building footprints.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from AE underground electric facilities to customer building foundations and permanent structures, and prohibits buildings from being constructed over AE underground facilities. The following deficiencies are present:
- Underground electric conduit routed to wall-mounted meters on all 8 buildings must approach building walls within the 5-foot exclusion zone at each meter connection; some conduit (at Buildings 2 and 8 where meters are in recessed notches) appears to route directly beneath or against foundation walls
- Transformer pads near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 have no clearance dimension callouts verifying the required 5-foot separation from building foundations
- No dimensioned exhibits on any plan sheet document horizontal clearances between proposed underground conduit and building foundations, other underground utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain), or drainage features
- Plans do not confirm that underground electric lines avoid passing beneath any of the 8 building footprints; branch lines to wall-mounted meters may require routing through or beneath building slabs
- Clearance from transmission structures (25-ft no-excavation zone noted on Sheet 3) is not dimensioned on the electrical plan
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 buildings (Buildings 1–8); underground electric routing throughout site; transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8; crossing points with water, wastewater, and storm drain lines
comments.resolution: Add clearance dimension callouts on Sheet 21 (and Sheets 9, 11, and 19 as applicable) showing the horizontal distance from all proposed underground electric conduit, transformer pads, and pull boxes to the nearest building foundation, confirming minimum 5-foot clearance at every location. For the 8 meter connections where conduit approaches building walls, either demonstrate with dimensions that 5-foot clearance is maintained in the final design, or provide coordination documentation from Austin Energy Design authorizing any reduced clearance under a license agreement with sealed engineering and metal conduit sleeves. Add clearance dimensions between underground electric and all crossing or parallel underground utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Confirm on plan that no underground electric line passes beneath any building footprint.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Locations where the 5-foot clearance cannot be maintained may require coordination with Austin Energy Design for license agreement approval and sealed engineering documentation.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: The core violation at meter connections is high-confidence (3/3 runs); sub-items regarding conduit beneath footprints and clearances from other utilities are medium-to-low confidence and may benefit from field verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical conduit branch lines route directly to electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings. No dimensional callouts on the electrical plan verify that the required 5-foot horizontal clearance from building foundations to underground electric facilities is maintained at meter connection locations.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters mounted on the exterior walls of all 8 buildings. Branch conduit lines must route from the main underground electrical trunk lines to these wall-mounted meters. Vision analysis confirmed that electrical routing approaches and connects directly to these meters, with the branch lines definitely entering the area within 5 feet of building foundations at all meter connection locations. No dimensional callouts verify that the 5-foot horizontal clearance is maintained.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Building foundations must maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities per UCM § 1.10.5.B. The electrical meters mounted directly on the exterior walls require electrical service lines to run to those wall locations. Without explicit dimensional documentation showing the 5-foot clearance is maintained, compliance cannot be verified.

perRunFindings.comment: All eight building foundations have underground electric conduit routing within 5 feet (typically within 0 to 2 feet) of building walls to serve wall-mounted electrical meters. This violates the required 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations.
perRunFindings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (scale 1" = 20') reveals that electrical meters are mounted directly on the building foundation walls for all eight buildings. Underground electric conduit routing to these meters is shown running immediately adjacent to (and in some cases directly against) the building foundation walls. The electrical conduit serving each meter breaches the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone and runs within inches of the building foundations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to customer buildings and foundations. The presence of wall-mounted meters inherently requires conduit to enter the building within the 5-foot zone. This is not a design that coordinates with the clearance requirement—it fundamentally violates it.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical transformer pads are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8, but no horizontal clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from building foundations.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows five electrical transformer pads positioned on the site. No horizontal clearance dimensions are shown between any of the transformer pads and the building foundations or walls. The Utility Notes on Sheet 21 state that 'Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities prior to construction,' but this is a general directive rather than a demonstration of compliance.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that building foundations maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities including transformer pads. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant through the site plan documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical routing shown on the plans traverses the site to connect to building-mounted meters and runs through internal site corridors. No explicit documentation verifies that no underground electric facilities pass beneath the footprints of any of the 8 buildings.
applicableAreas: Building footprints relative to underground electric routing
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 shows footprints of all 8 buildings. Sheets 19 and 21 show proposed electric line routing throughout the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted that main trunk lines route primarily around the outer perimeter, but branch lines connect to meters on each building and internal routing passes between buildings. No explicit documentation verifying that no electric facilities pass under any building foundations was found.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Customer buildings and permanent structures shall not be installed over Austin Energy underground facilities per UCM § 1.10.5.B. Without explicit documentation verifying that no electric facilities pass beneath any building foundations, compliance cannot be confirmed.

perRunFindings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing to serve wall-mounted electrical meters on all eight buildings would require conduit to pass beneath or through building foundations, which violates UCM § 1.10.5.B. Relocate electrical meters to pedestals or external equipment enclosures outside building footprints, or coordinate with Austin Energy Design to document a license agreement and sealed engineering design if conduit must pass through building foundations.
perRunFindings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 shows that underground electric conduit is routed to and directly beneath building foundations to serve electrical meters mounted on building walls. In some cases (Buildings 2, 8), the meters are mounted in recessed notches in the building walls, requiring conduit to route into these recessed areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Wall-mounted electrical meters inherently require underground conduit to be routed to the building. When buildings are designed with slab-on-grade construction, conduit routing beneath the slab violates the prohibition. The routing of conduit as the primary service to wall-mounted meters is not addressed by any applicable exception without a license agreement and engineering.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance dimensions for electric facilities not documented on plans. Add clearance dimensions to the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan showing that all proposed electrical facilities (transformers, conductors, meter pedestals, service lines) maintain required clearances from buildings, drainage features, trees, and other structures per UCM § 1.16.0(2) and National Electric Safety Code standards.
perRunFindings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical equipment (transformers, meters, pull boxes) and underground routing but does not include specific clearance dimensions or annotations demonstrating compliance with safety clearance standards. Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement clearance requirements (noting no digging within 25 feet, no trees within 25 feet, 20-foot clearance for equipment) but the site plan does not dimension these clearances for verification.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2). This includes clearances per the National Electric Safety Code and City of Austin requirements.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for electric facilities. Sheet 21 lacks dimensioned clearance information for proposed electric infrastructure. Add clearance dimensions to electrical plans showing: (1) minimum setbacks of transformer pads and pull boxes from buildings per NEC standards, (2) clearances from all drainage features per UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.7, (3) clearances from other utilities, (4) 25-foot clearance from transmission structures, and (5) clearance maintenance areas accessible for Austin Energy.
applicableAreas: Electric facility clearances on site plan
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground routing with location labels but NO clearance dimensions are shown. Vision analysis confirmed absence of clearance callouts, setback dimensions from buildings, property lines, drainage features, or other infrastructure. The transmission line requirements on Sheet 3 Block 20 specify clearances (25 feet from structures, 20 feet for aerial equipment/staging) but these are notes, not dimensioned on electrical drawings.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per design and safety standards. The complete absence of dimensioned clearances fails to meet this requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Underground electric cable and conduit clearances from buildings, foundations, and permanent structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details on utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from all AE underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: Underground electric conduit routing throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines routing throughout the site. The vision analysis confirmed that there are no dimension lines or notes showing the clearances from the underground electric conduit to customer buildings, foundations, permanent structures, or other utilities.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires minimum 60-inch (5-foot) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer buildings, foundations, or permanent structures. The existence of underground electric lines on the plan does not constitute compliance documentation; the clearances must be explicitly shown and dimensioned.

perRunFindings.comment: No exhibit is provided with dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing. Design must provide dimensioned drawings showing the distance from each building footprint to the proposed underground electric conduit and lines, demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.5 (minimum 60 inches from customer buildings).
applicableAreas: Proposed underground electric routing between and near proposed buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed underground electric lines (blue lines) routing from the property boundary to four transformer pads and then daisy-chaining to building meter banks. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings. The relationships shown are purely graphical.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that 'an exhibit be provided showing dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing.' Without dimensioned exhibits, the applicant has not demonstrated that the underground routing will comply with clearance standards.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide dimensioned underground utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from proposed underground electric conduit to all building foundations and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5. If any location has less than 60 inches, provide alternative routing or written approval from Austin Energy Design.
applicableAreas: Underground electric lines routing to buildings and electrical equipment
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines routing from the property boundary through the center of the site, connecting to the four transformer pads and daisy-chaining to building meter banks. Vision analysis found: 'There are no dimensions shown indicating the clearance or offset distance of the underground electrical routing from the building foundations or other structures.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 60 inches (5 feet) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer building foundations and permanent structures. Without dimensioned drawings showing the distance of the underground lines from building foundations, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not include clearance dimensions between the underground electric lines and buildings, permanent structures, or other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric line routing, transformer pad locations, and meter locations but does not include clearance dimensions between buildings, permanent structures (retaining walls, fences), other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain lines), and the electric facilities. Sheet 19 shows water, wastewater, and storm drain crossing electric line locations but does not provide clearance dimensions. No profile sheets showing vertical clearances between electric lines and other utilities are evident.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that plans 'demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities.' The requirement is to show 'Clearance dimensions shown for buildings, permanent structures, and other utilities relative to electric facilities.' The absence of clearance callouts and dimensions constitutes non-compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to all plan sheets showing sufficient clearances between electrical facilities (transformers, meters, conduit, overhead lines) and buildings, other utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.16.0(2). Provide dimensions per UCM § 1.10.3 (overhead clearances) and UCM § 1.10.4 (padmount equipment clearances).
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21, Sheet 9, and Sheet 31 for clearance dimensions between electrical facilities and other structures. No dimension callouts or clearance notes are shown between transformer pads and buildings, between overhead electric lines and buildings/structures, between underground conduit and other utilities, or between electrical equipment and landscaping. No clearance specifications per UCM § 1.10.3 or UCM § 1.10.4 are noted on any sheet.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans to demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. The absence of clearance dimensions or specifications creates uncertainty about whether electrical facilities meet minimum setback requirements.

comments.title: Electrical Pull Boxes Lack Documented 5-Foot Clearance from Buildings and Property Line
comments.comment: Eight electrical pull boxes are shown on Sheet 21 without any clearance dimensions verifying the required 5-foot minimum from all sides, and at least four appear to be positioned within 5 feet of building corners based on visual scale inspection.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires pull boxes to be located inside the property line and maintain 5-foot clearance from all sides. None of the 8 pull boxes shown on Sheet 21 has dimensional callouts confirming these requirements. Visual inspection at 1" = 20' scale identified pull boxes at Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8 appearing to be within 5 feet of building corners (estimated 2–4 feet based on graphic position). Pull boxes require clear working space for maintenance access; proximity to structures creates both code and operational conflicts.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 pull box locations throughout site — near transformer pad west of Building 1, south of Building 2, west of Building 8, north of Building 3, east of Building 5, east of Building 6, south of Building 7, and northeast of Building 4
comments.resolution: Add clearance dimension callouts on Sheet 21 for each of the 8 pull box locations showing: (1) distance to the nearest building foundation or corner, and (2) distance to the nearest property line. Confirm all pull boxes are inside the property line and maintain a minimum 5-foot clearance on all sides. Relocate any pull boxes that cannot maintain the required clearances.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Runs 1 and 3 were 'unclear' (no dimensions to confirm violations); run-2 identified probable violations at Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8 based on visual estimation at 1" = 20' scale — field or scaled measurement should confirm before requiring relocation.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical plan shows 8 pull box locations but does not document that each pull box is located inside the property line and maintains 5-foot clearance from all sides. Provide dimensional callouts or a coordination note verifying all pull box locations meet the property line and clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Pull box locations throughout site perimeter and interior
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical pull boxes labeled at various positions around the site. However, the electrical plan contains no dimensional callouts or annotations verifying that each pull box is (1) located inside the property line and (2) maintains 5 feet clearance from all sides.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Pull boxes must be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B. While the pull boxes are shown on the electrical plan, there is no documentation verifying these requirements are met.

perRunFindings.comment: Four electrical pull boxes (near Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8) are positioned within 5 feet of building foundations and corners. Relocate pull boxes to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B.
perRunFindings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 reveals electrical pull boxes in close proximity to building foundations: (1) Building 1: Pull box at southwest corner, appearing to be within 5 feet (visually estimated 2-4 feet); (2) Building 4: Pull box to the northeast near Unit 404, close to the east foundation line; (3) Building 7: Pull box at southeast corner near Unit 704, appearing to be within 5 feet; (4) Building 8: Pull box at northwest corner near Unit 801, appearing to be within 5 feet.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires pull boxes to maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides, including from building foundations. The visual positioning of pull boxes at or within building corners at the 1" = 20' scale indicates they fail to maintain the required 5-foot clearance zone.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical pull boxes are shown on the preliminary electrical design plan in eight locations around the site perimeter, but no clearance dimensions or verification are provided demonstrating that they are located inside the property line and maintain the required 5-foot minimum distance from all sides.
applicableAreas: Electrical pull box locations distributed throughout site perimeter
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 clearly identifies eight electrical pull box locations using callout boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' with leader lines pointing to small nodes on the blue underground electric lines. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, clearance arcs, or written notes indicating the horizontal distance of these pull boxes from property lines or from adjacent site features.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that pull boxes be located inside the property line and maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides. Without dimension callouts or verification notes, compliance cannot be confirmed.

comments.title: One Meter Per Building Instead of Required Individual Unit Meters for 39 Townhome Units
comments.comment: The electrical design provides one meter location per building for the 8-building, 39-unit townhome development, but the plans do not document individual service drops and separate meters for each residential unit as required by Austin Energy standards.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.8 requires each individual unit to have a separate service drop and meter per Austin Energy standards. Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations (one per building), with each building containing approximately 3–5 of the 39 townhome units. Whether the depicted meter banks constitute gang meters with individual unit service drops, or building-level consolidated service, is not documented. No Austin Energy Design approval for the proposed metering configuration has been submitted, and no unified development determination is included in the plan set.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Addressing Plan (Sheet 29)
comments.applicableArea: All 39 townhome units across 8 buildings (Buildings 1–8)
comments.resolution: Revise Sheet 21 to explicitly document that each of the 39 individual townhome units has a separate service drop and individual meter, showing the number of service drops per building corresponding to the unit count. Alternatively, provide written confirmation from Austin Energy Design that the proposed gang meter configuration has been reviewed and approved, including AE approval correspondence and service drop routing details for each unit.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Confirmation of acceptable individual unit metering configuration for multi-unit townhome development typically requires coordination with Austin Energy Design; unified development status determination by Austin Energy may affect which standard applies.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-3 noted that if gang meters include individual unit service drops the requirement may be satisfiable; unified development determination from Austin Energy may affect applicability — verify with AE Design before requiring full redesign.

perRunFindings.comment: The proposed electrical design shows one meter per building serving multiple units, not separate meters and service drops for each individual townhome unit as required by UCM § 1.3.8. Revise the electrical design to provide individual service drops and separate electrical meters for each of the 39 individual townhome units.
applicableAreas: All 39 individual townhome units across 8 buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows eight (8) locations labeled 'Electrical Meters' with one meter assigned to each building. The site plan describes 39 total townhome units distributed across these 8 buildings, with buildings varying in size from 3,290 sf to 4,997 sf. Each building contains approximately 3-5 units. The design provides one electrical meter per building (building-level service), not one meter per individual residential unit.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.8 requires that 'Each individual unit [shall have a] separate service drop and meter as required by AE standards.' The proposed design with one meter per building serving 3-5 units does not provide the required individual unit service drops and meters.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide documentation from Austin Energy Design confirming that each of the 39 townhome units has a separate service drop and individual meter as required by AE standards per UCM § 1.3.8. Include service drop routing details and AE approval correspondence.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 buildings with individual unit meters (gang meters) for 39 townhome units. Vision analysis confirmed: 'There are eight (8) specific callouts reading "Electrical Meters." There is one callout pointing to an exterior wall of every single building...visual hash marks on those banks roughly correspond to the number of units in that specific building, these appear to be clustered individual unit meters (gang meters).' However, no documentation found indicating how many individual service drops are provided per unit, whether each unit has its own service drop, or whether AE approved individual unit meter configuration.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item requires 'Each individual unit lacking separate service drop and meter as required by AE standards' per UCM § 1.3.8. While gang meters are shown, AE requires separate service drops for each unit in multi-unit residential developments. The preliminary design shows meters clustered by building but does not document how many service drops are provided or whether AE Design approved individual service drops per unit.

perRunFindings.comment: Individual unit service configuration unclear. Design shows 8 meter locations for 39 units, but whether each unit has individual service drop and meter per Austin Energy standards is not documented.
perRunFindings.observation: The project proposes 39 multi-family townhome units across 8 buildings. Sheet 21 shows electrical meters labeled for 8 locations (one per building). Sheet 29 is the Addressing Plan showing individual unit addresses, suggesting each unit has a separate address. However, the preliminary electrical design shows 8 meter locations for 39 units, implying not every individual unit has a separate meter.
perRunFindings.reasoning: For multi-unit developments like townhomes, Austin Energy standard practice typically requires separate service drops and meters for each individual unit. The preliminary design shows 8 meters for 39 units, suggesting shared/consolidated service. Without documentation confirming Austin Energy approval, this requirement cannot be verified as met.

comments.title: Meter Locations Not Approved by Austin Energy Metering Group
comments.comment: Proposed meter locations on all 8 buildings have not been reviewed or approved by Austin Energy's Metering Group, and the plans do not demonstrate that meter locations satisfy required siting criteria.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3 requires meter locations to be approved by AE Metering Group and to meet specific siting requirements: located outdoors, readily accessible, on the first floor or ground level, and within line of sight of the AE transformer. No AE Metering Group approval documentation has been submitted, and Sheet 21 does not include meter enclosure specifications, sight-line verification to transformers, or accessibility details demonstrating compliance with these requirements.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Eight building meter locations — Building 1 north wall, Building 2 south wall, Building 3 north wall, Building 4 north wall, Building 5 north wall, Building 6 south wall, Building 7 south wall, Building 8 south wall
comments.resolution: Obtain written approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group (Distribution Metering business unit) for all 8 meter locations and include the approval correspondence in the resubmittal. Revise Sheet 21 to add: meter enclosure type and specifications, confirmation of outdoor and ground-floor mounting, accessible pathway dimensions, and a notation or graphic confirming line-of-sight from each meter bank to its serving transformer.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires written approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group (Distribution Metering), which is a distinct internal Austin Energy coordination from AE Design approval.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2 of 3 runs); AE Metering Group approval may exist but not be included in the submitted document set — confirm with Austin Energy before requiring resubmittal.

perRunFindings.comment: Obtain approval from AE Metering Group for all meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3. Verify each meter is: (1) outdoors, (2) readily accessible, (3) on first floor/ground level, (4) within sight of the AE transformer, and (5) not in prohibited locations (under porches, under overhangs >72 inches, within 3-foot radius of gas meters).
applicableAreas: Eight building locations - individual unit meter locations shown on Sheet 21
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows eight individual 'Electrical Meters' callouts (one for each building). Vision analysis indicated these appear to be individual unit meters (gang meters). However, no documentation found indicating meter locations were discussed with or approved by AE Metering Group. No details provided on Sheet 21 showing that these meter locations meet UCM § 1.9.3 requirements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Meter locations not approved by AE Metering Group per UCM § 1.9.3.' While meters are shown on Sheet 21, no evidence was found that AE Metering Group reviewed and approved these locations, or that the meter locations comply with UCM § 1.9.3 requirements.

perRunFindings.comment: Meter locations shown on preliminary design but approval from Austin Energy Metering Group not documented. No correspondence or approval evidence from AE Metering Group (Distribution Metering) visible in accessible documentation.
applicableAreas: Sheet 21 - 8 meter locations on building exteriors
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations (one per building) labeled as 'Electrical Meters' attached to building exteriors. However, the preliminary design does not show meter specifications, enclosure types, accessibility details, or approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group. No correspondence approving meter locations is visible in accessible documentation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The requirement states 'Meter locations [must be] approved by AE Metering Group per UCM § 1.9.3.' While meter locations are proposed on the preliminary design, approval from Austin Energy's Metering Group is not documented. Written approval from both AE Design and Distribution Metering business unit is required for any exceptions.

comments.title: Meters and Disconnects Not Grouped Within Required 20-Foot Distance with Line of Sight
comments.comment: Electrical meters are distributed across all 8 building locations throughout the 2.16-acre site, separated by 60–150 feet, and no disconnect switches are labeled anywhere on the electrical plan.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires meters and disconnects to be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and within line of sight of each other. Meter-to-transformer separation distances are visually estimated at 30–150 feet for different pairings — significantly exceeding the 20-foot maximum. No disconnect switches are labeled or depicted on Sheet 21 as distinct elements, making compliance with the grouping and distance requirements impossible to verify. Line of sight between transformer pads and some meter banks may be obstructed by building structures at corner locations.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 building meter locations (Buildings 1–8); transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8; electrical service connections throughout site
comments.resolution: Identify and label all electrical disconnect switches as distinct elements on Sheet 21. Add dimension callouts showing the distance between each meter bank and its associated disconnect, confirming separation does not exceed 20 feet. Demonstrate unobstructed line of sight between paired meters and disconnects. Reconfigure the electrical design so that meters and disconnects are grouped in a common location per UCM § 1.9.3.1(I); if an alternative configuration has been authorized by Austin Energy, provide that documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical meters are scattered across multiple building locations throughout the site rather than grouped at a common location. Meters shown on Bldg. 1, Bldg. 2, Bldg. 5, Bldg. 8 areas, and spaces between buildings — separated by 60+ feet, exceeding the 20-foot maximum. No disconnects are shown on the plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical meters distributed across multiple locations: north side of Bldg. 1/3, space between Bldg. 2 and Bldg. 4, east side of Bldg. 5, west side of Bldg. 8, and space between Bldg. 6 and Bldg. 7. At least 5-6 separate meter locations spread across the entire site. No disconnect switches are explicitly shown anywhere. At 1" = 20' scale, the distances between scattered meter locations would be approximately 60-100+ feet.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and line of sight. Meters scattered across multiple buildings throughout the 2.16-acre site cannot comply with the 20-foot maximum distance requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Meters and disconnects not grouped together with documented separation distance. Identify and label all electrical disconnects on the site plan. Show distance measurements between meters and disconnects, documenting that separation does not exceed 20 feet and that meters and disconnects are within line of sight.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 'Electrical Meters' labeled on the exteriors of the eight buildings. However, 'Electrical Disconnects' are NOT explicitly labeled or identified anywhere on the sheet. No dimension lines or distance measurements are shown between meter locations and any disconnect locations. Pull boxes are shown but cannot be confirmed as disconnects.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and within line of sight. Without both meters and disconnects identified and dimensioned, compliance cannot be verified.

perRunFindings.comment: Meters and transformers are not grouped in a common location and are separated by more than 20 feet in multiple instances, exceeding the maximum separation allowed. Some meter/transformer pairs may lack adequate line of sight. Reconfigure electrical infrastructure to group meters and disconnects in common locations within 20 feet of each transformer.
applicableAreas: Transformers 1, 2, and 3 locations; building meter locations
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows three electrical transformer pads and six meter locations (on building exteriors). Vision analysis measured separation distances: Transformer 1 to meters range 30-50 feet; Transformer 2 to meters range 10-150 feet; Transformer 3 to meters range 60-150 feet. Transformers are in standalone pads in easements/common areas while meters are mounted on building walls.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires meters and disconnects to be grouped together in a common location, with maximum 20-foot separation, and within line of sight. The separation distances measured on the electrical plan exceed the 20-foot maximum threshold for multiple transformer/meter combinations.

comments.title: Electrical Design Plan Missing Service Routing, Power Source, and Facility Specifications
comments.comment: Sheet 21 omits the required service routing from existing Austin Energy infrastructure, power source identification for each building, and technical specifications for all proposed electrical facilities, and the proposed design is inconsistently shown across plan sheets.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) and § 1.16.0(5) require proposed electric facilities to be shown with sufficient detail. The following are absent:
- The proposed electrical route from the existing AE connection at the property boundary to proposed transformer pads and building service entrances is not traced, dimensioned, labeled, or supported by a one-line diagram on any sheet
- Power source for proposed buildings is not identified: no callouts indicate which transformer serves which buildings, and no service voltage, amperage, or service type (single/three-phase) is shown for any of the 39 units across 8 buildings
- Technical specifications are absent for all proposed underground infrastructure: conduit sizing and material type, transformer kVA ratings and voltage configurations, distribution line sizes, and pull box dimensions are not labeled on Sheet 21
- Proposed electric facilities are inconsistently shown across plan sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows only one transformer pad with no meters or underground routing; Grading Plan (Sheet 11) shows no electric distribution lines; Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows legend symbols for proposed underground electric and transformer pads but no actual facilities in plan view
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site; all 8 proposed buildings (Buildings 1–8); west property boundary service connection point to all transformer pads and service endpoints
comments.resolution: Provide a one-line electrical schematic or annotated service routing diagram on Sheet 21 tracing the full service path from the AE connection point at the property boundary to each transformer pad and each building's service entrance, with labels identifying intermediate equipment (pull boxes, disconnects). Add an equipment schedule or callout table identifying which transformer serves which buildings, service voltage and type per building group, and projected electrical load (kVA or amperage) per transformer. Add conduit size, material specifications, transformer kVA ratings, and distribution line sizes to all underground routing on Sheet 21. Update Sheets 9, 11, and 19 to consistently depict all proposed electric facilities, or add cross-reference notes directing reviewers to Sheet 21.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electrical routing path from existing service to proposed buildings shown with blue line on Sheet 21, but route lacks dimensional callouts, measurements, turning points, depth changes, and routing specifications necessary for Austin Energy approval.
applicableAreas: West property line from existing service connection to all proposed service points
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electrical route as a blue line originating from existing underground electric line on west side near Valley View Road, connecting to a pull box, then to transformer pads and building service locations. However, the routing lacks explicit dimensioning and callout notations showing the exact path, transition points, depth changes, and equipment relationships.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires the proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service to be explicitly shown on plans. A visual blue line without dimensional documentation is insufficient for design approval.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electrical service route from existing Austin Energy connection to proposed service points is not clearly documented. Please provide: (1) one-line electrical schematic showing service path from AE connection point to each building's service entrance; (2) annotations on site plan showing service routing with arrows and labels; (3) notes identifying which route serves which building; (4) identification of any intermediate disconnect/metering locations.
applicableAreas: From point of connection through entire service routing to all buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows blue conduit lines routing throughout the site, but the routing path from the point of connection to the proposed service point(s)/buildings is not clearly labeled or documented. While conduit lines are drawn, there are no notes, annotations, or callouts explaining the routing path, voltage being carried, or service endpoint. No schematic or one-line diagram shows the electrical service path from AE system to each building.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service [to be] shown.' The current plans show conduit routing graphically but lack the documentation needed to understand which route serves which building, intermediate connection points, or service voltage.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electrical service routing from existing Austin Energy infrastructure to proposed service not shown. Clearly show the routing path for the service entrance, including conduit sizing, length, and routing details from the point of connection to the proposed transformer locations.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines connecting transformers and pull boxes to building meter locations. However, there is no indication of how the service enters the site or connects from the existing AE facilities at the property boundary (shown as 'OHE' lines and poles) to the proposed transformer pads and distribution points on the site.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) specifically requires documentation of 'Proposed electrical route from existing AE service to proposed service.' Without this routing shown, it is unclear whether the service can physically reach the proposed transformer locations or whether adequate space and clearances exist.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed conduit routing shown on Sheet 21, but conduit sizing (pipe diameter, duct bank dimensions, material specifications) not labeled or specified. Complete conduit sizing and material specifications must be added to all electrical routing documentation.
applicableAreas: Underground electrical conduit routing throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electrical infrastructure including transformer pads, pull boxes, electrical meters on all eight buildings, and underground conduit routing depicted as blue lines. However, the proposed conduit routing lacks specification of pipe sizing/diameter. Utility Notes require contractors to verify existing utilities but do not specify proposed conduit sizes, material, or duct bank dimensions.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires complete documentation of proposed electric facilities including distribution lines and all infrastructure. Incomplete facility specifications (missing conduit sizes, pipe diameters, duct bank details) constitute incomplete documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electrical facilities are incompletely shown. Please provide: (1) conduit sizing and material specifications for all underground routing on Sheets 9, 11, 19, and 21; (2) transformer pad kVA ratings and voltage configurations; (3) distribution line sizes; (4) pull box dimensions; (5) consistent depiction of all proposed equipment across all plan sheets.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformers (4 pad-mounted), meters (attached to buildings), pull boxes, and underground conduit routing in blue. However, vision analysis identified critical absences: no conduit sizing or material specifications labeled, no transformer kVA ratings or voltage configurations shown, no pull box dimensions, no distribution line sizes. Sheet 9 shows only one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and lacks all underground routing and meters. Sheet 11 shows no electric distribution lines at all. Sheet 19 has legend symbols for 'Proposed Underground Electric' and 'Transformer Pad' but NO actual facilities are drawn on the plan view.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iii) and (5) require proposed electric facilities to be 'shown' with sufficient detail. The incompleteness includes no conduit/wire sizing, no transformer ratings, no voltage designations, no equipment specifications. Cross-sheet inconsistency means critical sheets (9, 11, 19) do not show the complete proposed design shown on Sheet 21.

perRunFindings.comment: Power source for proposed buildings not clearly identified. Please add: (1) equipment schedule or one-line diagram showing which transformer(s) serve which buildings; (2) service voltage and load data for each building; (3) connection routing from transformers to each building's service entrance; (4) clarification of whether multiple buildings share service or have individual service points.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads and meters on buildings but does not identify which transformer(s) serve which buildings. No callouts or connection lines indicate power routing from transformers to specific buildings. No indication of primary vs. secondary service. Sheet 9 shows one transformer pad but no meters and no indication of service routing. The electrical design does not include a one-line diagram, equipment schedule, or notes identifying the power source for the 39 residential units.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires plans to show 'Power source for proposed buildings.' The omission means it is unclear which transformer(s) power which buildings and load distribution among transformers cannot be verified.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed power source and service specifications (voltage, amperage, service type) not identified for proposed buildings. Specify the service voltage (primary/secondary), amperage, and service type (single/three-phase) for each building or building group on the electrical design plan.
applicableAreas: Site plan, Electrical design plan - all proposed buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 which shows 8 proposed buildings. Vision analysis confirms that meters are depicted with generic 'Electrical Meters' labels and transformers are shown as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' callouts. However, the plan does not clearly indicate the power source (service voltage, amperage, or service type) for any of the proposed buildings. The vision tool response explicitly states: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires that plans show 'Power source for proposed buildings.' While the physical locations of meters and transformers are graphically depicted, without identification of the power source (voltage level and capacity), the requirement is not met.

comments.title: Electrical Routing Exceeds Maximum Two 90-Degree Bends Between Transformer and Meter
comments.comment: The proposed underground electrical routing contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary loop alone, and most branch paths to individual buildings include multiple additional bends — all exceeding the maximum 2 turns permitted between transformer and meter.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q limits electrical routing between a transformer pad and its associated meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends. The primary electrical loop on Sheet 21 follows a rectangular circuit around the central buildings requiring at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners. Branch connections to transformer pads and individual meters add further turns. Routing paths to Buildings 3, 5, and 7 are specifically identified as having multiple (3+) 90-degree turns. No routing path on the site is identified as complying with the two-turn maximum. The site layout systematically cannot meet this requirement without a fundamental redesign of the electrical routing topology.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Underground electrical routing throughout site; all routing paths from transformer pads to meter locations, particularly to Buildings 3, 5, and 7
comments.resolution: Redesign the underground electrical routing to limit 90-degree bends between each transformer pad and its associated meters to a maximum of two, or provide written approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing a deviation from the two-turn maximum for this site configuration. As part of the resubmittal, annotate the electrical plan with a bend count for each routing path from transformer pad to meter, confirming compliance or identifying approved exceptions.

perRunFindings.comment: Number of 90-degree turns in electrical routing from each transformer to meter not documented. Provide detailed electrical routing schedule or plan annotations showing the count of 90-degree bends in the conduit path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter(s), confirming maximum two 90-degree bends.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths from transformers to meters on all eight buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 which shows electrical routing from transformers to meters as blue lines. Visual inspection shows multiple turns. For example, routing from the transformer pad adjacent to Building 8 to the building's meters shows approximately 2 turn angles. However, the plan is schematic and does not explicitly count or label the number of 90-degree bends. For many routing paths, multiple 90-degree turns are visually apparent as lines navigate around building footprints.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code requires maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer and meter. The plan does not explicitly document or count the number of 90-degree bends in each routing path. Some routing paths appear to have more than two distinct directional changes.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary underground electrical loop, exceeding the maximum of 2 turns permitted by UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q. Revise the electrical routing design to limit turns between transformer pads and meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends, or provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing path from transformers to meters throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis traced the primary electrical routing: 'It enters the site from the mid-western boundary... splits to form a continuous underground loop that follows the inner perimeter of the internal drive aisle, circling the central buildings.' Analysis specifically identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends. Counting just the primary main loop (excluding small jogs to individual pads/meters), there are at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners to navigate the rectangular layout of the site.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q specifies maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter. The vision analysis conclusively identified at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary electrical routing loop — triple the maximum allowable. This configuration cannot be reconfigured without a complete redesign of the electrical routing topology.

perRunFindings.comment: More than two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter. Most routing paths show multiple bends to navigate around building perimeters.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan, scale 1" = 20') vision analysis identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends throughout the site's electrical routing. Almost every path from a transformer to a distant meter (e.g., from the west pad to Bldg 3, or from the east pads to Bldg 5 and 7) involves multiple 90-degree turns to navigate around building corners and pull boxes.' The vision analysis did not identify a single routing path with two or fewer 90-degree bends.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q limits electrical routing between transformer and meter to a maximum of two 90-degree bends. Vision analysis explicitly confirmed 'numerous 90-degree bends' on most routing paths, with specific mention that paths to Buildings 3, 5, and 7 involve 'multiple 90-degree turns.' This pattern demonstrates systematic non-compliance across multiple meter routing paths.

comments.title: Vault Easement Notation Conflicts with Network Area Prohibition on Transformer Vaults
comments.comment: A 'Vault Easement' label on the electrical plan conflicts with pad-mounted transformer designations and, if it represents a subsurface vault, is prohibited at this location outside the Austin Energy Network Area.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5 restrict transformer vault rooms exclusively to the downtown Network Area; this site (3759 Valley View Road, South Austin, MF-2 zoning) is confirmed outside the Network Area. The following deficiencies arise from the 'Vault Easement' notation on Sheet 21:
• Sheet 21 labels all four transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (pad-mounted) but includes a 'Vault Easement' label adjacent to Transformer 4 (west of Building 8), and a separate 'Vault Easement' label near the Building 2 transformer area, creating ambiguity as to whether a subsurface vault installation is intended
• If a vault installation is proposed, it is prohibited at this location outside the Network Area; the only permissible alternatives are pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) transformers or specialized niches meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility)
• No vault design specifications, interior dimensions, access details, fire ratings, ventilation provisions, load calculations, or AE Network Design coordination/approval documentation are provided on any submitted sheet, as required by UCM § 1.11.1 for vault installations (3–6 month review lead time required)
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer 4 location (southwestern portion of site, west of Building 8); Building 2 transformer area — both with adjacent 'Vault Easement' labels on Sheet 21
comments.resolution:
• If only pad-mounted transformers are proposed: Remove or annotate the 'Vault Easement' label(s) on Sheet 21 to confirm no subsurface vault installation is intended; add a plan note stating all transformers are pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) in compliance with UCM § 1.5.2.6.
• If a transformer vault is intended: Demonstrate the site is within the Austin Energy Network Area per UCM § 1.11.5, or redesign to use pad-mounted transformers or specialized niches meeting all UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements; submit complete vault design documents (interior dimensions, access specifications, 3-hour fire ratings, ventilation details, load calculations) with documented AE Network Design approval per UCM § 1.11.1.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Applicant must clarify whether the 'Vault Easement' notation represents a proposed vault installation or a property/access easement only — this determination controls whether a fail or pass applies.

perRunFindings.comment: Sheet 21 references an 'Electrical Vault Easement' but the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' Clarify whether the transformer is pad-mounted (compliant) or installed in a subsurface vault (non-compliant outside Network Area per UCM § 1.5.2.6). If a vault installation is proposed outside the Network Area, reconfigure to either: (a) pad-mounted transformer (clear to sky), or (b) specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) visual analysis identified the presence of an 'Electrical Vault Easement' labeled near the southwest entrance of the site. The vision analysis noted this easement 'encompasses a transformer pad and pull box.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 in the MF-2 zoning district, which is not part of the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5). No Network Area service is indicated on the site plans. The term 'vault easement' is used in the labeling, but the transformer within it is described as a 'pad' (pad-mounted), which typically refers to aboveground equipment. However, the use of the term 'vault' in the easement designation creates ambiguity as to whether the transformer is truly a subsurface vault installation or simply an easement area serving a pad-mounted transformer.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.22 specifies 'Vaults or meter rooms proposed outside Network Area where vaults are not permitted' and applies only when 'vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed.' UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted (clear to sky) or installed in specialized niches meeting specific requirements (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3). The site is clearly outside the Network Area. The ambiguity arises from the sheet's reference to an 'Electrical Vault Easement' while the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' This terminology conflict must be clarified: if the transformer is truly installed in a subsurface vault, it violates UCM § 1.5.2.6. If it is a pad-mounted transformer within an easement area, it is compliant. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan and lack of detailed transformer installation specifications (normal pad-mounted vs. vault vs. niche configuration) prevent a definitive determination.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer installation method and site location relative to Network Area require clarification. Confirm whether proposed installation near Building 8 is pad-mounted or vaulted. If vaulted, verify site location against Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5); vaults are permitted exclusively within Network Area. If outside Network Area and vault is proposed, verify specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility). Clarify 'Vault Easement' designation on electrical site plan.
applicableAreas: transformer installation near Building 8 (southwest portion of site)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (indicating pad-mount configuration per vision analysis). However, near Building 8 in the southwestern area, the plan also includes a label for 'Vault Easement,' which raises the question of whether a vault installation is being proposed in addition to or instead of a pad-mount transformer. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes this explicit 'Vault Easement' label in the bottom right area near the Bldg 8 transformer location. UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; vaults outside the Network Area are not permitted. The preliminary electrical site plan does not explicitly state whether a vault is proposed or whether the 'Vault Easement' is simply a property easement designation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 states that transformer vaults are permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries. If the site is outside the Network Area and a vault is being proposed, this violates the requirement. The vision analysis found an explicit 'Vault Easement' labeled on Sheet 21, which suggests that some kind of vaulted or enclosed transformer installation may be planned. However, the same sheet labels transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (pad-mount). The ambiguity between the vault easement designation and the pad-mount labels, combined with the inability to verify Network Area status from site plans alone, creates an unclear status. If a vault is proposed outside the Network Area, this would be a clear violation; if only pad-mount installations are proposed, the vault easement may be a property easement that does not trigger this deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Verify the site location relative to the Austin Energy Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5) at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.com/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png. If the site is within the Network Area, confirm transformer installation is vault-type per UCM § 1.5.2.6. If outside the Network Area, confirm transformers are pad-mounted (as shown) or, if enclosed, demonstrate they meet specialized niche requirements: 35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, accessible from outside the building, proper ventilation, and truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four 'Electrical Transformer Pad' locations depicted as rectangular symbols. These appear to be pad-mounted transformers (clear-to-sky installation), not subsurface vaults or enclosed transformer rooms. UCM § 1.5.2.6 states 'Transformer Installation Requirements (vaults restricted to Network Area).' Pad-mounted transformers are permissible outside the Network Area. However, the Network Area status of the site at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 has not been verified from site plans or in the documentation. Without Network Area determination, and given that the transformers shown are pad-mounted (not vaults), this item appears to have limited applicability. However, if a vault installation were proposed, Network Area confirmation would be critical.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults exclusively to the Network Area. Outside the Network Area, only pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) transformers or specialized niches meeting specific requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3) are permitted. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers, which are compliant outside the Network Area. The Network Area determination cannot be verified from site plans. If the site is actually within the Network Area and the transformers should be vaults instead, or if specialized niches are being proposed, this would need verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Vault Easement notation appears on electrical plan for property outside downtown Network Area. Clarify whether transformer vault rooms (subsurface rooms) are proposed; if so, provide evidence that site is within the downtown Network Area per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is outside Network Area (as facts indicate), transformer vaults are prohibited; transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation per UCM § 1.5.2.6.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and proposed service configuration
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) showing four transformer pads labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". The property is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704, which is in South Austin. According to facts.md, there is no Network Area designation at this property and no regulating plan applies. The Network Area is defined in UCM § 1.11.5 as the downtown Austin area providing vault-only service. The site location is outside downtown and the project facts confirm no Network Area status. However, Sheet 21 shows one transformer location with an adjacent "Vault Easement" label, suggesting a possible vault configuration may be planned.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code limits transformer vault rooms to the downtown Network Area only (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5). Outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or located in niches (with AE Design consultation). The site is clearly outside the Network Area (South Lamar area, no Network Area designation per facts.md). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label on Sheet 21 near Building 2 raises the question of whether a transformer vault room (subsurface room with multiple transformers) is being proposed outside the Network Area.

perRunFindings.comment: Sheet 21 shows a 'Vault Easement' notation adjacent to Transformer 4, indicating proposed vault infrastructure. The property is located outside the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5) where vault rooms are prohibited. Transformers outside the Network Area must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation. Clarify: (1) Remove the Vault Easement notation if transformers will be pad-mounted, or (2) If a vault is intended, this site does not qualify per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5 and cannot proceed with vault design at this location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 4 (southwestern side, west of Bldg. 8) and vicinity
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows Transformer 4 in the southwestern portion of the site (west of Bldg. 8).
