The notation of a 'Vault Easement' indicates the applicant intends or is planning for vault infrastructure at this location. Per facts.md, the property address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) is in South Austin, MF-2 zoning, and there is NO notation of the site being in the 'Network Area.' The facts.md specifically confirms: 'Regulating Plan: None' and the site address and zoning clearly place this property outside the downtown Network Area defined in UCM § 1.11.5.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The notation of 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Transformer 4 indicates an intent to construct or provide access to underground vault infrastructure. Per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5, transformer vault rooms are only permitted within the downtown Network Area. The property is clearly outside the Network Area (South Austin location, Valley View Road, MF-2 zoning). Therefore, vault room construction is prohibited at this location. The applicant must either: (1) remove the vault easement notation and confirm all transformers are pad-mounted only, or (2) if a vault is intended, relocate the infrastructure to a property within the downtown Network Area.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer vault is referenced by 'Vault Easement' label on electrical plan, but no vault design specifications or evidence of AE Network Design approval is provided. If transformer vault service is proposed, provide complete vault design including interior dimensions, access specifications, fire ratings, ventilation details, load calculations, and documented AE Network Design approval. applicableAreas: Transformer locations near Building 2 with nearby 'Vault Easement' label

Near Building 2, one of the four transformer pad locations is accompanied by a text label reading "Vault Easement" pointing to a dashed rectangular boundary area that also contains an "Electrical Pull Box" label. perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify vault requirements from available evidence. perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads (5 total) but no indication of vault structures. The facts.md indicates the site is located in Austin, TX but does NOT place it within the Downtown Network Area per facts.md statement "Regulating Plan: None". The applicability note in the checklist states vaults are required only "Inside Network Area: vaults required for services above 800 amps. Outside Network Area: vaults generally not permitted - only pad-mounted transformers or specialized niches." The site appears to be outside the Network Area, suggesting pad-mounted transformers (which are shown) would be the appropriate service type. However, without formal Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the service type decision and demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) if pedestals/niches are used, the determination cannot be conclusively verified.

The absence of such documentation means the applicant's choice of pad-mounted transformers cannot be verified as AE-approved.

Sheet 21 labels all transformers only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no equipment specifications, and the Engineer's Summary Letter addresses water and wastewater only; no electrical load calculations or transformer specifications appear anywhere in the submitted documents.

comments.resolution: Submit: (1) complete electrical engineering calculations including transformer count, kVA ratings, voltage classes, and amperage specifications for all proposed transformers; (2) completed ESPA form submitted to Austin Energy Network Design; and (3) final voltage and load documentation confirming the proposed equipment meets the development's power requirements and complies with Austin Energy standards.

perRunFindings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and the Engineer's Summary Letter supplementary document. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires that Austin Water vaults maintain required 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault structure, with no other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures allowed to encroach within this zone. comments.title: Required Austin Energy Plat Notes Absent from Plat Sheet
comments.comment: The subdivision plat (Sheet 2) does not include any of the eight Austin Energy plat notes required when electric facilities and easements are present.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires eight specific plat notes on any plat submitted with a land development application where electric facilities or easements are present. Sheet 2 is the original 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat and contains none of these notes. The following required notes are absent from the plat:
- **(i)** Austin Energy right to prune and remove trees and obstructions to keep electric facility easements clear
- **(ii)** Easement and access provision for Austin Energy
- **(iii)** Owner responsibility for temporary erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and initial tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of proposed overhead electric facilities centerline
- **(iv)** Owner responsibility for maintaining NESC, OSHA, City of Austin, and Texas state law clearances
- **(v–viii)** Transmission easement restrictions (prohibition of structures, landscaping, and fencing within easement and related access/maintenance obligations)

Note: Per one review run (1/3), language for items (i), (iii), and (iv) appears on Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 8), but the code requirement is for plat notes appearing on the recorded plat document to bind the property and provide notice to future owners.

comments.reviewerAttentionNote: One of three runs (low confidence) found that items (i), (iii), and (iv) language exists on Sheet 3 (General Notes) — reviewer should verify whether plat note language on the coversheet satisfies the UCM § 1.16.0(8) plat note requirement or must be duplicated on the recorded plat.

comments.title: Moonlight Tower Proximity Cannot Be Verified from Submitted Plans
comments.comment: The submitted site plan documents do not include moonlight tower location data, making it impossible to determine whether construction activities fall within the 100-foot trigger zone that requires a Moonlight Tower Construction Permit.
comments.issue: Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201 requires a Special Moonlight Tower Construction Permit, enhanced insurance coverage ($500,000 minimum), and protective barriers when construction occurs within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its associated guy wires. Neither the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) nor the Site Plan (Sheet 9) depict any moonlight tower or guy wire locations, and the City of Austin's geospatial inventory of moonlight tower locations is not included in the submittal. The 2.26-acre limits of construction are shown, but applicability of this requirement cannot be confirmed or ruled out without external GIS data.
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Sheet 21
comments.applicableArea: 100-foot radius around any moonlight tower or associated guy wires within or adjacent to the 2.26-acre limits of construction at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704 (Council District 5)
comments.resolution: Verify with City of Austin GIS or Austin Energy records whether any of Austin's 17 historic moonlight towers are located within 100 feet of the project limits at 3759 Valley View Road. If a moonlight tower is present within 100 feet: (1) show the tower location and all guy wires/posts on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and Site Plan (Sheet 9); (2) obtain a Special Moonlight Tower Construction Permit prior to site plan approval; and (3) provide documentation of required protective barriers and minimum $500,000 insurance coverage.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Verification may require coordination with Austin Energy, which maintains records of the 17 historic moonlight tower locations throughout the city, and City of Austin GIS for geospatial proximity analysis.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Cannot be resolved from plan review alone — reviewer must cross-reference City of Austin moonlight tower GIS inventory or Austin Energy records against the project address (3759 Valley View Road, 78704) before this item can be closed.

perRunFindings.comment: Moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of construction limits cannot be determined from submitted site plan documents; requires verification against City of Austin geospatial data
applicableAreas: Limits of construction; 100-foot radius from any moonlight tower or guy wires if present

perRunFindings.reasoning: Code § 14-11-201 and UCM § 5.2.1 establish that activities within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires trigger special permitting (Moonlight Tower Construction Permit), enhanced insurance requirements ($500,000 minimum), and protective barriers. The applicability rule states: 'Only when moonlight tower or associated guy wires are within 100 feet of limits of construction.' The grouping guidance acknowledges that determination of moonlight tower proximity 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone' and instructs to 'flag for human verification.' The site plan documents do not show moonlight towers, and facts.md does not indicate their presence. Without access to the City's geospatial database of moonlight tower locations, it is not possible to determine from the submitted site plan materials whether a moonlight tower is within 100 feet of the 2.26-acre limits of construction.

perRunFindings.comment: Verify with City GIS or Austin Energy records whether any historic moonlight towers are located within 100 feet of the Valley View Townhomes construction site. If a moonlight tower is present within 100 feet, show its location and guy wires/posts on the plans and provide documentation of Special Moonlight Tower Construction Permit compliance (Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201).
perRunFindings.observation: The grouping guidance states: 'Note: Cannot be determined from plans alone—requires external location data. Flag for human verification if proximity uncertain.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704 in Council District 5. Austin maintains 17 historic moonlight towers throughout the city. The closest known moonlight tower locations would require City GIS lookup or Austin Energy records. The survey and plans do not indicate any moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of the construction area.

perRunFindings.comment: Moonlight tower proximity cannot be verified from submitted site plan documents. Requires verification using City of Austin geospatial moonlight tower location database to determine if a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction.
applicableAreas: 100-foot radius around any existing moonlight tower or guy wires
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan documents, including the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and all other sheets reviewed, do not identify or call out the location of any existing moonlight towers or associated guy wires on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping instructions for this item explicitly note that moonlight tower locations 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone.' No geospatial analysis or moonlight tower proximity study is attached to or referenced in the site plan documents. perRunFindings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201 requires a moonlight tower construction permit when construction activities occur within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or associated guy wires. The requirement to include a plan note regarding removal and storage of moonlight towers during construction (EL-7.18) is triggered only when such a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction. The submitted site plan documents do not contain sufficient information to determine whether a moonlight tower exists within the 100-foot proximity threshold. The City of Austin maintains geospatial data on moonlight tower locations that is not included in the site plan document set. perRunFindings.comment: Verify with City of Austin GIS or Austin Energy records whether a moonlight tower exists within 100 feet of the property. If yes, show guy wire locations and labels on plans, and provide documentation of required Moonlight Tower Construction Permit.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not indicate the presence of a moonlight tower on or within 100 feet of the property. perRunFindings.reasoning: Per Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201, construction within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires requires special permits, protective barriers, and enhanced insurance. comments.title: 48-Hour Austin Energy Notification Note Missing from Plans
comments.comment: Plans do not include the required conspicuous note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning work near high-voltage overhead electric lines.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.2 incorporates Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, which requires a stand-alone plan note mandating 48-hour advance notification to Austin Energy before any work, excavation, or construction near high-voltage overhead lines. While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a pre-construction safety meeting for transmission facilities specifically, no corresponding stand-alone notification note exists for work near distribution overhead lines on the cover sheet or in the general notes. The note must be conspicuous and include Austin Energy contact information.
comments.citation: UCM § 1.10.2; Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003
comments.sheets: Cover sheet (Sheet 1); General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Cover sheet and general notes — applies project-wide to all construction adjacent to overhead electric facilities
comments.resolution: Add a conspicuous stand-alone note to the cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact: [Austin Energy contact information]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'

perRunFindings.comment: Add note to cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Notification is required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact information: [Austin Energy contact details]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for entire project
perRunFindings.observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) reveals the following: Sheet 1 contains project title, location map, fire department requirements, environmental notes, various compliance statements, but NO note requiring 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work begins near overhead lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 includes 'Electric Transmission Notes' (16 items) which specifically require (Item 3): 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction... OSHA requires a 20' clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' This note applies specifically to TRANSMISSION facilities and includes a 48-hour requirement for a SAFETY MEETING. However, Sheet 3, Blocks 8/14 ('Electric Notes') address general distribution lines but contain NO requirement for 48-hour notification before construction work begins near distribution overhead lines.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 explicitly requires a plan note: 'Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a 48-hour pre-construction safety MEETING for transmission lines specifically, there is NO corresponding note for general construction notification before work begins near distribution overhead lines.

perRunFindings.comment: Specific 48-hour notification note required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 is not clearly called out on cover sheet or plans. Add conspicuous note: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work near overhead electric lines. Contact [Austin Energy contact information].'
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) have been reviewed. Block 14 of Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy requirements addressing maintenance of clearances per NESC and OSHA but is phrased as developer responsibility language. The specific requirement per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 for owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines is not clearly called out as a discrete note on the cover sheet or title block.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752 Section 752.003 requires notification to Austin Energy 48 hours before work near overhead electric lines. While general Austin Energy notes are present on Sheet 3, the specific 48-hour notification requirement is not clearly set out as a distinct, stand-alone note with notification procedures.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not include required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. Add this requirement to the cover sheet general notes or site plan release notes in a location where all contractors and the owner will see it during project execution.
applicableAreas: General notes on cover sheet or site plan sheets
perRunFindings.observation: The cover sheet (Sheet 1) and general notes sheet (Sheet 3) were reviewed in detail. Sheet 1 contains standard project information, Fire Department requirements, and administrative notes, but no mention of a 48-hour notification requirement to Austin Energy. Sheet 3 contains comprehensive notes about utilities, construction sequence, benchmarks, fire department requirements, and electric transmission clearances, but no explicit note requiring the owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy 48 hours before work near high-voltage overhead lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly contains site plan release notes but no mention of the 48-hour notification requirement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The grouping's Documentation Requirements section explicitly states: '48-hour notification plan note: Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' Since overhead electric facilities clearly exist on and adjacent to this site, the required notification note must be prominently displayed on the plans.

comments.title: Grading Within 25 Feet of Transmission Structures Lacks Austin Energy Approval
comments.comment: The grading plan shows approximately 2–3 feet of excavation at the NW corner of the site immediately adjacent to a confirmed transmission pole and guy anchor, with no Austin Energy evaluation or written approval documentation provided.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.14.5.2 prohibits excavation deeper than 1 foot within 25 feet of transmission foundations without Austin Energy evaluation and written approval. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows approximately 2–3 feet of cut at the NW corner property line where a transmission pole and guy anchor are confirmed on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey). No Austin Energy written approval or coordination documentation is included in the submittal. Additionally, a separate ambiguity exists: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains 16 detailed transmission-specific notes (including the 25-foot no-dig zone and coordination requirements), yet no transmission structures are clearly labeled on the site plan or grading plan. The plans must both resolve this ambiguity and obtain documented approval for the identified excavation.
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: NW corner of site near transmission pole and guy anchor on Valley View Road frontage; all areas within 25 feet of transmission pole bases and guy anchor locations
comments.resolution: Contact Andrew Perez at Austin Energy (512-505-7153) and obtain written approval for all grading and excavation within 25 feet of transmission structures and guy anchors before construction commences. Submit proof of Austin Energy written approval with the site plan response. Additionally, clearly label all confirmed transmission structure locations (poles, guy anchors) on Sheets 9 and 11 to resolve the ambiguity between the transmission notes on Sheet 3 and the absence of transmission infrastructure on working drawings.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy (Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153) for written approval of grading activities within 25 feet of transmission foundations per UCM § 1.14.5.2.

perRunFindings.comment: Transmission facility presence and location unclear. Plans reference transmission-specific safety requirements and 25-foot clearance zones (Block 20, Sheet 3) but do not clearly identify transmission structures or establish their locations relative to grading limits. Must clarify whether transmission infrastructure exists and provide specific locations of transmission poles, structures, and guy anchors if present; otherwise, transmission-specific requirements should be removed from plans to avoid confusion during construction.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains 16 detailed notes referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, and requiring 25-foot no-dig/grade zones and Austin Energy coordination. However, vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), and Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) found no transmission poles, transmission structures, or transmission-level easements depicted. Only distribution-level infrastructure is visible: 5-foot electric easements, overhead distribution line along Valley View Road, and utility poles with guy wires.

comments.title: Down Guy Anchor Locations, Clearance Zones, and Easements Not Shown on Working Plans
comments.comment: Guy wire anchors confirmed on the existing conditions survey are omitted from the site plan and grading plan, 25-foot clearance zones around anchors are not established on working drawings, and required 10-foot-wide down guy anchor easements are not shown on the plat or site plan.
comments.issue:
- Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms power poles with guy wires ('GUY') and guy anchor symbols at both the NW and SW corners along Valley View Road, yet Sheets 9 (Site Plan) and 11 (Grading Plan) do not depict these features.
- UCM § 1.16.0 requires existing guy wire foundations and anchors to be shown on plans; UCM § 1.14.5.2 and Sheet 3 Block 20 notes require a 25-foot no-dig/grade zone around transmission structures including down guy anchors. These zones are not established on the grading or site plans.
- Proposed excavation of approximately 2–3 feet at the NW corner occurs with no indication of the adjacent guy anchor location or clearance envelope.
- Reviewer Convention (Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards) requires a dedicated 10-foot-wide easement extending minimum 5 feet past the anchor ground entry point for each down guy anchor; neither the plat (Sheet 2) nor the site plan (Sheet 9) shows these easement boundaries.
- Proposed driveways, accessible paths, and site features are not verified as free of guy anchor conflicts; if conflicts exist, pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles is required.
comments.citation: UCM § 1.16.0; UCM § 1.17.0; UCM § 1.14.5.2; Reviewer Convention (Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards)
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Plat (Sheet 2); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: NW and SW corners of property along Valley View Road where transmission poles, guy wires, and guy anchors are located
comments.resolution:
- Transfer guy wire and anchor locations from Sheet 4 onto Sheets 9 and 11, dimensioned relative to all proposed site features.
- Establish and annotate 25-foot clearance zones around all guy anchor locations on the grading plan and site plan.
- Show 10-foot-wide down guy anchor easements on the plat (Sheet 2) and site plan (Sheet 9), with minimum 5-foot extension past each anchor ground entry point.
- Confirm that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchor locations; if conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution may require coordination with Austin Energy to confirm guy anchor locations and with the plat authority for easement dedication.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each source finding) — reviewer should verify guy anchor locations on Sheet 4 and confirm they are absent from Sheets 9 and 11.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly depict on site plan the location of existing down guy wire anchor points shown on the existing survey (Sheet 4). Verify that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchors or guy wire cables. If conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles per utility company standards.
applicableAreas: Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features relative to down guy wires from existing utility poles
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a 'GUY ANCHOR' symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road, indicating down guy wires are present. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site layout with driveways, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths, but does NOT depict existing guy wire locations or down guy anchor points. The survey shows the guy anchor exists, but its location relative to proposed driveways and accessible paths is not dimensioned or verified on Sheet 9.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Down guy wires represent a potential obstruction and conflict risk if proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features are routed over or through the guy anchor zone. UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) defines 'Down Guy' as a distinct feature. Sheet 4 confirms a guy anchor exists, but Sheet 9 does not show where it is located in relation to proposed site features.

perRunFindings.comment: Depict on site plan and plat all down guy anchor easement boundaries for existing utility poles, showing 10-foot easement width extending minimum 5 feet past the point where the guy wire enters the ground. Verify that proposed site features (buildings, driveways, sidewalks, landscaping) do not encroach on or obstruct the down guy anchor easement area.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing utility poles
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a guy anchor symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road. Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show or reference down guy anchor easement boundaries. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Down guy anchor points require dedicated easements to ensure access for maintenance, replacement, and inspection. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point. The existing survey confirms a guy anchor exists, but the plat and site plan do not show the dedicated easement for this anchor.

perRunFindings.comment: Guy wire anchor locations from existing conditions survey not adequately depicted on grading and site plans; 25-foot clearance zones around guy anchors not established on working drawings despite proposed excavation at NW corner.
applicableAreas: NW and SW corners of property along Valley View Road where transmission structures and guy anchors are located
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 clearly shows power poles ('P.P.') with guy wires ('GUY') and guy anchors at both the NW and SW corners of the property on Valley View Road. However, Sheets 9 and 11 do not adequately depict these guy wire structures or establish 25-foot evaluation zones around them. The grading plan shows excavation occurring at the NW corner with no indication of the guy anchor location or required clearance envelope.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Existing guy wire foundations and anchors' be 'shown on plans.' The existing conditions survey shows guy wires and anchors exist at NW and SW corners. The grading and site plans do not adequately depict these structures or the 25-foot clearance zones required around them.

comments.title: Laydown Curb Not Specified for Transmission Easement and Transformer Access Routes
comments.comment: The site plan and grading plan do not identify which curbing falls within transmission easements or along transformer pad access routes, and no curbing is labeled as laydown curb as required.
comments.issue:
- Sheet 3, Block 20 states: 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be laydown (over-roll) curbing' and 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5-foot spacing).'
- UCM § 1.14.4.E and § 1.14.4.F require laydown curbs along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces, and within all transmission easements.
- Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show curbing throughout but do not label any curbing as 'laydown curb' or identify it as within transmission easement access routes.
- Transformer pads are shown on Sheet 21 but not on Sheets 9, 11, or 31, making it impossible to verify transformer proximity to drivable surfaces or whether access routes require laydown curb.
- Construction Details (Sheet 22) includes COA 430S-1 laydown curb specifications but does not call out where on site they apply.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Construction Details 1 (Sheet 22)
comments.applicableArea: Parking areas and curbing along access routes to transmission easements and transformer pads
comments.resolution:
- Show transformer pad locations on the site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) so distances to drivable surfaces can be verified.
- Identify all curbing within transmission easements or along truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces.
- Label identified curbing as 'Laydown Curb — COA 430S-1, rated for 46,000 lb tandem axle, 5-foot spacing' on the grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9).
- If no transmission easements exist on site, note this clearly on Sheet 3 and clarify applicability of the transmission easement curb requirements.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each); applicability depends on whether transmission easements exist on site and transformer proximity to drivable surfaces — verify with Sheet 21 transformer locations.

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify whether laydown curbs are required without transformer locations shown on site plan and landscape plan. If transformers are located >6 feet from parking/traffic areas, identify the required access routes and verify curbing is laydown curb per UCM § 1.14.4 rather than standard curb.
perRunFindings.observation: Transformer pads are shown on Sheet 21 but not on Sheets 9, 11, 31, or 12, making it impossible to verify whether transformers are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces or if laydown curbs are required. Curbing on the site appears to be standard curb as shown in landscape and grading plans, not laydown curb.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Laydown curbs are required only when: (1) curbing is within transmission easement/ROW, OR (2) along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads NOT within 6 feet of drivable surface. Without transformer locations on the site plan and landscape plan, distances to drivable surfaces cannot be measured.

perRunFindings.comment: Laydown curb rated to withstand required vehicle loading not provided for Austin Energy truck access where parking areas or curbing are located along access routes to transmission easements. Clarify whether transmission easements exist on this site. If transmission easements are present along or near parking or curb areas, specify that all curbing within transmission easement access routes shall be laydown curb (over-roll curb) rated for 46,000 lb tandem axle loading with 5-foot spacing per SSM Item 430s and UCM § 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and curbing along access routes to transmission easements
perRunFindings.observation: Construction Details Sheet 22 confirms that laydown curb specifications (COA 430S-1) are available and shown on the details sheet. The sheet explicitly depicts 'LAYDOWN CURB' in the curb type panel. However, the site plan does not explicitly call out or specify which curb types will be used in areas where vehicles access transmission easements. The General Notes (Sheet 3) state that curbing within transmission easement must be over-roll curbing, but no site plan annotation indicates where transmission easements are located or whether laydown curbs are specified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4.E and 1.14.4.F address transmission easement access and curb specifications. While the construction details sheet includes laydown curb specifications, the site plan itself does not specify whether transmission easement access routes will use laydown curbs.

perRunFindings.comment: Identify all curbing that falls within transmission easements or along transformer equipment pad access routes, and label as 'Laydown Curb' per UCM § 1.14.4.E and Austin Energy requirements. Show curb profiles and clearance dimensions for access.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 states: 'All curbing within the electric transmission easement must be laydown curbing' and 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing).' The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows transmission easement boundaries and various curb details but does not explicitly show or label curbing as 'laydown curb' in the transmission easement areas. No drivable access routes to the transformer pads are shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.14.4.E, laydown curbs are required when curbing is installed within transmission easements or along Austin Energy truck access routes to transformer pads located more than 6 feet from drivable surfaces. Without showing the transformer access routes and identifying required laydown curb locations, it cannot be verified that the design accommodates Austin Energy truck access for equipment installation and maintenance.

comments.title: Construction Staging Plan and Transmission Barricades Not Provided
comments.comment: No construction staging plan showing clearance zones from energized overhead lines exists in the plan set, and the erosion control plan does not show required 10-foot barricades around transmission structures.
comments.issue:
- UCM § 1.10.2 (referencing OSHA 1910.333) requires plans to show minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead distribution lines and 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction. No construction staging plan, equipment layout plan, or crane swing radius diagram exists in the 39-sheet plan set.
- UCM § 1.14.9 requires barricades to be erected 10 feet from all transmission structures before construction commences. Sheet 3, Block 20 states this requirement, but Sheets 5 and 6 (Erosion Control Plans) do not show barricade placement delineating a 10-foot protection zone around transmission poles (Pole 1 at NW corner, Pole 3 at SE corner) or guy anchor locations.
comments.sheets: Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan (Sheet 5); Erosion Control Notes (Sheet 6); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Construction staging areas and material storage zones throughout site; 10-foot protection zone around all transmission poles (NW corner Pole 1, SE corner Pole 3) and guy anchor locations
comments.resolution:
- Provide a construction staging/logistics plan (or annotate Sheet 5) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance exclusion zones from energized overhead distribution lines; (3) 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines where applicable; (4) crane swing radius zones with required clearances; and (5) a note referencing OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.
- Add barricade placement details to Sheets 5–6 showing 10-foot barricades erected around all transmission poles and guy anchor locations before construction begins, and reference this in the construction sequence notes.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each) — reviewer should confirm no construction staging plan exists and verify transmission pole locations relative to construction limits on Sheet 5.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide construction staging/logistics plan (or site phasing plan) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance boundaries from overhead distribution lines (marked as exclusion zones); (3) crane swing radius zones with 10-foot radial clearance from energized lines; (4) 20-foot clearance from transmission lines if transmission structures are present; (5) note requiring contractor to maintain clearances and reference to OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, material storage zones, and equipment laydown areas throughout the site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) addresses temporary erosion control measures and construction sequencing but does not include a detailed construction staging plan or equipment layout plan showing staging areas, equipment zones, crane swing radius, or material storage locations in relation to overhead electric lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not designate specific construction staging areas or address 10-foot radial clearances during construction. NO plans address OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2 requirements for 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines during construction activities.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 references OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements for construction working clearances. Additionally, OSHA requires a 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction. The plans do not demonstrate that construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms will maintain required clearances from overhead energized lines.

perRunFindings.comment: Add barricade placement details to the Erosion Control Plan (Sheets 5–7) showing 10-foot barricades erected around all transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3) and guy anchor locations before construction begins. Include this on the construction sequence diagram and reference it in construction notes.
applicableAreas: 10-foot zone around transmission poles (Pole 1 NW corner, Pole 3 SE corner) and guy anchor locations
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes state: 'Barricades must be erected 10 feet from electric transmission structures during construction.' Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) shows temporary erosion control barriers and construction sequencing. However, the plan does not show barricades specifically placed 10 feet from the three utility poles or from the guy anchor location. The erosion control plan does not delineate a 10-foot protection zone around transmission structures with specific barricade placement as required.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The transmission structures (Pole 1 and Pole 3 with guy anchors) are located within or immediately adjacent to the construction limits. UCM § 1.14.9 requires barricades to be erected before construction commences. The specific placement of barricades at 10-foot distances from transmission structures is a safety and access requirement that must be shown on the construction/erosion control plans.

comments.title: Existing Electric Pole and Line Removal Not Coordinated or Labeled on Plans
comments.comment: The demolition plan acknowledges that existing power poles and electric lines must be coordinated for removal, but neither the demolition plan nor the site plan clearly labels electric facilities with removal/relocation status or includes the required Austin Energy coordination callout note.
comments.issue:
- Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines,' indicating existing utility poles and overhead lines require removal or relocation.
- UCM § 1.16.0 and AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) require that existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated be clearly labeled on the demolition plan with their disposition (remove, relocate, or retain).
- The required plan note — 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' — is not present on the demolition plan or site plan.
- Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show existing poles with callouts identifying disposition (removed, retained, or relocated), nor does it provide a utility coordination drawing.
- Demolition notes on Sheet 8 (Block 9, Site Demolition Notes, Items 1–10) address tree protection, private utility abandonment, materials removal, and gas/water meter removal, but contain no explicit electric facility removal instruction.
comments.sheets: Tree Removal & Demolition Plan (Sheet 8); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Demolition plan and site plan — existing power poles and overhead electric lines on and adjacent to the site
comments.resolution:
- Add the required coordination note to Sheet 8: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles.'
- Label all existing electric poles on Sheet 8 with their disposition: 'REMOVE,' 'RELOCATE,' or 'REMAIN.'
- Show existing poles on Sheet 9 with the same disposition callouts, and include any new pole locations or overhead line routing required for the development.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy for approval of any pole removal or relocation.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each source finding) — reviewer should verify that the coordination callout note is absent from Sheet 8 demolition notes and confirm pole disposition on Sheet 9.

perRunFindings.comment: Add required callout to demolition/site plan notes: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 8 is titled 'Tree Removal & Demolition Plan.' The current site plan sheets do not contain the required callout: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0. While prior demolition is complete, any future excavation or construction activities affecting underground utilities must include this coordination note.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires a specific callout on demolition/relocation plans when existing AE facilities require removal or relocation. This callout must be clearly stated on the site plan. The callout is not present on the reviewed sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated are not clearly labeled on demolition plan, or the status of existing electric infrastructure from the prior use is unclear. Please clarify on the demolition plan whether any existing electric poles, lines, or transformers from the prior facility remain on site and if so, clearly label them with removal or relocation status.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) guide.md mentions Block 2 contains 'Notes instructing coordination with the City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' However, in the detailed block content (Block 9 — Site Demolition Notes), the notes listed (items 1–10) do not include any specific instruction about removing or relocating electric facilities. perRunFindings.comment: On the site plan (Sheet 9), clearly show existing power poles and electric lines, indicate which will be removed/relocated/retained, and show any new poles or overhead electric routing required for the development. Include Austin Energy coordination notes referencing removal approvals.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) contains two callout boxes stating 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' This indicates existing utility poles and overhead electric lines are present on the site and must be coordinated for removal or relocation. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show these poles with specific location callouts, nor does it provide a utility coordination drawing showing which poles are removed vs. retained or relocated.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Easements Not Shown or Adequately Dimensioned
comments.comment: No transformer-specific easements are defined, dimensioned, or shown on any plan sheet around the five transformer pad locations; existing 5-foot plat-dedicated electric easements along property lines are insufficient to cover transformer clearance and access requirements.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.24 and § 1.10.3 require dedicated easements around transformer pads to protect Austin Energy's right of access for construction, operation, maintenance, and equipment replacement. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements that vary from 3 to 15 feet depending on equipment side and use. The plans show only pre-existing plat-dedicated 5' electric easements at property-line-based locations; no easement polygons, boundaries, or dimension callouts are drawn specifically around any transformer pad. Existing 5' easements are facially insufficient for transformer clearance zones that can require up to 15 feet, leaving compliance unverifiable and AE maintenance access legally unprotected.
comments.sheets: Plat (Sheet 2); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All five transformer pad locations site-wide
comments.resolution: On Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), add dedicated transformer easement polygons around each transformer pad showing: (1) easement boundary dimensions adequate to encompass the physical pad location, all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (3–15 feet depending on equipment side and access requirements), and AE maintenance/access area; (2) labeled dimension callouts; and (3) recording information or 'to be dedicated' notation. Coordinate exact easement widths with Austin Energy Design based on each pad's configuration and equipment orientation. If any new easements require dedication, reflect dedications on Plat (Sheet 2) and coordinate with Planning accordingly.

perRunFindings.comment: No transformer-specific easements are shown on the site or plat plans. Define transformer easement areas around each of the five pads with appropriate width and clearly indicate on all relevant plans (Plat, Site Plan, Electrical Plan).
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (additional clearance and access easements may be required)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) shows various easements recorded on the property (25' Drainage Easement, 5' Electric Easements, 7.5' Public Utility Easements, 10' Wastewater Easement). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows drainage, electrical, and public utility easements noted on the site plan. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, NONE of the plan sheets call out or define transformer-specific easements around the five transformer pads with specified widths and accessibility requirements. Transformer equipment typically requires defined easement areas for AE personnel to access and maintain the equipment.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and related provisions indicate that additional clearance and access easements may be required around transformer equipment for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance. While general utility easements are shown on the plat, no transformer-specific easement areas are defined on the site plan with documented widths and boundaries. This is essential information for ensuring ongoing maintenance access and compliance with AE requirements. Missing transformer easement documentation is a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad easements are not shown or documented on the electrical plan. Establish and document transformer pad easements around all five pads with dimensions and widths specified by Austin Energy Design to provide the required access for equipment maintenance and accessibility. Show these easements clearly on the electrical plan with dimensions and callouts.
perRunFindings.observation: Review of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and the full site plan set reveals no explicit transformer easement boundaries, widths, or callouts shown around any of the five transformer pads. The plans do not identify specific easement areas reserved for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance around the pads. While electrical easements are shown at certain property locations (e.g., 5' Electric Easement near Pads), no dedicated transformer pad easements with specified widths are documented.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 indicates that 'additional clearance and access easements may be required' for AE facilities. This grouping's Regulatory Overview states 'Transformer easements required around pads (width determined by AE Design for accessibility).' The absence of any easement boundaries, dimensions, or callouts specifically designating transformer pad easements on the plans indicates that this requirement has not been addressed. The applicant must demonstrate that the necessary easements have been reserved.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer easements not shown on electrical design plan. Provide easement exhibits showing transformer pad locations and surrounding easement areas (width and dimensions to be determined by Austin Energy Design standards) necessary for equipment accessibility and maintenance.
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but provides no documentation of transformer easement areas around the pads. Plat sheet (Sheet 2) and easement exhibits would show recorded easements but transformer-specific easement areas are not indicated on any plan sheets. No easement diagram or table provided showing easement widths, dimensions, or locations around the transformer pads.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformer easements around pads with widths determined by Austin Energy Design for accessibility and maintenance. The electrical design plan must depict transformer easement areas (typically rectangular areas extending from the pad) to demonstrate adequate space for AE personnel to access, operate, and maintain equipment. The complete absence of any easement delineation around the transformer pads represents failure to document this requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Identify and show on plans a transformer-specific electrical easement with dimensions adequate to encompass the transformer pad location, all required clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side), and an access zone for Austin Energy operations and maintenance.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9, 11, and 21 show various electrical easements (5' Electric & Tele. Easement, 5' P.U.E., etc.) labeled with recording information. However, these easements are shown as property-line-based boundaries and do not specifically delineate easement areas around the transformer pad locations. The grouping guidance states: 'Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover specific facility clearances and access requirements' and references UCM § 1.3.24 (Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities). No easement dimensions are verified against the specific clearance requirements for the transformer pads themselves (which require clearances ranging from 3-15 feet depending on side and use).
perRunFindings.reasoning: Austin Energy requires easements that are adequate in size to cover not only the physical location of electrical facilities but also the clearance zones and access areas required by code. The grouping notes state: 'There is no uniform "5-foot electrical easement" standard in Austin codes. Easement dimensions must be adequate to cover the physical location of facilities, required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side and configuration), and areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access per UCM § 1.3.24.' Without showing transformer-specific easement boundaries with dimensions verified against code clearance requirements, compliance cannot be confirmed.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical easement around transformer facilities not shown or not adequate. Show dedicated easement boundaries around each transformer pad sufficient to cover: (1) the physical equipment location, (2) all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (10-15 feet depending on equipment side and access requirements), and (3) Austin Energy access and maintenance areas. Label easement with recording information or 'to be dedicated' notation.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pad locations but does not show any dedicated electrical easement boundaries or polygons around the transformer facilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing electrical easements on property boundaries (labeled as '5' Electric Easement') but does not show proposed easements around transformer equipment. The grouping overview notes that electrical easements must be adequate to cover: (1) the physical location of facilities, (2) required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side), and (3) areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access. No such easement polygons are depicted in the site plan set.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 defines easements as property rights necessary to ensure safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access to electric facilities. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies varying clearance requirements: hot-stick use areas require 10-15 feet clearance; sides with controls require 5 feet clearance from fencing; sides without operators may be 3 feet from removable fencing. Each transformer requires an easement adequate to encompass all clearance zones and access areas. UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly show easement boundaries. The complete absence of transformer easement delineation prevents verification that property within the site is reserved for electrical facilities and that access for Austin Energy maintenance is protected.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical easement dimensions must be adequate to cover transformer facilities and required clearances. Analyze whether existing 5-foot electric easements shown on the plat are sufficient for the five transformer pads, or propose new/modified easements. Show all easement boundaries clearly on Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) with dimensions and recording information. Easement widths must accommodate the transformer pad physical location plus all clearance requirements (up to 15 feet depending on location and equipment orientation).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements labeled with recording information (Vol. numbers, Pg numbers, document references) such as '5' Electric & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' However, these labeled easements are plat-dedicated easements of record (existing easements), not proposed easements around the transformer facilities. The facts.md lists several existing electric easements (5' electric easements per plat documents) but no analysis is provided showing whether these existing easements are adequate to cover the 5 transformer pad locations, their required clearances (which can range from 3-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), and access requirements. No proposed electrical easement is shown around transformer facilities.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Electrical easements around transformer facilities must be shown or proposed with adequate dimensions to cover physical location, all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and access requirements per UCM § 1.3.24. Existing plat-dedicated easements shown on Sheet 21 are 5 feet wide, but transformer clearance requirements can extend 10-15 feet depending on equipment orientation and building features. Unless a detailed analysis demonstrates existing easements are sufficient, proposed easement dedications or modifications must be shown.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Dimensions and AE Design Detail References Missing
comments.comment: The five transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 have no dimension callouts, no service-type designation, and no reference to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.18.0 require that transformer pad installations be designed and constructed to Austin Energy Design-approved specifications, with dimensions determined by service type (single-phase or three-phase). Sheet 21 depicts all pads as simple unlabeled rectangles with no length, width, or depth annotations, no specification callouts, and no reference to AE Design-approved detail sheets obtainable through the ESPA process. Without documented pad dimensions, service type, and AE Design detail references, neither construction adequacy nor compliance with AE specifications can be verified, and contractors have no basis for pad construction.

comments.resolution: For each transformer pad on Sheet 21: (1) add dimension callouts showing pad length × width (and depth where applicable); (2) specify service type (single-phase or three-phase); (3) reference the applicable Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheet obtained through the ESPA process; and (4) confirm that annotated dimensions match AE Design specifications for the specified service type. Ensure pad dimensions are also consistent with any depictions of transformer locations on Sheets 9, 11, and 31.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows five transformer pads depicted as small hatched rectangles with leader line callouts reading 'Electrical Transformer Pad.' The sheet provides NO documentation of service type (whether single-phase or three-phase). perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.18.0 (Appendix) require that transformer pad installations be designed according to Austin Energy Design-approved specifications. These specifications include detailed pad dimensions that vary by service type (single-phase vs. three-phase) and equipment configuration. The absence of (1) specific pad dimensions, (2) service type specification, and (3) reference to or attachment of AE Design-approved detail sheets represents a significant deficiency. The 'preliminary' designation on this electrical plan suggests final details are pending, but the lack of any reference to AE Design specifications is a notable gap in the plan set.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not specified on the electrical plan. Provide the pad dimensions (length × width) for each transformer and reference the corresponding AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheet for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase), demonstrating that the pad configuration matches AE Design specifications.

For each of the three transformer pads, provide: (1) specific pad dimensions (length x width x depth); (2) confirmation of service type (single-phase or three-phase); (3) reference to applicable Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets; and (4) construction material and reinforcement specifications.

On Sheet 21, no specific pad dimension measurements (e.g., 24" × 36", 30" × 48") are annotated.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Transformer pad dimensions (length and width) must be shown on all plan sheets where transformers appear to ensure consistency and allow verification of clearances and access. Sheet 21 shows transformer locations but no pad dimensions are annotated. Since transformers don't appear on other sheets, consistency across sheets cannot be evaluated.
