comments.title: Point of Service Unlabeled and Service Conductor Routing Not Identified
comments.comment: Sheet 21 does not label the Point of Service where Austin Energy conductors connect to customer conductors, and the service conductor routing from that point to AE facilities is not clearly identified or called out.
comments.issue:
• UCM § 1.3.4 requires the POS to be clearly identified — the specific equipment (meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or AE-approved enclosure) where AE conductors hand off to customer conductors. Without this label, the boundary of AE vs. customer responsibility is undefined, and disconnects cannot be verified as correctly located.
• UCM § 1.16.0 requires service conductors from the POS to AE facilities (transformers) to be shown on plans. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing from the west property boundary through pull boxes to transformers and meters, but lacks explicit callouts for: (1) where the AE service stub enters the site, (2) the POS connection point and enclosure type, (3) the SDE or main disconnect location, and (4) direction of conductor flow from POS to transformer. Without POS identification, it is ambiguous which portions of the routing shown are service conductors 'from' the POS versus before it.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire electrical design plan — all service connections from west property boundary through pull boxes to transformers and building meters
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, label the specific equipment (meter socket, SDE, pull box, or other AE-approved enclosure) that serves as the Point of Service for each service connection. Add callouts identifying: (1) the AE service entry point (underground stub from west boundary), (2) the labeled POS enclosure type and location, (3) the SDE or main disconnect location, and (4) direction of service conductor flow from POS to transformer. Verify that all customer conductors originate from the labeled POS.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: EL-15.36 (service conductor routing from POS) flagged as unclear in 2/3 runs — reviewer should confirm that routing ambiguity is resolved once POS is labeled.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service (where Austin Energy service conductors connect to customer service equipment) on the electrical plan. This may be shown as a meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or other AE-approved location.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows service entry point labeled 'Underground Electric Line' at the western property boundary, transformers, pull boxes, and meters. However, no specific location is labeled as the 'Point of Service' where Austin Energy's service conductors hand off to the customer's service conductors. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' While pull boxes are shown, it is unclear which component represents the actual point of service.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.4 and the grouping definition, the point of service must be clearly identified on plans because it defines the boundary between Austin Energy's responsibility and the customer's responsibility for electrical infrastructure. This location also determines where disconnects and service distribution enclosures must be placed per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B. Without clear identification, design coordination and code compliance verification are incomplete.

perRunFindings.comment: Point-of-service location not shown. Identify and label the point-of-service (POS) location(s) where Austin Energy conductors connect to customer conductors. This may be at a meter socket, pedestal, SDE (service distribution enclosure), pull box, or other approved enclosure. Label with "Point of Service" notation and specify the type of enclosure. Verify that all customer conductors originate from the labeled POS.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electrical routing, transformer pads, and meter locations, but does not explicitly identify or label a point-of-service (POS) location. UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as the location where Austin Energy's conductors connect with the customer's conductors. The plan shows meters on building walls and transformers in common areas but does not label the specific location(s) where the connection point(s) between AE and customer infrastructure occur. No callout identifies the meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other location where the POS connection is made.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as a critical infrastructure element. The POS location must be clearly identified because it designates the boundary between Austin Energy responsibility (up to the POS) and customer responsibility (from the POS onward). Without explicit POS identification, the reviewer cannot verify that the service configuration is properly documented, that customer conductors are correctly routed, and that Austin Energy access to the service point is protected. For multi-unit developments, the POS is especially important for understanding service distribution, metering grouping, and disconnect coordination.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly identify the point-of-service location on Sheet 21. Label the specific equipment (meter socket, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other approved enclosure) that serves as the point where Austin Energy facilities connect to customer conductors. Add a note stating the point-of-service definition and location(s). This should be shown for each service/building connection.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters and pull boxes but does not explicitly identify which location is the point-of-service (point where AE conductors connect to customer conductors). The grouping definition states that Point-of-Service is the 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect.' Without a clear label or callout indicating the point-of-service location, it cannot be determined where Austin Energy's responsibility ends and customer responsibility begins.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The point-of-service is the critical junction where utility responsibility transfers from Austin Energy to the customer. It must be clearly marked on plans so that: (1) Austin Energy and customer can verify the boundary of responsibility, (2) disconnects are properly located, (3) permits can be accurately issued, and (4) inspections can verify correct installation. Without explicit identification, there is ambiguity about which equipment serves this critical function.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly identify the Point of Service location (where AE and Customer conductors connect) on the electrical plan, then verify that service conductors from this point to AE facilities (transformers, service entry) are shown and properly routed.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows blue lines labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing from the service entry point (western property boundary) through pull boxes to transformers and then to meters. The routing from the primary service entry to the transformers is shown. However, the 'point of service' where customer and Austin Energy conductors connect is not clearly identified, making it ambiguous whether the service conductors 'FROM the point of service' are properly shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, 'Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities' must be shown. If the point of service is not clearly labeled, it is unclear which portions of the routing shown represent service conductors 'from' the point of service vs. before it. The grouping guidance defines point of service as 'meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull-box, or AE-approved enclosure where AE and Customer conductors connect,' but the electrical plan does not explicitly identify which element is the point of service.

perRunFindings.comment: Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities not clearly identified. Label the point where the underground service stub enters the site and the point of service connection (where AE and customer conductors meet). Show the routing clearly with callouts identifying: (1) service entry point from AE (duct bank, pole, or underground source), (2) point of service location, (3) service distribution enclosure (SDE) or main disconnect location, (4) direction of conductor flow to transformers and meter banks. Verify that service conductors are protected per code and sized per load calculations.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows "Underground Electric Line" routing from the west property edge, through pull boxes, to transformers and meter locations. The underground line enters the site from the left (west) boundary and is drawn as a continuous blue line. However, the plan does not explicitly label: (1) where the service stub originates or enters the site, (2) the specific point of service where AE and customer conductors connect, (3) the direction of conductor flow from the POS to transformers and meters. The routing is shown but the origin point and termination points are not clearly called out.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that service conductor routing be clearly shown from point of service to AE facilities (transformer). The current documentation shows the routing line but lacks explicit identification of the POS location and the service stub entry point. This creates ambiguity: it is unclear whether the line entering from the west represents a service drop from overhead AE lines, an underground service stub from an AE duct bank, or another configuration. Without explicit callouts identifying the POS and service origin, Austin Energy cannot confirm that customer conductors are properly sized, protected, and routed.

comments.title: Service Enclosure Type Unconfirmed — AE Design Documentation Required
comments.comment: Sheet 21 labels 8 meter locations but does not specify the enclosure type, and no Austin Energy Design documentation confirms whether pedestals or other AE-approved enclosures are the approved service equipment for this development.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.5.3.4 provides that electrical pedestals may be used for residential services up to 200 amps maximum. This is a 39-unit multi-family development with pad-mounted transformers and underground service; pedestals are typically not used for multi-family buildings at this scale. However, Sheet 21 labels 8 'Electrical Meters' without specifying the enclosure type (pedestal, meter socket, SDE, or other). No ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, or AE Design utility coordination notes confirming the approved service enclosure type — or confirming that pedestals are not required — are included in the submittal.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 meter locations on building exteriors
comments.resolution: Provide Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination correspondence) confirming the approved service equipment enclosure type for this development. If pedestals are approved, show pedestal locations on Sheet 21. If a non-pedestal enclosure (SDE, meter socket, etc.) is the approved type, label the enclosure type at each meter location on Sheet 21.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires Austin Energy Design (ESPA) confirmation of approved service equipment type.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Status is unclear — reviewer should confirm whether AE Design approval for service enclosure type has been received or is pending ESPA review.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical service pedestals are not shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), which instead shows pad-mounted transformers. Whether pedestals are required must be confirmed through Austin Energy Design documentation or Letter of Agreement. For a multi-family development of this scale, pad-mounted transformers appear more appropriate, but final service type determination requires AE Design confirmation.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows two pad-mounted transformer pads labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but does not indicate whether electrical service pedestals are required or planned for this development. UCM § 1.5.3.4 establishes that electrical pedestals may be used for 'residential lots up to 200 amp maximum underground services' per optional policy. However, this is a multi-family townhome development (39 units in 8 buildings), not traditional residential lots, and pedestals would typically not apply to multi-family service. The applicability of this item depends on whether Austin Energy Design has determined that pedestals are required for the service type selected for this development.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The grouping definition states this item applies 'Only when electrical pedestals are required for service' and requires checking 'Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service.' Without access to AE Design documentation confirming pedestal service is required for this multi-family development, the status cannot be definitively determined. Pedestals are typically used for single-family or small residential lots with limited service capacity (≤200 amps), not multi-family buildings with distributed service. If pedestals ARE required per AE Design, they should be shown on the plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify whether electrical service pedestals are required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type and equipment enclosure specification (pedestal, meter socket, service distribution enclosure, or other AE-approved enclosure) per UCM § 1.5.3.4.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" but does not specify whether these are pedestal-mounted service equipment or other enclosure types. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers with underground service to meter locations, but the specific meter enclosure type is not detailed. No Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, utility coordination notes) is provided confirming whether pedestals are the approved service type for this project. UCM § 1.5.3.4 notes pedestals are typically used for residential services up to 200 amps maximum.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability note states: "Check: Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service." The absence of this documentation means the service type (whether pedestals are required/approved) cannot be verified from site plan review alone. While the physical location of meters is shown, their enclosure type (pedestal vs. other) is not specified on the drawings.

comments.title: Service Configuration Ambiguous — Disconnects and SDE Locations Not Shown
comments.comment: Sheet 21 does not document whether building meters are served individually or from a shared service point, and no disconnects or service distribution enclosures are shown for any of the 8 building meter locations.
comments.issue:
• UCM §§ 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B require that when two or more meters are installed at one location served from one set of service conductors, meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location with a service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway. Sheet 21 shows 8 individual meters (one per building) with no disconnects or SDEs, and no note clarifying whether buildings share a service point.
• UCM § 1.9.3.4.A requires meter bank/rack location to be shown when grouped meter configurations are used. If meters are distributed individually with independent service points per building, this must be explicitly noted on the plan.
• Without a service configuration note and without showing disconnects and SDEs, it cannot be determined whether grouped metering requirements apply and whether the design complies.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 building meter locations — entire electrical design plan
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, add a service configuration note clarifying whether each building has an independent service point (individual service) or whether multiple buildings share a service point (grouped service). If individual service per building: label each building's service point and show the disconnect location within 20 feet and in line of sight of each meter. If grouped service: show the meter bank/rack location, SDE, wireway, and all disconnects grouped at the common service point.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (max 1/3 runs per contributing ref) — reviewer should verify whether service configuration has been clarified in any supplemental documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: If the electrical design includes any grouped meter configuration (two or more meters at a single location served from one service point), show the meter bank/rack location on Sheet 21. If meters are distributed individually to each building (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned individually on or near each building (Bldg. 1-8). The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors. Check: electrical plan for number of meters and service configuration.' The current design shows 8 separate meter locations, one per building, not multiple meters at a single location served from one service point. There is no meter bank or grouped meter installation shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item applies to meter bank/rack configurations where multiple meters are physically located together at one point of service. The current design shows distributed metering with individual meters at each building. Therefore, this item does not apply.

perRunFindings.comment: If the electrical design includes grouped metering for multiple buildings from a single service point, verify that meters and disconnects are grouped in a common location with service distribution enclosure and wireway per UCM § 1.9.3.4. If individual building service is provided (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters distributed individually to 8 buildings (one meter per building) and 5 transformers distributed across the site. The applicability note states: 'Only when multiple meters are served from one set of service conductors or when meters and disconnects must be grouped per code. Check: electrical service configuration showing single point of service serving multiple units.' The current design shows 8 separate service connections (one per building), not multiple meters served from a single service point.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This requirement applies to grouped metering configurations where multiple meter units share a common service point. The current electrical design shows individual building-level service, not grouped multi-unit metering. Therefore, this item does not apply.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearly identify the service configuration: if meters are served from a single point of service, show the service distribution enclosure and disconnect locations grouped with the meters. If each building has an independent service point, note that on the plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters (one per building) on building exteriors but does not show any disconnects or service distribution enclosures. The grouping guidance states: 'When two or more meters are installed at one location and served from one set of service conductors, meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location with a service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway.' With 8 buildings and 8 individual meters, the grouping/point-of-service configuration is unclear. No legend or notes explain the service configuration.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.I and 1.9.3.4.B, when multiple meters serve a single development, they must be coordinated as a grouped metering system if they share a point of service. If each building has its own individual service point, that must be clearly documented. Without showing disconnects and grouping configuration, it cannot be determined whether the design complies with grouped metering requirements.

comments.title: Meter Line-of-Sight to Transformers Not Documented
comments.comment: Sheet 21 does not demonstrate or document that each of the 8 electrical meters has clear line-of-sight visibility to its serving transformer, as required by UCM § 1.9.3.1.B.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and 5 transformer locations, but contains no sight-line diagrams, dashed sight-line callout symbols, or plan notes confirming that each meter is positioned with unobstructed visibility to its serving transformer. Without this documentation, sight-line compliance cannot be verified, and any exceptions would require separate written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 meter locations and 5 transformer locations
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, add either: (1) a plan note stating 'All meters are located within sight of their serving transformer. No line-of-sight exceptions are claimed,' supplemented with dashed sight-line symbols or callouts from each meter to its serving transformer; or (2) if any meter lacks clear unobstructed visibility to its serving transformer, provide written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering for the sight-line exception.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify sight-line feasibility given building placement relative to transformer pad locations on Sheet 21.

perRunFindings.comment: Verify and document that all meter locations are within sight of serving transformers per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B. Add a note to Sheet 21 stating: 'All meters are located within sight of their serving transformer. No line-of-sight exceptions are claimed.' OR, if any meter locations do not have clear sight-line visibility, provide documentation of written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering for the exception. Alternatively, add sight-line symbols or dashed lines from each meter to its serving transformer to visually demonstrate visibility.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and 5 transformer locations. The vision analysis indicated that meters are 'generally corresponding to the eight buildings on the site' and transformers are distributed across the site with underground electric routing connecting them. However, no explicit visual confirmation is shown on the plan that each meter has clear line-of-sight visibility to its serving transformer. No callouts, sight-line diagrams, or notes state that meters are within sight of transformers. The arrangement suggests meters should be visible to transformers (given underground routing), but this critical requirement is not explicitly documented on the plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' This is a specific requirement for safety and operations. Without explicit sight-line confirmation on the plans, or without a note stating that meters are positioned for visibility, there is no documented verification of compliance. Additionally, the plans do not state whether any exceptions requiring AE Design approval are being claimed.

comments.title: Load Center Location Not Indicated on Electrical Plan
comments.comment: Sheet 21 does not show or reference a load center, and the submittal does not clarify whether a centralized load center is required by the project's electrical design.
comments.issue: Per Reviewer Convention, a load center location must be shown on the electrical plan when required by the project's electrical design. Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and 8 pull boxes but no load center. It is not apparent from the preliminary electrical plan or project specifications whether a centralized load center is required or whether building service connections are made directly from individual building meters.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire electrical design plan
comments.resolution: If a load center is required by the project's electrical design, show its location and type on Sheet 21. If no load center is required, add a plan note to Sheet 21 stating that the design uses distributed building-level service without a central load center.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm whether a load center is required for this service configuration.

perRunFindings.comment: If a load center is required by the project electrical design, show its location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). If no load center is required, note in the electrical specifications that the design uses distributed building-level service without a central load center. Clarify this in the design submittal.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads and 8 pull boxes but does not show any load center location. The applicability note states this item is only required 'when load centers required by project electrical design.' No load center is indicated on the preliminary electrical plan shown. It is not clear from the submitted plans whether a load center is required for this project or whether the building service connections are made directly from meters.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Load centers are not always required; they depend on the electrical service design and building layout. The applicability of this item depends on whether the project's electrical design includes a centralized load center. Without an explicit requirement stated in the electrical design documents or specifications, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed.

comments.title: Electrical Meter Separation from Gas Utilities Not Verified
comments.comment: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical meter locations but does not indicate proximity to gas meters, regulators, or other utility apparatus, making the required 3-foot minimum separation unverifiable.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3.1.C requires electrical meters to maintain at least 3 feet from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows an existing gas meter on the exterior of the former main building. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) does not show proposed gas meter locations, gas regulators, or distance callouts from electrical meters to gas utility equipment. Without both electrical and gas meter locations on the same plan, the 3-foot separation requirement cannot be verified.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 electrical meter locations on building exteriors
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, show the locations of all proposed gas meters, gas regulators, and relief valves and annotate the distance from each electrical meter to any adjacent gas utility equipment. Confirm that all electrical meters maintain a minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters, regulators, and relief valves.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May involve coordination with Austin Energy and the gas utility (e.g., Atmos Energy) to confirm gas meter placement relative to proposed electrical meters.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs per contributing ref) — reviewer should verify whether gas meter locations are shown on any other submitted sheet.

perRunFindings.comment: Verify that all electrical meter locations maintain minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C. If gas appliances or other utility apparatus are present, show their locations on the Electrical Design Plan and annotate distances to electrical meters.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' but does not provide specific callouts showing distances from each meter to gas meters, regulators, relief valves, or other electrical apparatus. The site plan does not show gas meter locations or other utility equipment that might create conflicts. Without detailed site analysis showing the location of all meters and utility apparatus, the 3-foot separation requirement cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This requirement depends on identifying all gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus on the site, then verifying at least 3-foot separation from electrical meters. Sheet 21 does not provide this level of detail for meter-to-utility spacing.

perRunFindings.comment: Show on the electrical plan the locations of all proposed electrical meters and reference existing/proposed gas meters, gas regulators, and other utilities to verify minimum 3-foot separation per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls but does not indicate proximity to gas meters, regulators, or other equipment within 3-foot separation distance. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows an existing 'GAS METER' attached to the left exterior wall of the main building structure. New site plans do not show gas meter locations or infrastructure, making it impossible to verify the 3-foot separation requirement between electrical and gas facilities.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.C, meter locations must be at least 3 feet away from gas meters, regulators, relief valves, and other electrical apparatus. Without showing both electrical meter locations and gas utility locations on the same plan, this separation requirement cannot be verified. The absence of gas utility information from the electrical plan creates ambiguity about compliance.

comments.title: Disconnect Locations Not Shown — Meter-to-Disconnect Distance Unverifiable
comments.comment: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical meters but no disconnect locations, making it impossible to verify that meter-to-disconnect distances do not exceed 20 feet and that disconnects are within line of sight of meters.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3.1.J limits the distance between a meter and its associated disconnect to a maximum of 20 feet, requires that they be within line of sight of each other, and requires that each disconnect be readily accessible. Sheet 21 shows 8 meters on building exteriors and transformer locations but no disconnects. Without showing disconnect locations and distance callouts between each meter-disconnect pair, neither the 20-foot maximum nor the line-of-sight requirement can be reviewed or verified during plan check or construction.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 building meter locations
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, show the location of the disconnect associated with each meter. Add distance callouts from each meter to its disconnect and confirm: (1) meter-to-disconnect distance does not exceed 20 feet, (2) each meter-disconnect pair is within line of sight of each other, and (3) each disconnect is readily accessible.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs per contributing ref) — reviewer should confirm whether disconnect locations are detailed elsewhere in the submittal.

perRunFindings.comment: If meters and disconnects are paired, show their spatial relationship on Sheet 21 with: (1) clear identification of meter-disconnect pairs, (2) distance callouts showing the separation between each meter and its disconnect, (3) verification that distance does not exceed 20 feet, and (4) confirmation that meters and disconnects are within line of sight of each other. If meters and disconnects are not paired, clarify the electrical service configuration.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations and transformer locations, but does not specify which meters are paired with which disconnects, nor does it provide distance callouts showing meter-to-disconnect distances. The checklist item requires: (1) meter to disconnect distance not to exceed 20 feet, and (2) meter and disconnect within line of sight. Without explicit labeling of meter-disconnect pairs and distance callouts, these requirements cannot be verified from the plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This requirement is conditional on having grouped metering with associated disconnects. If meters and disconnects are paired, their locations and distances must be clearly shown and verified on the plans. Sheet 21 does not provide sufficient detail for this verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Show disconnect locations on the electrical plan and indicate the distance from each meter. Verify that meter-to-disconnect distance does not exceed 20 feet and that they are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exteriors and four transformers at various locations, but no disconnects are shown. The code requirement per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J states: 'Maximum distance between meter and disconnect is 20 feet; they must be within line of sight of each other and readily accessible.' Without showing disconnect locations, distances between meters and disconnects cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J, the meter-to-disconnect distance is limited to a maximum of 20 feet, and they must be within line of sight of each other. This ensures that the disconnect can be located quickly in an emergency and that the electrical service can be readily shut off. Without showing disconnects on the electrical plan, this code requirement cannot be reviewed or verified during plan check or construction.

comments.title: Individual Unit ESPAs Not Submitted for 39-Unit Development
comments.comment: The applicant has submitted a single project-level approach rather than individual ESPA forms for each of the 39 residential units, as required by Reviewer Convention for multi-unit projects.
comments.issue: Per Reviewer Convention, multi-unit projects require a separate ESPA submission for each unit with the unit number clearly identified. The project contains 39 individual units across 8 buildings (building data on Sheet 9; unit addresses on Sheet 29). Individual unit-level ESPA submissions are required so that Austin Energy Design can coordinate individual service characteristics for each residential unit. Without unit-level ESPAs, AE Design review of individual unit service cannot be verified.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All 39 residential units across 8 buildings
comments.resolution: Submit a separate ESPA form for each of the 39 residential units with the unit number (as shown on Sheet 29 – Addressing Plan) clearly identified on each ESPA form.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires coordination with Austin Energy Design — ESPAs are submitted to and reviewed by AE Design.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm whether unit-level ESPAs are required at this stage or are deferred to the ESPA submission stage.

perRunFindings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each unit in the 39-unit multi-unit project with unit number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 39 units with unit numbers clearly identified.
perRunFindings.observation: Site plan Building Data Table (Sheet 9) shows 39 individual units distributed across 8 buildings. Individual unit addresses/identifiers are noted on Sheet 29 (Addressing Plan). However, no separate ESPA submitted for units. The applicant has submitted a single project-level approach rather than unit-level ESPA submissions for this multi-unit residential project.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, multi-unit projects require separate ESPA submissions for each unit with unit number included. This allows individual service coordination for each residential unit. The absence of unit-level ESPAs prevents verification that AE Design has reviewed individual unit service characteristics.

comments.title: Multiple Points of Service or Voltages Not Documented or Approved
comments.comment: Sheet 21 appears to show multiple transformer service points across the site, but no documentation confirms whether multiple points of service are proposed and, if so, whether AE Design approval for a multi-point exception has been obtained.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.3 establishes a default rule of one point of service at one service voltage to a single building on a single lot. Exceptions for multiple points of service or multiple voltage levels require AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval. Sheet 21 shows multiple transformer locations suggesting multiple service drop points, but it cannot be determined from the preliminary electrical plan alone whether these constitute multiple service points requiring an exception. No AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval letter for a multiple-point exception is included in the submittal.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site — service point configuration and voltage determination
comments.resolution: Clarify on Sheet 21 how many points of service are proposed for the development (i.e., how many service drops from AE transformers to customer equipment). If more than one point of service is proposed, provide an AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval letter authorizing the multiple-point exception. If the design falls within the one-point-of-service rule, add a note to Sheet 21 confirming this.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May require AE Design or Spot/Conduit review and written approval if multiple service points are proposed.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should determine from Sheet 21 whether multiple service drops are actually proposed and whether the one-point-of-service rule applies.

perRunFindings.comment: Multiple points of service or multiple voltages not verified. Confirm whether the project requires one or multiple points of service and one or multiple service voltages. If multiple points of service or voltages are proposed, provide AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval letter for the exception to the one-point-of-service rule.

perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 establishes a default rule of one point of service at one service voltage to a single building on a single lot. Exceptions require AE Design or Spot/Conduit approval. If the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows multiple points of service (multiple service drops to different buildings or multiple voltage levels), documentation of the exception approval is required. Without clarity on whether multiple service points are proposed, or without approval documentation if they are, this requirement cannot be verified.

comments.title: Master Electrical Plan from MEP Consultant Not Provided
comments.comment: No master electrical plan from an MEP consultant has been submitted, and it is unclear whether this single-lot multi-building development triggers the master electrical plan requirement.
comments.issue: Per Reviewer Convention, a master electrical plan is required for master planned developments with multiple lots, showing building loads for all buildings and the overall service routing strategy. This project is a single unified development (39 units, 8 buildings on one lot) rather than a platted multi-lot subdivision. It is ambiguous whether the 'master planned development' requirement applies to this site configuration. No separate master electrical plan from an MEP consultant is included in the submittal.
comments.sheets: No specific sheet — concerns the overall submittal package
comments.applicableArea: Entire development — all 8 buildings
comments.resolution: Clarify whether a master electrical plan from an MEP consultant is required for this single-lot, multi-building development. If required, provide a master electrical plan showing building loads for all 8 buildings and the overall service routing strategy. If not required, provide written confirmation from Austin Energy that the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is sufficient for this development type.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May require Austin Energy Design clarification on whether a master electrical plan is required for this single-lot multi-building development type.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should determine whether this single-lot multi-building development triggers the master electrical plan requirement under Reviewer Convention.

perRunFindings.comment: Clarify whether a separate Master Electrical Plan from the MEP consultant is required for this multi-building residential development. If required, provide the master electrical plan showing loads for all buildings and service routing strategy per Reviewer Convention.
perRunFindings.observation: This is a master planned development with 39 townhome units across 8 buildings in a unified site plan, but it is not a multi-lot subdivision with separate lot development phases. The single site plan shows all proposed buildings and infrastructure in one development. No separate master electrical plan from the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) consultant is provided in the supplementary documents or referenced in the plan set. The applicability note states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots" - the interpretation of whether this unified multi-building development triggers the master plan requirement is ambiguous.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability language states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots." This site is a single unified development of 39 units in 8 buildings, not a platted subdivision with separate lots held by different owners. However, the phrase "master planned development" could potentially include any large multi-building development. The grouping does not define this term precisely. Without a clear definition distinguishing single-site multi-building developments from true master planned multi-lot subdivisions, the applicability cannot be definitively determined. If this project type is intended to require a separate master plan from an MEP consultant, that requirement should be clarified.

comments.title: Underground Ductbank Maintenance Access and Existing AE Infrastructure Not Documented

comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.16 requires maintenance access along the full length and width of distribution ductbanks for Austin Energy trucks and equipment; UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from ductbanks to structures; UCM § 1.16.0 requires existing AE underground infrastructure to be clearly identified on utility plans. Sheet 21 labels routes only as 'Underground Electric Line' without specifying whether the infrastructure is ductbank (conduit system) or direct-buried cable, without dimensioning clearances to buildings, and without designating maintenance access pathways. Existing AE underground facilities upstream of the property in Valley View Road ROW are not clearly delineated.

comments.resolution: Revise Sheet 21 to: (1) label all underground electric facilities as ductbank (conduit system) or direct-buried cable; (2) dimension clearances from all proposed buildings and permanent structures to ductbank routes confirming 5-foot minimum per UCM § 1.10.5; (3) designate and label maintenance access pathways along the full length and width of each ductbank route confirming unobstructed truck and equipment access; and (4) clearly identify and label existing Austin Energy underground infrastructure and ductbanks at the Valley View Road entry point and in the adjacent right-of-way.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Status is unclear because it cannot be confirmed from plans whether underground routing constitutes ductbank vs. direct-buried cable — clarification from applicant or AE Design is required before this item can be resolved.

comments.title: Transmission Line Crossing Profile Drawings and Clearance Conflict Resolution Not Documented
comments.comment: AutoCAD profile drawings for any infrastructure crossing the AE transmission easement have not been provided, and no documentation is included confirming that clearance conflicts with the existing transmission easement have been reviewed and resolved with AE Design.

UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires AutoCAD profile drawings showing crossing design and clearances when any proposed infrastructure crosses an AE transmission line. UCM § 1.10.0 requires that clearance conflicts with existing AE facilities be discussed and resolved with AE Design prior to site plan approval. The following are missing:

- Whether proposed site infrastructure (underground electric routing, drainage, grading, buildings) actually crosses the transmission easement path is not clearly depicted in plan or profile
- Sheet 3, Block 20 documents the transmission easement and requires 25-foot clearance from transmission structures and prohibits digging or grading within that zone, but no clearance analysis relative to proposed improvements is shown

comments.title: Warning Signs Under Overhead Transmission Lines and Caution Signage for AE Facilities Not Shown on Construction Plans
comments.comment: Construction plans do not show required warning signs under overhead electric transmission facilities, and no comprehensive caution signage or construction staging plan for all existing Austin Energy facilities during construction has been provided.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.14.9 requires warning signs to be shown under all overhead electric transmission facilities on construction plans. Sheet 3, Electric Transmission Note 6 acknowledges the requirement ('Warning signs must be placed under the overhead electric transmission facilities as notification of the electrical hazard'), but the erosion control and construction plans (Sheets 5–7) and other construction sheets do not show warning sign placements. UCM § 1.10.1 additionally requires caution signage for all existing AE facilities during construction. The following are missing:
- 'Danger — High Voltage Transmission Lines' warning sign locations under OHE lines along the south and north property boundaries not shown on construction plans
- No construction staging plan specifying protective barriers or caution signage for transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground electric lines
- No sign specifications (dimensions, text, placement height) included on any plan sheet
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan (Sheet 5); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Under overhead electric (OHE) transmission lines along south and north property boundaries; electrical transformer pad locations throughout site; underground electric line routes and pull box locations
comments.resolution: On the Erosion Control Plan (Sheet 5) or a dedicated construction safety plan, add: (1) locations and specifications for 'Danger — High Voltage Transmission Lines' warning signs under all overhead electric lines, including placement height and required pre-construction installation note; (2) protective barrier and caution signage locations for all existing AE facilities (transformer pads, pull boxes, underground lines); and (3) a general note that all required warning signs must be installed before construction begins.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: EL-4.7 is a fail (1/3 runs, UCM § 1.14.9); EL-19.24 is unclear (2/3 runs, UCM § 1.10.1) — combined status is fail; reviewer should confirm exact OHE line locations from Sheets 3 and 4 and whether construction staging applies to existing transformer pads.

comments.title: Pre-Construction AE Transmission Safety Meeting and 48-Hour Notification Not Documented
comments.comment: Documentation that a pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission has been scheduled and that the required 48-hour advance notification for work near high-voltage lines has been arranged is not included in the submitted materials.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.14.0 requires a Notice of Electrical Hazard tailgate safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission Construction & Maintenance before demolition or grading near transmission structures begins. Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and UCM § 1.10.2(B) require documented notification to Austin Energy at least 48 hours before construction within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines, with satisfactory arrangements to de-energize or relocate lines. The following are not documented:
- No meeting minutes, confirmation letter, or scheduling record for the pre-construction tailgate safety meeting (contact: Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153; Chuck Hendry, 512-505-7151 if cranes are used)
- No documentation of 48-hour advance notification arrangement for construction within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines
- Sheet 3, Block 20, Items 2 and 3 reference both requirements, but no evidence of compliance is in the submitted materials
comments.citation: UCM § 1.14.0; UCM § 1.10.2(B); Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: Construction areas within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines; transmission easement corridor throughout site
comments.resolution: Submit documentation of a scheduled or completed pre-construction tailgate safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission Construction & Maintenance (Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153; Chuck Hendry, 512-505-7151 if cranes are involved) and confirmation that the 48-hour advance notification arrangement for work near high-voltage lines is in place. Include this documentation with grading and demolition permit applications.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — these are pre-construction requirements that may be addressed at the permitting phase rather than site plan phase; reviewer should confirm appropriate phase for this documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Notice of Electrical Hazard meeting with AE Transmission Construction & Maintenance not documented. Schedule and conduct pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission (Contact: Andrew Perez 512-505-7153; Chuck Hendry 505-7151 if cranes used) at least 48 hours before construction begins. Submit meeting confirmation documentation with grading and demolition permit applications.

Pre-construction notification arrangement with Austin Energy for work near high-voltage lines to be documented prior to construction. Ensure that before any construction or grading activity begins within 10 feet of overhead transmission lines, Austin Energy is notified at least 48 hours in advance per Texas Health & Safety Code § 752.003 and arrangements are made to de-energize or relocate lines.

comments.title: Overhead Electric Line Voltage Class Unspecified — Transmission Safety and Crane Requirements Undetermined
comments.comment: The voltage class of existing overhead electric (OHE) lines along the property perimeter is not specified on the plans, making it impossible to determine whether transmission-class safety meeting, clearance, and crane operating requirements apply.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.14.0 and § 1.14.3.2 apply only to transmission facilities (≥60kV); Austin Energy operates transmission at 69kV, 138kV, or 345kV and distribution at typically 12.5kV. Without confirmed voltage class, the following cannot be determined:
- Whether the tailgate safety meeting with AE Transmission C&M is required (UCM § 1.14.0)
- Whether crane operators must maintain 20-foot clearance (transmission, per OSHA 1926.1400) or 10-foot clearance (distribution)
- Whether a crane safety personnel pre-construction briefing is required (UCM § 1.14.3.2)
Sheet 3 includes a section titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' suggesting transmission-class lines are present, and Sheet 21 shows dashed OHE lines along the property perimeter, but neither sheet specifies voltage. Construction of eight multi-story townhome buildings on a 2.16-acre site will likely require crane use.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Overhead electric (OHE) lines along south and north property boundaries; all construction areas near property perimeter requiring crane use
comments.resolution: Coordinate with Austin Energy to confirm the voltage class of all existing overhead electric lines on the property perimeter and add the voltage class to Sheet 3 or Sheet 21. If transmission-class (≥60kV): (1) implement tailgate safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.0 in construction documents; (2) specify 20-foot minimum crane clearance per OSHA 1926.1400; and (3) document crane safety personnel pre-construction briefing requirement per UCM § 1.14.3.2. If distribution-class (<60kV), document applicable distribution clearance requirements.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — Sheet 3 references 'Electric Transmission Notes' suggesting transmission-class lines, but voltage is unconfirmed; reviewer should verify with AE Design before requiring transmission-specific crane safety documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Coordinate with Austin Energy to determine the voltage class of existing overhead electric (OHE) lines shown on the property perimeter. If lines are transmission-class (69kV or higher), implement the tailgate safety meeting requirement with Austin Energy Transmission C&M per UCM § 1.14.0 and add the requirement to construction documents. If distribution-class (<60kV), standard distribution clearance and safety requirements apply.

If cranes or other mechanical equipment will be used during construction near existing Austin Energy facilities (existing OHE lines shown on property perimeter), crane operating plans must include Austin Energy facility clearance analysis. Implement the crane safety personnel pre-construction safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.3.2 and specify minimum clearances: 20 feet for transmission facilities or 10 feet for distribution facilities per OSHA 1926.1400.

comments.title: Inter-Departmental Agreement for Overlapping AE Transmission and Drainage Easements Not Submitted
comments.comment: No inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy and other city departments has been submitted to address the overlapping utility easement requirements present on this site.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.14.0 requires an inter-departmental agreement or MOU when AE transmission or electric easements overlap with other department jurisdictions. comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: Utility easement corridors throughout site; NE corner City of Austin drainage easement (0.130 acres, Instrument 2011021137); AE electric easements; Austin Water easement areas
comments.resolution: Submit an inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy, Austin Water, and the City of Austin Watershed Protection Department addressing the overlapping easement corridors on this site, clarifying access rights, maintenance responsibilities, and emergency protocols for areas where easement jurisdictions conflict.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution may involve Austin Water Utility and City of Austin Watershed Protection Department, both of which hold easement interests that overlap with AE easement corridors on this site.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should determine whether a formal inter-departmental MOU is standard practice for this type of easement overlap or whether this is a project-specific concern requiring escalation.

comments.title: Primary Service Routing and One-Line Diagram Missing
comments.comment: The primary routing from the Austin Energy transformer to each building's service entrance is not clearly documented, and no one-line electrical riser diagram has been provided.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that plans show the primary routing from the AE transformer to each building and include a one-line diagram of the electrical riser. Sheet 21 labels underground lines generically as 'Underground Electric Line' with a dash-E notation but does not specify which line segment represents the primary AE distribution path, conduit/conductor sizes, service voltage, or routing distances. Without this documentation, reviewers cannot verify that adequate space is reserved for AE facilities or that the service design is complete.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Utility Plan (Sheet 19)

(2) Identify the primary AE distribution path with explicit labels distinct from customer-owned secondary lines. (3) Label each routing segment with conduit size, conductor gauge, and service voltage.

perRunFindings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building is not clearly shown on plans with adequate specificity and labeling. Please provide detailed routing on the electrical plan showing the specific primary distribution path from the transformer(s) to each building's service entrance with dimensions and specifications.

perRunFindings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building not clearly shown or labeled. Provide clear routing diagram showing the complete path from transformer through pull boxes to service entrance of each building. Label routing with conduit size, conductor gauge, and service voltage specifications.
