comments.title: Electric Facility Labels Missing Required Technical Specifications
comments.comment: All electric facility labels on the electrical plans and site plan identify only the general facility type and omit required technical specifications including voltage, size, burial depth, and ownership.
comments.issue:
AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires electric facility labels to include applicable technical specifications. Labels observed on Sheets 9, 19, and 21 are limited to generic type descriptions and omit all required technical data:
- Transformers: labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad' only — no kVA capacity, voltage class, phase (single vs. three), or ownership (AE vs. customer)
- Pull boxes: labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' only — no conduit diameter, burial depth, or conductor specifications
- Meters: labeled 'Electrical Meters' only — no voltage or amperage rating
- Underground lines: labeled 'Underground Electric Line' or '-E-' only — no conductor gauge, service voltage, burial depth, or ownership
- Overhead line: labeled '-OHE-' on Sheet 9 only — no voltage or clearance specifications
Without this information, reviewers cannot verify code compliance, safety standards, service adequacy, or distinguish AE-owned from customer-owned facilities.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Plan (Sheet 19)
comments.applicableArea: All electric facilities shown on plans — transformer pads, pull boxes, meter banks, underground electric lines, and overhead electric lines throughout site
comments.resolution: Revise all electric facility labels on Sheets 9, 19, and 21 to add technical specifications relevant to each facility type: transformers — kVA capacity, primary/secondary voltage, phase, and ownership (AE or customer); pull boxes — conduit diameter, burial depth, and conductor gauge; meters — voltage and amperage rating; underground lines — conductor gauge, service voltage, burial depth, and ownership; overhead lines — voltage class. Distinguish AE-owned from customer-owned facilities on all labels.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facility labels are missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Please revise all facility labels to include applicable technical specifications such as voltage, conduit/conductor size, burial depth, and ownership.
applicableAreas: All electric facilities on site and utility plans

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Add complete technical specifications to all electrical facility labels including transformer kVA/voltage, pull box conduit size/burial depth, meter voltage/amperage, and underground line conductor gauge/voltage/burial depth. Labels must appear on all plan sheets where facilities are depicted.
applicableAreas: All electrical facilities shown on plans

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facility labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth), voltage (primary voltage level), and ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. All labels must include technical specifications relevant to each facility type for code compliance verification and construction clarity.
applicableAreas: All electric facility labels on electrical plans

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facilities are not clearly labeled on plans or labels lack facility type identification and technical specifications. Please provide labels for all electric facilities that clearly identify the type (e.g., 'Transformer Pad - AE Owned', 'Service Entrance Conduit', 'Pull Box') along with applicable voltage, size, and ownership information.

Electric facility labels missing facility type identification (customer vs. Austin Energy owned, voltage class, capacity). All electric facilities must include clear type identification and relevant technical specifications.

comments.title: Preliminary Electrical Plan Missing Conceptual-Design and No-Bid Disclaimers
comments.comment: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) does not include any explicit notes stating that the electric facilities shown are conceptual and not for bidding or construction purposes.
comments.issue: Reviewer Convention requires that when Austin Energy has not completed final electrical design, plans must include explicit disclaimer notes stating that (1) electric facilities shown are conceptual and not final design, and (2) the layout should not be used for bidding, material takeoff, or construction purposes, and that final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy. The word 'Preliminary' appears only in the Sheet 21 title block — no text note on the sheet or the general notes sheet (Sheet 3) contains this disclaimer language. Contractors bidding based on the preliminary electric design may face significant cost overruns when final AE Design coordination changes facility locations, sizes, or routing.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Sheet 21 — all preliminary electric facility locations (transformer pads, underground routing, pull boxes, meter banks)
comments.resolution: Add a prominent text note to Sheet 21 (and/or the cover sheet or general notes sheet) stating: 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Final electrical design will be coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy. These plans are not approved for bidding, material takeoff, or construction purposes.'

perRunFindings.comment: Plans showing 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' must include a note stating that electric facilities are conceptual design and final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy. Add disclaimer language to the general notes or electrical sheets.

Add explicit note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating that electric facilities shown are conceptual design and subject to final coordination with Austin Energy, and that this preliminary design is not approved for construction or bidding purposes.
applicableAreas: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and preliminary design coordination

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not clearly note that electric facilities shown are conceptual and not final design. Add explicit note to utility plan and/or coversheet stating: 'The electric facilities shown on this plan are preliminary and conceptual. Final electrical design will be coordinated with and approved by Austin Energy. These plans are not for bidding or construction purposes.'
Plans must include note stating that electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes and will be subject to final Austin Energy design coordination.

Add note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating: 'Electric facility layout shown herein is preliminary design and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design and coordination with Austin Energy is required before construction.'

Plans do not include note that electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes. Add explicit note to electrical plan and/or coversheet: 'This is a preliminary electrical design plan. These plans should not be used for bidding, material takeoff, or construction purposes. Final design will be provided by Austin Energy.'

comments.title: Electric Facilities Absent from Landscape Plan — Clearance Unverifiable
comments.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show any underground electric infrastructure from Sheet 21, making it impossible to verify tree and vegetation clearance compliance for underground utilities.
comments.issue: Reviewer Convention requires that AE overhead and underground electric facilities be shown on the landscape plan to enable clearance verification. Sheet 21 clearly shows four to five transformer pads, underground electric lines marked '-E-', pull boxes, meter banks, and associated easements throughout the site. Sheet 31 at the same scale (1"=20') shows building footprints, trees, shrubs, and paving, but includes only a single '-OHE-' overhead electric line along the bottom edge — no underground lines, no transformer pads, no pull boxes, and no electric easement boundaries. Without this overlay, reviewers cannot verify compliance with any tree-to-utility clearance requirements (including the 0–5 foot prohibition and 5–20 foot root barrier requirements for underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.10.4), nor can they assess potential canopy conflicts with overhead electric facilities.
comments.sheets: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site — all landscape areas where trees or shrubs are proposed in proximity to underground or overhead electric infrastructure
comments.resolution: Overlay all electric facilities from Sheet 21 onto Sheet 31, including: all transformer pad locations (with access clearance zones), underground electric line routing (with clearance buffer zones marked), pull box locations, meter bank locations, electric easement boundaries, vault easement, and overhead electric line with clearance/canopy conflict zone. Label each electric facility type to match Sheet 21.

perRunFindings.comment: Austin Energy overhead and underground facilities are not shown on landscape plans. Landscape Plan does not show transformer pads, pull boxes, or underground electric line routing shown on Electrical Design Plan, preventing verification of clearance compliance.

Overlay all electric facilities from Sheet 21 onto the landscape plan (Sheet 31), including transformer pads, underground electric lines (with 5-foot and broader clearance zones clearly marked), pull boxes, utility poles, vault locations, electric easement boundaries, and transmission easement boundaries.
applicableAreas: Entire site - all utility and landscape areas

perRunFindings.comment: Underground electric facilities (conduits, duct banks, pull boxes, transformer pads, vaults) shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not depicted on landscape plan (Sheet 31). To verify tree clearances from underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.10.4, add underground electric infrastructure to the landscape plan, showing all pull boxes, transformers, duct banks, and service routes.
applicableAreas: Entire site for underground electric infrastructure

comments.title: Electric Facilities Not Shown at Legible Scale on Site Plan
comments.comment: Electric infrastructure on the site plan (Sheet 9) is depicted with significantly less visual clarity and detail than other utility systems shown on the same sheet.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(1) requires that electric facilities be shown clearly and at legible scale on required plans, with symbols large enough to distinguish facility types. On Sheet 9, the overhead electric line is labeled '-OHE-' and transformer pads as 'Transformer Pad (Typ.),' but electric routing lacks the bold line weight, detailed callouts, and dimensional labeling used for water, wastewater, and storm drain systems on the same sheet. On Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), only a single '-OHE-' line is shown along the bottom edge at minimal scale with no clearance zones, making it difficult to distinguish from landscape features and raising potential canopy conflict concerns that cannot be evaluated.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Electric facility representations on Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 — overhead electric lines, transformer pads, underground electric routing
comments.resolution: Revise Sheet 9 to show electric routing and facility symbols with line weights and callout detail equivalent to other utility systems depicted. On Sheet 31, the landscape-electric coordination deficiency is separately addressed; however, at minimum, the existing '-OHE-' line on Sheet 31 should be shown with a clearance/canopy conflict buffer zone and a legible label.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-1 flagged Site Plan clarity deficiency (Sheet 9); run-3 flagged Landscape Plan legibility (Sheet 31) — the landscape plan issue is primarily addressed by the separate EL-16.22 comment; reviewer should confirm Sheet 9 electric symbology is independently adequate.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facilities may not be shown clearly and at legible scale on all required plan sheets. On Sheet 9 (Site Plan), electric facility routing and symbols lack the visual clarity and detail shown for other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Please enhance the electric facility representation on the site plan to provide equivalent clarity, with clearer routing, larger symbols, and more detailed labeling to match the standard used for other utility systems.

Electric facilities not shown clearly and at legible scale on landscape plan, or symbols too small to distinguish. Transformer locations, pull boxes, underground electric line routing, and electric easements must be shown on the landscape plan at adequate scale for visual coordination with landscaping.

comments.title: Electric Utility Easements Not Clearly Delineated; Two Recorded Easements Missing
comments.comment: Electric utility easements on the plans lack clear visual delineation distinguishing them from other linework, and two recorded easements are not depicted on the site plan at all.
comments.issue:
AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that electric utility easements be clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans. Two distinct deficiencies are present:
- Delineation deficiency: Easements shown on Sheets 9, 19, and 21 are labeled with text (e.g., '5' P.U.E. Vol. 69, Pg. 14', '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76', '3' Electric Easement', '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883') but are not visually distinguished with shading, hatching, bold boundary lines, or color fill that would make them readily identifiable as protected infrastructure areas.
- Missing easements: Per project facts, two recorded easements are not depicted anywhere on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (~0.31 ac, northeast interior), and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (~0.130 ac, northeast corner). Their absence prevents verification that proposed buildings and utilities do not conflict with these recorded restrictions.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Utility Plan (Sheet 19)
comments.applicableArea: All electric utility easements throughout property — including recorded easements along east and southeast property boundaries, 5' P.U.E., and two missing easements in the northeast portion of the site
comments.resolution: On Sheets 9, 19, and 21: (1) Add graphic visual emphasis to all electric utility easement boundaries — use hatching, shading, or bold boundary lines to distinguish easement areas from surrounding site. Retain existing text labels with volume/page references and widths. (2) Add the two missing recorded easements: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (~0.31 ac, NE interior) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (~0.130 ac, NE corner), with boundaries, widths, and recorded instrument references.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-3 identified two recorded easements absent from the site plan per project facts — reviewer should independently confirm easement boundaries and instrument numbers from the title report.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric utility easements are not clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans. Please add clear visual delineation (shading, hatch pattern, or bold boundary lines) to distinguish electric utility easements from the surrounding site area on site plan and utility plan, with labels showing easement width and recorded instrument numbers.
applicableAreas: Site plan and utility plan; all property boundaries

perRunFindings.comment: Electric utility easements not clearly delineated on plans. Two recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, City of Austin Drainage Easement) are missing from the site plan. All recorded electric and related utility easements must be clearly shown with locations, extents, and width dimensions.

comments.title: Trenching Assignments and Depth Notes Not on Electrical Plan
comments.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan does not include any notes specifying trenching responsibilities, depths, or material requirements for the underground electric work.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.5.3.4 establishes that the customer is responsible for trenching for underground electric work. Standard construction documentation practice requires that electrical plans include notes assigning this responsibility and specifying trench depths, material requirements, and existing utility conflict avoidance strategy. Sheet 21 shows extensive underground electric routing to all buildings but contains no callouts or notes addressing trenching assignments, required burial depths, conduit bedding specifications, or sequencing relative to other utilities. This creates ambiguity about customer obligations and contractor scope.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All underground electric line routing on site — entry from Valley View Road through transformer pads to all eight buildings
comments.resolution: Add a trenching note block to Sheet 21 specifying: (1) customer/contractor responsibility for all trench excavation per UCM § 1.5.3.4; (2) minimum trench burial depths for primary and secondary underground electric lines; (3) bedding and backfill material requirements; (4) requirement to locate and avoid existing utilities prior to trenching; and (5) any special constraints near the biofiltration-detention pond or drainage easement areas.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-1 flagged as unclear (operational practice vs. codified requirement) — reviewer should confirm whether AE requires trenching notes as a condition of preliminary plan approval.

perRunFindings.comment: Trenching assignments and responsibilities are not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). While customer trenching responsibility is established in UCM § 1.5.3.4 for underground work, the plans should include notes specifying trenching depths, materials, and construction responsibilities to ensure proper coordination with the contractor.

Add trenching assignment notes to the electrical design plan. Clearly identify the customer's trenching responsibilities, including trench depth, locating and avoiding existing utilities, and any special constraints per UCM § 1.5.3.4 and standard construction practice for underground electric service.

comments.title: Gas Service Status Not Documented on Any Plan Sheet
comments.comment: No plan sheet or supplementary document addresses whether natural gas service is required for the 39-unit residential development.
comments.issue: Reviewer Convention requires that plans indicate whether gas service is required and identify which site components will use gas service, or affirmatively state that gas service is not required. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and Engineer's Summary Letter all omit any reference to gas service. For a 39-unit multi-family townhome development, gas service determination for heating, cooking, and hot water systems is a material utility planning item. The absence of this information creates ambiguity about whether gas service was evaluated and determined unnecessary, or whether the requirement was overlooked.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire development — all 39 residential units across Buildings 1–8
comments.resolution: Add a utility note to Sheet 9 or Sheet 21 stating either: (a) the gas service provider, service routing, and which buildings/systems will use gas (if gas service is required); or (b) 'Natural gas service is not required for this development' (if all-electric). If gas service is required, show routing and service connection details on the utility plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not indicate whether natural gas service is required or identify which site components will use gas service. Add notation to the site plan and utility plans indicating gas service requirements and which buildings or building systems will use natural gas (e.g., unit heating, hot water systems).

Add a note to the site plan or utility plan clarifying whether natural gas service is required for the development. If gas service is required, show routing and service connection details. If gas service is not required, add a note stating 'Gas service not required for this development' per Reviewer Convention.

comments.title: Separate Electric Site Plan Submittal Status Unclear
comments.comment: It is unclear whether Sheet 21 constitutes a sufficient Electric Site Plan submittal or whether a separate, detailed electric site plan from a licensed professional engineer is required as a distinct document.
comments.issue: Reviewer Convention and UCM § 1.4.2.6 may require a separate Electric Site Plan submittal for projects of sufficient complexity. Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan,' raising the question of whether this constitutes a final accepted Electric Site Plan or a placeholder pending a more detailed separate submittal. No separate electric site plan document has been identified in the project file beyond Sheet 21. The determination depends on project complexity, AE coordination notes, and development type requirements — information not fully available in the submitted materials.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Plan set — Sheet 21 and potential separate submittal
comments.resolution: Confirm with Austin Energy whether Sheet 21 satisfies the Electric Site Plan requirement for this development type, or whether a separate detailed Electric Site Plan prepared by a licensed professional engineer is required as a distinct submittal to the AB+C portal. If a separate submittal is required, provide it as a separate document.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May involve Austin Energy Design — applicability determination depends on AE coordination notes and whether AE has accepted Sheet 21 as adequate.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Both runs flagged as unclear or conditional — reviewer should check AE coordination notes (Bluebeam) to determine if separate electric site plan was required.

perRunFindings.comment: A 'Preliminary' Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) is included in the site plan set, but it is unclear whether a complete, detailed Electric Site Plan has been submitted as a separate document or whether Austin Energy has accepted this preliminary sheet as adequate. Confirm with Austin Energy whether a more detailed separate Electric Site Plan submittal is required for this project.

Clarify whether Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) constitutes the required Electric Site Plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6, or whether a separate detailed Electric Site Plan from a licensed professional engineer is required. If a separate submittal is required, provide it as a separate document per Reviewer Convention.

comments.title: Building Setback Lines Not Explicitly Labeled on Electric Facility Plans
comments.comment: Building setbacks are referenced by scattered dimensional callouts on the site plan but are not drawn and labeled as explicit setback lines on the electric facility plans.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(v) requires that property lines and building setbacks be shown on electric facility plans (site plan and utility plan). Property lines are clearly shown on Sheet 9 with bearings and distances. However, building setbacks are conveyed only as individual dimension callouts (e.g., 26.1' from western boundary to Building 1, 21.3' from southern boundary to Building 8) and are not drawn as continuous labeled setback lines ('Building Setback' or 'B.L.'). Additionally, facts indicate a potential discrepancy in the depicted site area (site plan states 2.16 ac vs. deed 2.158 ac vs. TCAD 2.1970 ac vs. COA GIS 2.111 ac) and two unshown recorded easements that may affect where true property constraints lie.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All building setback lines throughout site — perimeter of Buildings 1–8 relative to property boundaries
comments.resolution: On Sheets 9 and 21, draw explicit setback lines labeled 'Building Setback' or 'B.L.' at the required setback distance from each property boundary. Convert the existing dimensional callouts into formal setback line annotations. Verify that property line depictions account for the two unshown recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use, City of Austin Drainage) before finalizing setback lines.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether the dimensional callouts on Sheet 9 satisfy AEDC setback labeling requirements or if formal setback lines are required.

perRunFindings.comment: Building setbacks not clearly shown on electric facility plans. While property lines are delineated, explicit building setback lines and labels must be shown on the site plan and utility plan to clearly establish the required buffer zones for electric facility planning.
applicableAreas: Electric facility plans (Site Plan, Utility Plan)

comments.title: Building Heights Not Shown on Electrical Plans
comments.comment: No plan sheet in the submitted set shows building heights, roof elevations, or overhead element dimensions needed to verify electric clearances to structures.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iii) requires that permanent structures be shown with both footprint and height on plans. Building footprints are shown on Sheet 21 and other sheets with finished floor elevations (FFE) noted (e.g., Building 1 FFE=687.50), but no roof elevations, total building heights, or dimensional data for architectural projections (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are provided. No dedicated building elevation sheets showing façade dimensions or roof heights are included in the 39-sheet plan set. FFEs alone do not establish total height or the relationship between structures and overhead electric facilities.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: All eight buildings on site — Buildings 1–8
comments.resolution: Provide building height information on Sheet 21 (and/or a separate building elevations sheet) showing the total height of each building from finished floor elevation to highest roof point, plus dimensions for any architectural projections (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies). Alternatively, annotate Sheet 21 with maximum building height callouts for each building footprint.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether building heights are available on other sheets not reviewed, or in supplementary documents.

perRunFindings.comment: Permanent structures not shown with both footprint and height on plans. Building elevation sheets must be provided showing building heights, roof lines, and all element dimensions (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) for clearance verification.

comments.title: Grading and Detention Pond Coordination with Electric Facilities Not Documented
comments.comment: No plan explicitly documents how the proposed grading, grade changes, and biofiltration-detention pond interact with underground electric facilities and easement access.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires that plans show final proposed topology — including grades, grade changes, floodplains, and detention ponds — for electric facility review. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows contour lines, building FFEs, and drainage infrastructure, and Sheet 15 addresses biofiltration-detention pond design. However, no plan confirms that: (1) underground electric line burial depths are adequate relative to proposed finish grades and grade changes; (2) easement access to transformers, pull boxes, and underground lines is maintained through or around the detention pond area; or (3) proposed structures and grading in or near floodplain areas do not conflict with electric facility locations.
comments.sheets: Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site — underground electric routing relative to proposed grades; biofiltration-detention pond area relative to electric easements and underground lines
comments.resolution: Provide a coordination note or overlay on Sheet 21 (or Sheet 11) confirming that: (1) underground electric line burial depths accommodate proposed finish grades and all grade changes; (2) transformer pad and pull box access is maintained through proposed grading; (3) the biofiltration-detention pond does not encroach on electric easements or interrupt underground line access; and (4) no electric facilities are located in mapped floodplain areas, or if they are, that appropriate protections are in place.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether the grading-electric coordination issue is independently reviewable from available plan sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans do not explicitly demonstrate that proposed topology (grades, grade changes, floodplains, detention ponds) will not adversely impact electric facilities. Grading plan must coordinate with electrical infrastructure to confirm adequate clearances and access are maintained for all electric facilities.

comments.title: Point of Electric Service Not Labeled on Required Plan Sheets
comments.comment: The point of electric service (POS) is not explicitly labeled or designated on any required plan sheet.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires the point of electric service to be shown on all required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 — specifically the site plan showing all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure and the apparent underground connection point from Valley View Road but contains no explicit 'Point of Service' or 'POS' label at the location where Austin Energy's conductors connect to the customer's conductors (as defined in UCM § 1.3.4). Sheet 9 shows a transformer pad but no POS designation. Sheet 31 shows only overhead electric lines with no POS marked. Without an explicit POS designation, compliance with the connection-point requirement cannot be verified.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Site-wide; western property boundary entry point from Valley View Road
comments.resolution: Add an explicit 'Point of Service (POS)' label on Sheet 21 at the specific location where Austin Energy's underground electric line connects to the customer's electrical infrastructure (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure). Carry this POS designation forward to Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) so the POS appears on all three required sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: Point of service location is not explicitly marked or labeled on any of the required plan sheets. The plans show electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines) but do not identify the specific point where Austin Energy's infrastructure connects to the customer's electrical system. The POS must be clearly designated on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

Point of service (POS) location is not explicitly labeled on any required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure but lacks a clear 'Point of Service' designation. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately identify the POS. Add explicit POS labeling to Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing where Austin Energy infrastructure connects to proposed customer infrastructure.

Point of electric service (POS) location is not explicitly designated on required plan sheets. Add clear labeling of the point of service location (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure) on all required sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(6) and UCM § 1.4.2.6.

comments.title: Electric Meter Locations Missing from Site Plan, Utility Tap, and Landscape Plans
comments.comment: The eight electrical meter locations shown on the Electrical Design Plan are not depicted on the site plan, utility tap plan, or landscape plan.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.4 and UCM § 1.9.3.1.A require electric meter locations to be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan showing all utilities, wet utilities/utility tap plan, and landscape plan). Sheet 21 clearly shows eight meter locations labeled 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors (Buildings 1–8), but Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains no meter locations, Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes a legend entry for utility symbols but no meters are drawn on the plan, and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no meter locations. Omitting meter locations from these sheets prevents verification of accessibility, line-of-sight to serving transformers, clearances from other utilities and landscape features, and compliance with grouped metering requirements under UCM § 1.9.3.4.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Building exteriors — Buildings 1–8 throughout site

perRunFindings.comment: Electric meter locations are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but are missing from the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Electric meter locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required plan sheets. Add 8 meter locations to: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - mark meter positions on each building; (2) Sheet 19 or 20 (Wet Utilities Plan) - show meter positions relative to water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities; (3) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - show meter positions to verify clearances from plantings. Label all meters with unique identifiers matching the electrical plan.

comments.title: Transformer Locations Inconsistent Across Sheets and Missing from Required Plans
comments.comment: The number and locations of transformer pads shown on the Electrical Design Plan do not match the site plan, and transformers are entirely absent from the utility tap, landscape, grading, and storm plans.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations to be shown consistently on all required plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable). The following deficiencies exist:
- Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows 4–5 transformer pads at specific distributed locations (northwest/west of Bldg. 1, west-central/west of Bldgs. 2 and 8, east of Bldgs. 4–5, and southeast/south of Bldgs. 6–7), while Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'— a representative symbol rather than the actual site layout
- Transformers are entirely absent from Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan — transformer pad symbol appears in legend but no transformers are drawn), Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan)
- Transformer labeling is inconsistent: Sheet 21 uses 'Electrical Transformer Pad' while Sheet 9 uses 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'
Absence of transformers from the grading and landscape plans prevents verification of required clearances, access routes, and conflicts with other utilities, trees, and site grading.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 20); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Site-wide — northwest (west of Bldg. 1), west-central (west of Bldgs. 2/8), southwest, northeast/east (east of Bldgs. 4/5), southeast (south of Bldgs. 6/7)
comments.resolution: Reconcile the transformer count and locations between Sheet 21 and Sheet 9, then show all proposed transformer pads at their actual site-specific positions (not as a single 'Typ.' symbol) on: Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), and Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan). Use consistent labeling across all sheets (e.g., 'Electrical Transformer Pad'). Update the Sheet 19 legend so that defined transformer symbols are actually drawn on the plan.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Different runs report 4 vs. 5 transformers on Sheet 21 — reviewer should confirm the exact transformer count from the electrical plan before requiring a specific number.

Add transformer locations to site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan. Ensure all transformer locations are consistent across all sheets.

Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) must match the transformer locations shown on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) in terms of quantity, position, and labeling. Currently, Sheet 9 shows one transformer marked '(Typ.)' while Sheet 21 shows four transformers with specific locations.

Transformer locations are not consistent across plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads while Sheet 9 shows only 1 transformer. Reconcile transformer locations and ensure all transformers appear on all required plan sheets with consistent positioning.

Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11), and Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) do not show any transformer locations. Revise all affected sheets to depict the five transformer pad locations with consistent positioning and labeling.

Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not consistent with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Sheet 9 shows one typical example while Sheet 21 shows 5 specific transformer locations. Revise Sheet 9 to show all 5 transformer locations in their actual positions on the site.

Transformer labels missing on required sheets or inconsistent. Establish consistent labeling (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad - Type [X], Size [Y] kVA") and show transformers on all required sheets: site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan (where applicable). Use a standard notation on all sheets.

comments.title: Street Lighting Layout and Conduit Plan Absent — AE Design Determination Required
comments.comment: No street lighting layout, pole locations, or conduit plan appears on any required sheet, and no documentation of Austin Energy Design's determination on street lighting applicability for Valley View Road frontage has been submitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.6.0 requires that when street lighting is required, the layout and pole locations be shown on the site plan and landscape plan, and the conduit plan (including connections and routing) be shown on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. The site abuts Valley View Road (a local street, ASMP Level 1), which may trigger street lighting requirements. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains a lighting note addressing only exterior building-mounted lights, not street lighting; Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows a street yard (H.2) along Valley View Road but no light poles; Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) contains no street lighting conduit layer. Per UCM § 1.6.0, the street lighting determination must be obtained by contacting AE Design — it cannot be made from plan review alone. Neither a street lighting layout nor documentation of an AE Design waiver or determination is present in the submittal.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Valley View Road frontage (western property boundary)
comments.resolution: Contact Austin Energy Design to obtain a written determination of street lighting applicability for the Valley View Road frontage. If street lighting is required: (1) add street light layout and pole locations to Sheet 9 and Sheet 31, and (2) add a street light conduit plan showing conduit routing and connections to Sheet 9, Sheet 31, and Sheet 21 per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. If street lighting is not required, include the AE Design waiver or determination letter in the submittal.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Street lighting determination requires coordination with Austin Energy Design; if street improvements along Valley View Road are also required, Transportation review may be involved.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Applicability cannot be determined from plan review alone — AE Design must confirm whether street lighting is required for this Valley View Road frontage.

perRunFindings.comment: Street lighting layout and light pole locations are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), though the site has public street frontage on Valley View Road. If street lighting is required per Austin Energy Design determination, the layout and pole locations must be shown on the site plan and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Confirm with AE Design whether street lighting is required for this project and provide documentation of the determination.

Cannot verify whether street lighting is required for this site from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required for the Valley View Road frontage per UCM § 1.6.0. If required, show street light layout and pole locations on site plan and landscape plan.

Street light conduit plan, conduit connections, and routing are not shown on any of the required plan sheets (Site Plan, Landscape Plan, Electrical Plans). If street lighting is required for this project, complete conduit plans must be provided per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. Confirm street lighting requirements with Austin Energy Design.

Cannot determine applicability from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required. If required, provide street light conduit plan showing conduit connections and routing on site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.6.0.

comments.title: Existing Transformer Pad and Meter from Survey Not Shown on Development Plans
comments.comment: An existing transformer pad and existing electrical meter visible on the existing conditions survey are not shown or accounted for on any development plan sheet.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that existing electrical facilities be shown on all applicable plan sheets with notation of their proposed disposition (retain, remove, or replace). Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an existing transformer pad in the southeast corner of the property and an existing electrical meter ('ELEC. METER') on the exterior wall of the main building, along with existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and utility poles. Neither facility is shown on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 11 (Grading Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) notes coordination with the City for removal of power poles and electric lines but does not specifically address the existing transformer pad or meter. Without showing these facilities on development plans, Austin Energy cannot verify how existing infrastructure will be handled during redevelopment.
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Southeast corner of property (existing transformer pad); main building exterior (existing electrical meter)
comments.resolution: Show the existing transformer pad (labeled 'EX Transformer Pad') and existing electrical meter (labeled 'EX Electrical Meter') on Sheet 21, Sheet 9, Sheet 31, and Sheet 11 using 'EX' or 'Existing' notation. Add a callout or general note on each sheet indicating whether each facility will be retained, removed, or replaced as part of the new development. Update the demolition plan (Sheet 8) to specifically address the disposition of both the existing transformer pad and existing electrical meter.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm the existence and locations of the existing transformer pad and meter on Sheet 4 before requiring disposition documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Existing transformer pad shown on survey (Sheet 4) must be depicted and labeled as 'Existing' or 'EX' on all applicable plan sheets, with notation indicating whether it will be retained, removed, or replaced.

Show and label the existing meter (with 'EX' or 'Existing' notation) on the electrical plan, site plan, and landscape plan. Include notation indicating whether it will be abandoned, removed, or retained and integrated into the new service design.

comments.title: Transformer Screening Intent Not Documented on Any Plan Sheet
comments.comment: No transformer screening is shown on any plan sheet, and no notation indicates whether screening is proposed or intentionally omitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that when transformer screening is proposed, the screening extent, dimensions, and door swing clearances be shown on all applicable plan sheets (site, grading, and landscape). Sheet 21 shows transformer pads as basic symbols with no screening details; Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) makes no reference to transformer screening or landscape treatment around electrical equipment; Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) contains no screening indication. Without a notation, it is ambiguous whether screening has not been designed or simply not documented.
comments.sheets: Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All proposed transformer pad locations throughout the site
comments.resolution: If transformer screening is proposed, add details to Sheet 21, Sheet 31, and Sheet 11 showing: (1) screening wall or fence extent and dimensions, (2) door swing clearances relative to screening, and (3) landscape plantings around screening. If no screening is proposed, add a note on Sheet 21 stating 'No Transformer Screening Proposed.'
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm whether transformer screening is required for this project type per Austin Energy standards.

perRunFindings.comment: If transformer screening is proposed, show on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan: screening wall/fence extent and dimensions, door swing clearances relative to screening, and landscape plantings around screening. If no screening is proposed, note 'No Screening' on electrical plan.

comments.title: Electrical Utility Legend Missing from Site Plan and Electrical Plan
comments.comment: No formal electrical utility legend exists on the site plan or electrical design plan, and the utility tap plan's legend defines electrical symbols that are not actually drawn on that sheet.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that proposed utilities be clearly delineated in plan legends. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) uses individual leader-line callouts ('Electrical Transformer Pad,' 'Electrical Meters,' 'Electrical Pull Box,' 'Underground Electric Line') but contains no formal symbol legend or key. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) has no electrical utility legend. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend in the top-right corner defining 'Proposed Underground Electric' and 'Transformer Pad' symbols, but neither symbol is actually drawn on Sheet 19 — making the legend non-functional. Without a consistent legend applied across sheets, reviewers cannot cross-reference electrical symbols or verify completeness of infrastructure documentation.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Plan-wide documentation
comments.resolution: Add a utility legend to Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 defining symbols for: (1) Electrical Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Pull Box, and (5) Electrical Easement (if applicable). Use the same symbols defined in the Sheet 19 legend, or reconcile the Sheet 19 legend to match. Ensure all symbols defined in any legend are actually applied and drawn on each respective sheet.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm whether a formal legend is required under UCM § 1.16.0 for this submittal type.

perRunFindings.comment: Add a legend to Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifying all proposed electrical utilities with symbols and descriptions, including: Transformer Pad, Electrical Meter, Pull Box, Underground Electric Line, and any other electrical facilities shown. Also add or enhance the legend on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to clearly show proposed electrical infrastructure symbols. Ensure symbols are consistent with any legend shown on other utility plan sheets (Sheets 19, 20).

Transformers not delineated in legend as proposed utilities. Add a Utility Legend to the site plan, wet utilities plan, and electrical plan defining the symbols for: (1) Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Easement, and (5) Pull Box. Use consistent symbols across all sheets. Ensure symbols are actually applied on the plans.

comments.title: Transformer Pad-to-Building Clearances Not Dimensioned on Plans
comments.comment: None of the five transformer pads include dimension callouts verifying the required minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from building faces, structures, and foundations.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to buildings, structures, and building foundations (with a limited exception for brick/masonry buildings with AE Design written approval). UCM § 1.10.5.B requires documentation of clearances to structures. No dimension lines or clearance annotations appear on the electrical plan or site plan for any of the five pad locations. Visual estimates from run-3 suggest Pad 4 (E of Building 4) may be approximately 5–10 ft from Buildings 4 and 5, placing it near the minimum threshold, but explicit dimensions are required to confirm compliance.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pad NW of Building 1; Transformer pad W of Building 2; Transformer pad W of Building 8; Transformer pad E of Building 4; Transformer pad E of Building 7
comments.resolution: Add dimension callouts on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) and/or site plan (Sheet 9) showing the measured horizontal clearance from each transformer pad edge to the nearest building face, structure, and foundation for all five pads. If any pad is adjacent to a brick/masonry building and relies on the AE Design exception, provide written AE Design approval in the submittal.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs; run-3 visual estimate places Pad 4 at approximately 5–10 ft from two buildings — verify actual dimension, as this pad is most likely to be at or near the minimum.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack specific dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot clearance from building faces, structures, and foundations. All five transformer pads must be dimensioned on the site or electrical plan to confirm compliance with UCM § 1.10.4.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies five transformer pads on the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these pads in relation to buildings and site features. However, NO dimension callouts or annotations specify the clearance distance from any transformer pad to any building face, structure, or foundation. Visual inspection of the scaled plans suggests the pads are immediately adjacent to or within feet of building edges, but without explicit dimensions, compliance with the minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from buildings, structures, and building foundations (with limited exceptions for brick/masonry buildings with AE Design written approval). The absence of dimension callouts showing these clearances is a deficiency. The burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate compliance through specific measurements on the plans. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes non-compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings are not dimensionally documented on the plans. No dimension lines or clearance callouts are shown to verify the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from buildings and building foundations. Provide dimension annotations on the electrical plan clearly showing the minimum 5-foot clearance from each building, or reference AE Design-approved pad detail sheets demonstrating compliance.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows 5 transformer pads without dimension callouts or clearance annotations. Visual analysis of the 1" = 20' scale drawing estimates distances: Pad 1 approximately 30-40 feet from Bldg 1; Pad 2 approximately 15-20 feet from Bldg 2; Pad 3 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 8; Pad 4 approximately 5-10 feet from both Bldg 4 and Bldg 5; Pad 5 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 7. No explicit dimension lines, measurement annotations, or written clearance specifications are shown on the plans. No reference to AE Design-approved pad detail sheets that would specify minimum clearance compliance.
perRunFindings.reasoning: While visual estimates suggest some pads may comply with the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement (Pads 1, 2, 3), the plans do NOT include actual dimension lines or clearance annotations to definitively confirm the requirement is met. The conservative pass/fail logic requires affirmative evidence (dimension callouts or clearance markings) that the requirement is met, not visual estimation. Pad 4, at approximately 5-10 feet from two buildings, is particularly ambiguous without precise dimensions. The applicant must demonstrate compliance through documented dimensions, not visual approximation.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Clearances from Back of Sidewalks Not Dimensioned
comments.comment: Transformer pads adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks lack dimension callouts verifying the required minimum 2-foot clearance from the back of sidewalks.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires transformer pads to be set a minimum of 2 feet from the back of sidewalks. Pads NW of Building 1, W of Building 2, and W of Building 8 (Pads 1, 2, 3) are positioned immediately adjacent to 5-foot concrete sidewalks and 4-foot decomposed granite walkways, but no dimension callouts or clearance annotations document the distance from any pad edge to the back of any adjacent sidewalk. Run-3 visual estimates place these pads at approximately 2–5 feet from sidewalk backs, making the minimum threshold potentially marginal without confirmed dimensions.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (Pad 1, adjacent to entry sidewalk); Transformer pad W of Building 2 (Pad 2, adjacent to sidewalk); Transformer pad W of Building 8 (Pad 3, adjacent to sidewalk); other pads with adjacent sidewalks
comments.resolution: Add dimension callouts on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9) showing the measured distance from each transformer pad edge to the back of the nearest sidewalk for all pads adjacent to pedestrian walkways. Dimensions must confirm at least 2 feet of clearance for each affected pad.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs; run-3 visual estimate suggests pads are approximately 2–5 feet from sidewalk backs — exact dimensions required, as some pads may be at or just at the 2-foot minimum.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalks where sidewalks are adjacent. Provide specific clearance dimensions on site plan.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (adjacent to entry sidewalk)
Transformer pad W of Building 2 (adjacent to sidewalk)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple sidewalk and walkway features throughout the site, including 5-foot concrete sidewalks along the entry drive and 4-foot decomposed granite walkways between buildings. Transformer pads are located in proximity to these sidewalks. However, no dimension callouts specify the distance from any transformer pad to the back of any sidewalk. The requirement is minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires transformer pads to be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks. The absence of specific dimensions showing this clearance on the site plan is a deficiency. Multiple sidewalks are shown near transformer locations, requiring verification of compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads positioned adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks (Pads 1, 2, 3) lack documented clearance dimensions from the back of the sidewalks. Provide dimension lines and callouts on the electrical plan showing the minimum 2-foot clearance from the back of sidewalks to each transformer pad, or demonstrate through AE Design approval that the configuration meets code.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows Pads 1, 2, and 3 each positioned immediately adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks running around the building perimeter. Visual analysis at 1" = 20' scale estimates these pads are approximately 2-5 feet from the back of the sidewalk. No dimension callouts are provided to document the exact clearance from the back of the sidewalk to the pad edge. The code requires 'minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks,' but the plans do not explicitly annotate this clearance.
perRunFindings.reasoning: While the visual estimate suggests the pads may be at or near 2 feet from the sidewalk (meeting the minimum), the plans provide no dimensional annotation to confirm this. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 2-foot minimum is met, not visual estimation. The pads appear to be within or very close to the sidewalk setback zone, creating ambiguity about whether they meet the 2-foot requirement.

comments.title: Hot-Stick Use Area Clearances and Access Door Orientation Undocumented
comments.comment: No transformer pad on the electrical plan indicates access door orientation or documents the required minimum 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance on the access door side.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires a minimum 10-foot clearance on the access door side of each transformer pad to open area or adjacent building/structure. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows all five pads as hatched rectangles but does not identify which side contains the access door for any pad, nor does it include dimension callouts for the required 10-foot clearance. Several pads are in constrained locations where access door orientation is critical: Pad 4 (E of Building 4) is approximately 5–10 ft from Buildings 4 and 5 on both sides; Pad 5 (E of Building 7) is approximately 2–5 ft from a parking drive lane per run-3 visual analysis. Without documented access door orientation and clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified for any pad.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All five transformer pad locations: NW of Building 1 (Pad 1), W of Building 2 (Pad 2), W of Building 8 (Pad 3), E of Building 4 (Pad 4), E of Building 7 (Pad 5)
comments.resolution: For each transformer pad on the electrical plan (Sheet 21), annotate the access door side and add a dimension callout showing the minimum 10-foot clearance from the access door face to the nearest open area or building/structure. Coordinate with AE Design to confirm that pad orientations as shown meet hot-stick access requirements prior to plan approval.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs; access door orientations are completely absent from the plans — Pad 4 (between two buildings) and Pad 5 (near parking lane) are highest priority for AE Design coordination.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack documentation of minimum 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance on access door side. All five pads require dimension callouts confirming clearance to open area or adjacent buildings.
perRunFindings.observation: The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows five transformer pads with hatched rectangles representing the pad footprint. However, no dimension callouts or annotations indicate the hot-stick use area clearance (the access door side). Sheet 9 shows these pads are located in constrained areas immediately adjacent to buildings, driveways, and other site features. No specific dimensions document a 10-foot minimum clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent building/structure.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies the hot-stick use area (access door side) must have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. This is a fundamental access requirement for equipment operation. Without documented dimensions, compliance cannot be verified. The constrained locations visible on the site plan suggest this clearance may not be met, but explicit dimensions are required to make a determination.

perRunFindings.comment: Hot-stick use area clearances (minimum 10 feet from access door side) are not documented on the electrical plan. For each transformer pad, clearly indicate which side the access door is located on and provide dimension callouts showing the minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. Verify compliance with AE Design specifications.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 does not document the direction of transformer access doors for any of the five pads, nor does it show the required 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance. Visual analysis shows: Pad 1 is approximately 2-5 feet from a sidewalk curb edge and approximately 5-10 feet from the main entry drive; Pad 4 is approximately 5-10 feet from Buildings 4 and 5 on both sides; Pad 5 is approximately 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane. The regulations require a 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent building/structure. Without documented access door orientation and clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The code specifies that the hot-stick use area (access door side) must have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. The plans do not identify which side of each pad is the access door side, nor do they document the clearance distance. Pads positioned 5-10 feet from buildings or 2-5 feet from sidewalks/parking areas may violate this requirement if the access door faces the nearby structure. The burden is on the applicant to document both access door location and clearance verification.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Clearances from Water, Wastewater, and Storm Drain Lines Undocumented
comments.comment: No dimension callouts on the electrical or utility plans document the required minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from any transformer pad to water service lines, wastewater service lines, or storm drain lines.
comments.issue:
UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water lines, wastewater lines, and storm drain lines. The following deficiencies exist across all three utility types:
- Water lines: Sheet 21 (electrical) and Sheet 19 (utility tap, showing 8-inch water main from Valley View Road and 2-inch HDPE domestic branches) are on separate sheets with no overlay or coordinated dimension callouts showing clearances between transformer pads and water lines.
- Wastewater lines: Sheet 19 shows wastewater infrastructure (6-inch PVC branches at 2.0% minimum slope, lift station, cleanouts) but transformer pads are not depicted on this utility sheet; no dimension callouts document clearances.
- Storm drain lines: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and Sheet 21 show storm drain ('SD') lines and transformer pads in proximity, particularly near the northeastern portion of the site, but no dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided at any pad location.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations relative to water service lines, wastewater service lines, and storm drain lines
comments.resolution: Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan (Sheet 21), utility tap plan (Sheet 19), and storm sewer plan (Sheet 12) — or on a coordinated overlay drawing depicting all utilities simultaneously — showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad edge to the nearest water line, wastewater line, and storm drain line, measured to pipe centerline or outer diameter. Note: Transformer Pad 3 has a reported physical overlap with a storm drain line that requires separate design resolution (see related comment).
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs for each utility type; run-1 additionally flags lack of a coordinated overlay drawing showing transformer pads and utility routing simultaneously.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from water lines. Provide specific clearance dimensions on electrical or utility plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows the transformer pad locations and includes blue line symbols representing 'Underground Electric Line.' The sheet references Sheet 19 for utility tap profiles showing water service connections. The plan indicates an 8-inch water line serves the site from Valley View Road. However, no specific dimension callouts on Sheet 21 or the electrical plan documents the horizontal clearance distance between any transformer pad and the water line serving the buildings. The requirement is minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and water lines. The water utility is shown on the site plans (noted as being 8 inches from Valley View Road per the Engineer's Summary Letter). Without specific dimensions showing the 5-foot clearance distance, compliance cannot be verified. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to water service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all water service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water service lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water line routing (-W- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads in close proximity throughout the site, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between the water lines and transformer pads at any location. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met, not general visual indication of separation.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pad locations not coordinated with water line routing on unified plan. Provide dimensioned utility coordination drawing showing transformer pads and water lines with documented 5-foot horizontal clearances.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water infrastructure
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pad locations but does not depict water line routing or utility conflicts. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows water line infrastructure (2" HDPE private domestic water branches and 6" main water lines) but does not depict transformer pad locations (transformer pads shown only on electrical sheet, not on utility sheet). While both utilities are shown on different sheets, no overlay or cross-reference plan is provided documenting distances between transformer pads and water lines.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and water lines. Without a coordinated drawing showing both transformer pads and water line routing simultaneously with dimensional measurements, clearances cannot be verified. The separation of transformer pads (on electrical sheet) from water infrastructure (on utility sheet) without a coordination overlay prevents documentation of compliance.

Sheet 19 shows wastewater service connections from the existing 8-inch wastewater line. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and wastewater lines. The wastewater utility routing is shown on the plans but clearance distances are not dimensioned. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to wastewater service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all wastewater service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows wastewater line routing (-WW- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between wastewater lines and transformer pads. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to wastewater lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater infrastructure
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads but does not show wastewater line routing. Utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater infrastructure (6" PVC wastewater branches at 2.0% minimum slope, lift station, cleanouts) but transformer pads are not depicted on this utility sheet. No overlay drawing provided showing both utilities simultaneously with dimensional clearance measurements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and wastewater lines. Separation of these utilities on different sheets without a coordination drawing showing distances prevents verification of compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from storm drain lines. Provide specific clearance dimensions on electrical, storm sewer, or site plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations and references Sheet 19 for profiles. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows the proposed storm drainage infrastructure. The storm drain system is illustrated on the site plan with 'SD' symbols indicating storm drain inlets and piping. However, no specific dimension callouts on the electrical plan, storm sewer plan, or site plan document the horizontal clearance distance between any transformer pad and the storm drain system. The requirement is minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance between transformer pads and storm drain lines. While the storm drainage is depicted on the plans, the required clearance dimensions are not provided. Missing required clearance documentation constitutes a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to storm drain lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the storm sewer and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all storm drain lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) show storm drain infrastructure (-SD- designated lines) and transformer pads on the site. Both drawings depict utilities and pads in close proximity, particularly near the northeastern portion where the biofiltration/detention pond and storm infrastructure are concentrated. No dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between storm drain lines and transformer pads to document compliance with the minimum 5-foot separation requirement.
