The storm and electrical plans show both utilities on coordinated sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.

comments.title: Transformer Pad 3 Physically Overlaps Storm Drain Line — Design Conflict
comments.comment: Transformer Pad 3 (central courtyard area) is drawn directly on top of a storm drain line labeled 'SD' on the electrical design plan, indicating zero horizontal separation where multiple code sections require minimum clearances and prior written approval for any crossing.
comments.issue:
Per visual analysis of Sheet 21, the Transformer Pad 3 symbol is positioned directly on top of the underground storm drain line routed through the central courtyard, violating the following requirements:
- UCM § 2.9.1.B.2: minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines
- UCM § 1.10.5.A: minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (zero clearance shown)
- UCM § 1.10.5.B: prohibition on locating transformer pads over other utility lines without written approval from the applicable utility authority
No written crossing approval from City of Austin Watershed Protection or AE Design is included in the submittal. The pad footprint (shown as a dotted rectangle) appears placed directly within the storm drain line routing.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer Pad 3, central courtyard area between Buildings 4, 5, and 6
comments.resolution: Resolve the design conflict by either: (1) relocating Transformer Pad 3 to a position that maintains the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from all storm drain lines per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 and minimum 12-inch clearance from other underground utilities per UCM § 1.10.5.A, and resubmit revised electrical and storm sewer plans; or (2) rerouting the storm drain line to achieve required clearances, with revised drainage and electrical plans submitted. If a utility crossing is determined to be unavoidable, provide written approval from City of Austin Watershed Protection Department and AE Design per UCM § 1.10.5.B before site plan approval.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution may involve coordination with City of Austin Watershed Protection Department regarding storm drain line rerouting or written crossing approval required under UCM § 1.10.5.B.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs flagged the physical overlap) — reviewer should independently verify Transformer Pad 3 position relative to 'SD' storm drain line on Sheet 21 before requiring design revision.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown directly on top of storm drain line on electrical design plan. This violates the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. Relocate transformer pad to avoid storm drain infrastructure, or modify storm drain routing with documented approval. Provide revised electrical and drainage plans showing minimum 5-foot clearance between transformer pad edge and storm drain line.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) explicitly states: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain). It is also adjacent to an underground electrical line route." This places Transformer Pad 3 directly overlapping the storm drain infrastructure shown on the electrical plan. Storm drain plan (Sheet 12) would document storm drain line routing in greater detail. Utility coordination between electrical and drainage systems is required to address this overlap.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. The vision analysis clearly confirms that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned on top of (zero clearance from) the storm drain line marked "SD" on the electrical design plan. This represents a complete failure to maintain the required 5-foot clearance and indicates either: (1) the transformer pad location is incorrectly placed, or (2) the storm drain routing conflicts with the intended transformer pad location. This conflict must be resolved by relocating either the pad or the storm drain line.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 overlaps underground storm drain line, providing zero clearance instead of required minimum 12 inches (horizontal and vertical). Revise design to relocate transformer pad outside of storm drain infrastructure or reroute storm drain to achieve minimum 12-inch clearance on all sides.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located over storm drain line
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned on top of underground storm drain line marked "SD" per vision analysis. This represents zero clearance in both horizontal and vertical dimensions from the storm drain infrastructure. UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from all underground utilities except those specifically exempted (gas, fuel, steam).
perRunFindings.reasoning: The overlapping of Transformer Pad 3 on the storm drain line (SD) shown on the electrical design plan demonstrates complete failure to maintain the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance required by UCM § 1.10.5.A. A transformer pad cannot be constructed directly over an underground storm drain line without creating structural and utility conflicts. This represents a design deficiency requiring resolution through pad relocation or utility rerouting.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 shown positioned over storm drain line, which violates prohibition against utilities crossing without approval. Provide documentation of written approval from City of Austin Watershed Protection Department and Austin Energy Design authorizing this utility crossing, or relocate transformer pad outside storm drain infrastructure.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central courtyard area
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of electrical design plan (Sheet 21) confirms: "The transformer pad symbol is drawn directly on top of an underground line labeled `SD` (Storm Drain)." This indicates that Transformer Pad 3 is positioned to cross over storm drain utility infrastructure. The pad footprint (shown as a dotted rectangle) appears to be placed directly within the storm drain line routing.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B prohibits locating transformer pads or Austin Energy underground facilities over or under other utility lines without written approval from the appropriate utility authority. The positioning of Transformer Pad 3 on top of the storm drain line represents a crossing/overlay configuration that violates this requirement. If utilities must cross, it requires documented written approval from both the stormwater utility (City of Austin Watershed Protection) and Austin Energy. No such approval documentation is provided in the site plan submittal.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Clearances from Other Underground Utilities Not Documented
comments.comment: No dimension callouts or cross-sections document the required minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities such as conduit, telephone, cable, and reclaimed water lines.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (excluding gas, fuel, and steam, which have separate higher requirements, and excluding water, wastewater, and storm drain, which are subject to the 5-foot requirement under UCM § 2.9.1.B.2). The utility tap plan (Sheet 19) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) show multiple utility types routed throughout the site. No cross-utility dimension callouts or clearance cross-sections are provided at any transformer pad location documenting compliance with the 12-inch horizontal and vertical separation requirement for conduit, telephone, cable, reclaimed water, or other underground infrastructure.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations relative to other underground utilities (conduit, telephone, cable, reclaimed water, and similar infrastructure)
comments.resolution: Provide detail cross-sections and/or dimension callouts on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) and utility tap plan (Sheet 19) showing the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from each transformer pad edge to all other underground utilities at locations where utilities are adjacent to or cross under pad footprints. Cross-sections must be drawn at adequate scale, identifying each utility type, and showing clearance measured from pad edge to utility centerline or outer diameter for both horizontal and vertical dimensions.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs; note that run-1 (1/3) also flags Transformer Pad 3 as physically overlapping a storm drain line — that specific conflict is addressed in a separate comment.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads lack dimension callouts verifying minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities. Provide comprehensive utility clearance documentation on plans.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple underground utilities including water, storm drain, and electrical lines labeled on the plan. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations and underground electric lines. The plans depict various utility lines throughout the site, but no specific dimension callouts show the 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearance required from transformer pads to other underground utilities (beyond the gas, water, wastewater, and storm drain already cited separately). Missing clearance documentation for other utilities such as reclaimed water, communications, or other underground infrastructure.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam which have higher requirements, and except the water/wastewater/storm drain which have 5-foot requirements). Without specific dimension callouts for all utilities, compliance cannot be verified. Missing required clearance documentation is a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearances from transformer pads to other underground utilities are not documented. Provide detail cross-sections and dimension callouts showing the minimum 12-inch clearance from each transformer pad to all other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, etc.), including both horizontal and vertical separations measured from pad edge to utility centerline or outer diameter.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to other underground utilities
perRunFindings.observation: Multiple utility sheets show water, wastewater, storm drain, and electric utility routing. However, no cross-utility dimension callouts are provided showing the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance between transformer pads and other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, reclaimed water, etc.). The utility tap plan and electrical plan show general routing but lack specific clearance documentation between different utility types adjacent to transformer pad locations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam - which have different clearance requirements). Without dimensional annotation on the plans documenting these clearances at specific locations where utilities cross or run parallel to transformer pads, compliance cannot be verified.

comments.title: No Cross-Section Drawings Provided for Transformer Pad Vertical Clearances
comments.comment: The 39-sheet plan set contains no cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at any transformer pad location, which is required to verify equipment access clearance where overhead structures, multi-story buildings, or parking areas are present.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes survey and design requirements for clearances from AE facilities to structures. None of the 39 submitted plan sheets include cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at any of the five transformer pad locations. The site includes multi-story buildings ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height, parking areas, and constrained courtyard locations. Transformer Pad 3 is surrounded by multi-story Buildings 4, 5, and 6 in a central courtyard configuration; Transformer Pad 4 (E of Building 4) is positioned between buildings; Transformer Pad 5 (E of Building 7) is near parking areas. No plan sheet shows vertical clearance from pad to overhead structures, building eaves, parking levels, or any enclosed features, nor does any sheet document clearance for crane or equipment access.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: All five transformer pad locations; highest priority: Transformer Pad 3 (central courtyard surrounded by Buildings 4, 5, 6) and Transformer Pad 4 (E of Building 4, between buildings)
comments.resolution: Submit cross-section drawings for each transformer pad location showing: (1) vertical clearance from finished grade to any overhead structure, building eave, parking level, or enclosed feature above the pad; (2) confirmation that no structures are positioned directly above the pad; and (3) adequate clearance for crane or equipment replacement access as required by AE Design. Drawings must be drawn at adequate scale with labeled dimensions and must correspond to each pad's specific site context.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged 2/3 runs; run-1 specifically flags Pad 3's central courtyard location surrounded by multi-story buildings as a critical location requiring vertical clearance verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at all transformer pad access paths are not provided. Submit cross-section drawings for each transformer pad location demonstrating minimum required vertical clearance for equipment access.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (survey requirement as required by AE Design)
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with overhead structures or enclosed access paths
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan set (39 sheets) includes plan views and various detail sheets but NO cross-section drawings are provided that specifically show vertical clearances at transformer pad access paths. The site has buildings on multiple levels with various finished floor elevations (ranging from 683.0' to 687.50' per Sheet 21), but there are no cross-sections showing the vertical space available for hot-stick access (35 feet clearance for standard access, or higher for specific confined situations). No vertical clearance profile is provided for any of the five transformer pad locations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Austin Energy Design typically requires cross-section drawings to verify vertical clearances at transformer pad access paths, particularly where overhead structures, building elements, or uneven topography could restrict clearance for equipment access and operation. Without these cross-sections, vertical clearance compliance cannot be verified. This is a standard documentation requirement for complete electrical site plan design.

perRunFindings.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations are not provided on the site plan. For each transformer pad location where overhead structures, building elements, or parking structures are present above or adjacent to the pad, provide cross-section drawings (drawn at adequate scale and clearly labeled) demonstrating the required vertical clearances from the pad to any overhead features.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with potential overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas
perRunFindings.observation: Review of all 39 sheets in the primary site plan revealed no cross-section drawings specifically showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations. The site plan shows buildings with various heights (33'-5" to 36'-1"), parking levels, and enclosed structures, but no cross-sections are provided to demonstrate vertical clearance compliance at transformer locations. The general notes reference cross-section requirements for other utilities (e.g., drainage, conveyance), but no cross-sections are provided specifically showing vertical clearances from transformer pads to overhead structures, parking garage levels, or enclosed areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes survey and design requirements for clearances from AE facilities to structures. Transformer pads located between buildings or adjacent to parking areas (particularly Pad 4 between Bldgs 4-5, and Pad 5 near parking) warrant vertical clearance verification through cross-section drawings. The absence of any cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at these locations is a clear failure to document compliance with this requirement. The code requires demonstrating that overhead structures, building eaves, or parking structures do not create vertical clearance violations.

perRunFindings.comment: Cross-section drawings not provided showing vertical clearances around transformer pads. Provide cross-section drawings through Transformer Pad 3 location demonstrating adequate vertical clearance for equipment access, maintenance, and operation; confirm no structures are positioned directly above pad.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations, particularly Transformer Pad 3 in central courtyard
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads as simple dotted rectangles. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout without transformer detail. Grading plan (Sheet 11) shows site topography and building elevation profiles. However, no cross-section drawings or vertical clearance profiles are provided showing: (1) vertical clearances in the central courtyard area where Transformer Pad 3 is surrounded by multi-story buildings (Buildings 4, 5, 6), (2) overhead obstructions or structures above the transformer pad locations, or (3) vertical clearances for crane/equipment access.
perRunFindings.reasoning: No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances around transformer pads are provided in the plan set. For Transformer Pad 3 especially, which is surrounded by buildings and located in a courtyard area, vertical clearance documentation is required to demonstrate that: (1) no structures hang directly above the pad, (2) adequate clearance exists for equipment maintenance and replacement, (3) proper ventilation is available if niche configuration applies, and (4) liquid drainage paths exist if oil-filled equipment.

comments.title: Bollard Protection Missing or Incomplete for Transformer Pads Near Vehicle Routes
comments.comment: Three of five transformer pads are within 4 feet of vehicle circulation driveways and lack bollard callouts, placement dimensions, or detail references on the site plan and electrical plan.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards per AE Design equipment pad details for transformer pads installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes, with spacing that allows the equipment door to open fully. The site plan (Sheet 9) documents bollard protection for the pads E of Building 4 and E of Building 7 (via 'Bollard (Typ)' callouts), but the following pads lack any bollard documentation despite being within or adjacent to vehicle circulation routes:
- Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (Pad 1): visually confirmed at 0 feet from driveway edge (touching entry driveway)
- Transformer pad W of Building 2 (Pad 2): within 4 feet of internal driveway
- Transformer pad W of Building 8 (Pad 3): within 4 feet of internal driveway (status to be confirmed per run-2); also cited by run-3 as Pad 5 (southeast location) at approximately 2–5 feet from parking drive lane
Construction details (Sheet 22) include bollard specifications per COA standards but no bollard callouts or detail references are provided on Sheet 9 or Sheet 21 for the unprotected pads.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Construction Details (Sheet 22)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (Pad 1, entry driveway); Transformer pad W of Building 2 (Pad 2, internal driveway); Transformer pad W of Building 8 / Pad 3 or Pad 5 per differing run descriptions (near parking/circulation drive lane)
comments.resolution: Add bollard callouts, placement dimensions, and AE Design equipment pad detail references on the site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) for each transformer pad within 4 feet of a parking area or vehicle route that does not already show bollard protection. Bollards must be 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts; spacing must allow the equipment door to open fully per AE Design equipment pad details. Verify that bollard specifications in construction details (Sheet 22) match AE Design equipment pad requirements for all pad locations.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-2 identifies pads NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 as missing bollards; run-3 separately flags Pad 5 (southeast location) — reviewer should verify which specific pads require bollards and confirm Sheet 9 bollard callouts for Bldgs 4 and 7 pads are complete and correctly referenced.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads NW of Building 1 and W of Building 2 are located within 4 feet of vehicle circulation driveways but lack bollard callouts and specifications. Provide bollard details and callouts on the site plan for all transformer pads within 4 feet of parking or vehicle routes, with specifications matching AE Design-approved pad details.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad NW of Building 1 (within 4 feet of entry driveway)
Transformer pad W of Building 2 (within 4 feet of internal driveway)
Transformer pad W of Building 8 (within 4 feet of internal driveway - status to be confirmed)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows all five transformer pads located immediately adjacent to vehicle circulation routes (driveways). Vision analysis confirmed that pads NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, W of Bldg 8, E of Bldg 4, and E of Bldg 7 are all within or very near the 4-foot threshold from vehicle circulation areas. The measure-distance tool confirmed the pad NW of Bldg 1 is 0 feet from the driveway edge (touching the driveway). Sheet 9 shows bollard callouts (labeled 'Bollard (Typ)') pointing to features at two locations: E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7. These two pads have bollard protection documented. HOWEVER, the pads at NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 are equally constrained by proximity to vehicle circulation but show NO bollard callouts or detail references on the site plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies that equipment pads installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes must be protected by 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details, with spacing that allows equipment door opening. The site plan clearly shows two of five transformer pads (E of Bldg 4 and E of Bldg 7) with bollard protection documented via callouts. However, the other three pads (NW of Bldg 1, W of Bldg 2, and W of Bldg 8) are equally exposed to vehicle circulation (based on spatial layout) but lack any bollard documentation. This represents an inconsistency and likely non-compliance for the unprotected pads. At minimum, the pads at NW of Bldg 1 and W of Bldg 2 require bollard documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 5, located within 4 feet of a parking/circulation drive lane, requires bollard protection. No bollard specifications, locations, or details are shown on the electrical plan or construction details. Provide dimension callouts and detail references (per AE Design equipment pad details) showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards installed to protect the transformer pad, with spacing that allows equipment door opening.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 and visual analysis show Pad 5 located in the southeast section of the site, positioned approximately 2-5 feet north of the southern driveway/parking lane. The Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) shows this area is part of the main circulation and parking zone. The code requires bollards (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts) when transformer pads are installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes. Pad 5's estimated 2-5 foot distance from the parking drive lane indicates it falls within the 4-foot bollard requirement threshold. However, no bollard specifications, locations, or detail references are shown on the site plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Based on visual analysis, Pad 5 is estimated to be 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane, placing it within the 4-foot triggering distance for bollard installation. The absence of any bollard callouts, specifications, or detail references on the electrical plan or construction details sheets suggests the requirement is not being addressed. Without explicit bollard documentation showing their location, spacing, and specifications per AE Design equipment pad details, compliance cannot be verified.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 located in parking/circulation area without bollard protection shown. Provide detailed electrical or site plan showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards positioned around Transformer Pad 3 to prevent vehicle contact. Bollard spacing must allow pad access door to open fully per Austin Energy Design equipment pad standards.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 located in central parking/circulation area
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned in the central courtyard area described as "located within an open paved/drive area surrounded by the three aforementioned buildings." Site plan (Sheet 9) shows this central area includes parking and circulation areas with driveways. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 states: "Bollards or protection barriers: None are shown or labeled." Construction details (Sheet 22) include bollard specifications per COA standards but no bollards are called out or dimensioned on the electrical plan for the transformer pad areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Transformer Pad 3 is positioned in the central site area that serves as a parking/circulation zone between Buildings 4, 5, and 6. This location puts the pad within the 4-foot proximity zone that triggers bollard requirements. No bollards are shown on any plan sheets protecting this pad from vehicle contact. Bollard placement and spacing must be shown on electrical/site plans to prevent accidental vehicle impact on the transformer equipment.

comments.title: Electrical Routing Clearance from Drainage Infrastructure Not Documented
comments.comment: Clearance distances between underground electrical conduit routing and storm drain/wastewater infrastructure are not dimensioned or annotated anywhere in the plan set.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 12-inch clearance between AE underground cable/conduit and other utilities; operational practice may require 5-foot clearance for drainage infrastructure. UCM § 1.13.0 additionally requires that proposed storm drain routing conflicts with existing street light conduit be discussed with AE Design for resolution. The following deficiencies are present:
- Sheet 21 shows electrical routing (solid blue lines) crossing storm drain (SD) and wastewater (WW) dashed lines at multiple locations throughout the site, including near Buildings 2, 4, 5, and 8, and adjacent to Transformer locations T1–T4, but no clearance dimensions or callouts appear at any crossing point
- Sheet 12 shows 18-inch and 24-inch HDPE storm drain pipes with profile elevations, but these profile details are not correlated with electrical routing clearance measurements on Sheet 21
- No AE Design coordination documentation has been provided confirming acceptable separation between storm drain routing and underground electrical conduit or street light conduit
- At plan scale (1" = 20'), visual separation on the plan does not constitute verified clearance
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: All locations where electrical routing crosses or runs parallel to storm drain (SD) and wastewater (WW) infrastructure — confirmed crossings near Buildings 2, 4, 5, and 8; Transformer areas T1, T2, T3, and T4
comments.resolution: Provide cross-section details or a dimensioned coordinate overlay at each electrical/drainage crossing location on Sheet 21 showing both horizontal and vertical separation distances; confirm minimum 12-inch clearance (or 5-foot if required by AE operational practice) is achieved at every crossing. Additionally, provide written AE Design coordination documentation or an Austin Energy letter of concurrence confirming acceptable separation between storm drain routing and underground electrical conduit/street light conduit throughout the site.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy (AE Design) to confirm acceptable separation distances and to obtain written concurrence documentation per UCM § 1.13.0.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Clearance compliance cannot be confirmed from plan-scale drawings alone; cross-section details or AE Design coordination letter must be submitted before this can be closed.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearances between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure not documented. Provide dimension details or engineering notes confirming that electrical conduit routing maintains minimum 12-inch clearance from all drainage pipes, storm drains, and related infrastructure at all crossing and adjacent locations.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths crossing or running near storm drain infrastructure
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan). Sheet 21 shows blue electrical routing lines (marked 'E') crossing or running near dashed lines representing storm drain (SD) lines marked with square inlet symbols. Multiple crossing locations are visible on the plan. For example, electrical routing crosses storm drain lines between Building 2 and Building 8, and near Building 4. However, no dimension labels or callouts indicate the clearance distance between the electrical lines and storm drain lines at these crossing locations. No specifications confirm that minimum 12-inch clearance (or operational practice 5-foot clearance) is maintained.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-inch clearance between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure. While the plans show electrical lines and drainage infrastructure, the clearance distances at crossing points are not dimensionally verified. Without specific clearance measurements at each crossing, compliance cannot be confirmed. The visual separation on a 1" = 20' scale plan may be deceptive and does not constitute adequate verification of actual clearances. Engineering coordination between electrical and drainage design should document these clearances explicitly.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 is located adjacent to wastewater easements (T1, T4) and storm drain infrastructure (T2, T3), but no specific clearance dimensions are documented. Overlay Sheet 21 electrical routing with Sheet 12 drainage infrastructure details to verify minimum 12-inch clearance from drainage facilities. Provide cross-section details or a coordinate overlay demonstrating that electrical conduit maintains adequate clearance from all drainage infrastructure, or provide documentation from Austin Energy confirming acceptable separation distances for this site configuration.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing near Transformers 1, 2, 3, 4 and associated drainage infrastructure
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 12 to identify proximity of electrical routing to drainage infrastructure. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted: 'Drainage: There is an underground storm drain network (marked with dashed lines and SD) running parallel to the electrical lines in several places, particularly close to the routing near Bldg. 8 and Bldg. 4/5.' Vision analysis of Sheet 9 identified: 'T1 has Wastewater Easement nearby; T2 and T3 have Storm Drain lines adjacent; T4 has Wastewater Easement nearby.' The site plan shows utility lines for water (W), storm drain (SD), and wastewater (WW) running throughout the property. However, no specific clearance dimensions or separation distances are provided on any of the sheets. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows 24-inch and 18-inch HDPE storm drain pipes with specific elevations and profiles, but these details do not correlate with specific electrical routing clearance measurements on Sheet 21.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 (Clearances for AE Underground Cable, Conduit, and Underground Facilities) specifies 'minimum 12-inch clearance to other utilities.' The code citation language allows for interpretation - the minimum 12-inch clearance standard applies, but operational practice (referenced in the grouping as 'operational practice may require 5 feet for drainage infrastructure') may impose stricter separation for compatibility. Without specific clearance dimensions shown on the electrical plan or correlated details between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure profiles, it cannot be definitively determined whether the 12-inch minimum (or operationally appropriate 5-foot) clearance is maintained. The visual proximity noted by the vision analysis (routing 'very close' to drainage lines) suggests potential inadequate clearance, but cannot be confirmed without detailed profile views or cross-section details showing the vertical and horizontal separation distances between electrical conduits and drainage pipes.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical routing from riser to transformer appears to cross drainage pipes and storm inlets. Clearance of drainage pipes and inlets with required minimum distance (12 inches per code, 5 feet per operational practice) cannot be verified from available evidence.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters throughout site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) vision analysis noted: 'The blue electrical lines frequently cross or run parallel to grey dashed lines labeled "SD" (Storm Drain) and "WW" (Wastewater) throughout the site layout.' Without specific distance callouts or sectional details showing clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 12 shows storm sewer plan; Sheet 21 shows electric design with underground routing. comments.title: Transformer Locations Not Shown on Building Elevation Sheets
comments.comment: No architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations or vertical clearances from building features have been identified in the 39-sheet plan set.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations and clearances to be shown on elevation sheets to verify compliance with separation requirements from building features including windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes, and overhangs. Two independent review runs flagged this deficiency. The 39-sheet plan set includes site plan, utilities, grading, drainage, landscape, and construction detail sheets, but no architectural elevation sheets depicting transformer locations or building facade clearance dimensions. Building heights are referenced in tabular form on Sheet 9, but no vertical cross-sections show transformer positions relative to building features. It is possible that elevation sheets exist in a separate architectural drawing set not included in this submission.

comments.applicableArea: All 5 transformer pad locations throughout site; facades of all 8 multi-story buildings where transformers are within proximity
comments.resolution: Provide architectural elevation sheets clearly showing each transformer pad location relative to adjacent building features (windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes, overhangs), with clearance dimensions per UCM § 1.16.0. If elevation sheets are contained in a separate architectural drawing set, submit that set as part of this application.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — confirm whether architectural elevation sheets exist in a separate architectural submittal before requiring resubmission; 8 multi-story buildings with pad-mounted transformers may require this review.

perRunFindings.comment: Architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations are not identified in the plan set. Either provide elevation sheets clearly depicting transformer locations, or clarify whether such sheets are included in the 39-sheet set.

The sheet index lists sheets 1-39 but does not clearly identify which sheets are architectural elevation sheets. Sheet 38 is 'Wall Plan' with details and cross-sections, and Sheets 29-37 are addressing, tree, landscape, and canopy/root zone exhibits, but architectural elevation sheets showing transformer locations are not apparent from the available sheet titles.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations shown on elevation sheets to verify vertical clearances and building feature conflicts (windows, stairs, doors). This site has 8 buildings with multiple stories (up to 3 stories per Sheet 9 data). Without identified architectural elevation sheets in the plan set, it cannot be determined whether transformers are shown at the required elevations. This could be a missing document type or a labeling issue in the sheet index.

perRunFindings.comment: If transformer locations are within 20 feet of building features (windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes) per UCM § 1.10.4, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on building elevation sheets to verify compliance. Provide elevations if transformers are located adjacent to buildings.
perRunFindings.observation: The primary site plan set (39 sheets) does not include dedicated elevation sheets showing transformer, meter, or electrical equipment details. Sheet index in README.md lists sheets 1-39, which include site plan, utilities, grading, drainage, landscape, and construction details, but no architectural elevation sheets specific to building facades or electrical equipment elevations. Building heights are shown on Sheet 9 site plan data table, but no vertical cross-sections showing transformer locations relative to building features are provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations and clearances must be shown on elevation sheets to verify compliance with clearance requirements from windows, doors, stairs, fire escapes, and building overhangs. If the site plan set does not include elevation sheets that show transformers, this deficiency cannot be fully evaluated. comments.title: Conditional Electrical Items Require Applicant Clarification on Applicability
comments.comment: Three conditional electrical checklist items cannot be evaluated without applicant clarification on whether their triggering conditions apply to this project.
comments.issue:
The following conditional UCM § 1.16.0 requirements have unclear applicability and require applicant response:
- Pull box documentation (UCM § 1.16.0): Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box,' but the plans do not state whether pull boxes are 'required by Austin Energy electrical service design specifications.' If required by design, they must be confirmed shown on all applicable utility plan sheets
- Underground vaults/manhole documentation (UCM § 1.16.0): Current design uses surface pad-mounted transformers and surface pull boxes; no underground transformer vaults or electrical vaults requiring manhole access appear to be included, but this has not been explicitly confirmed by the applicant
- Pole or driveway relocation (UCM § 1.16.0): The site was cleared following demolition of the prior assisted living facility (June 2022); the 2018 CDS survey should be reviewed to confirm whether any existing utility poles or driveways conflict with proposed electrical routing or transformer locations, and whether relocations are required
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Underground electrical routing throughout site; transformer pad locations T1–T5; site entrances and driveways
comments.resolution:
Applicant should provide written responses confirming:
- Whether pull boxes are required per AE electrical service design specifications; if required, confirm they are shown on all required utility plan sheets
- Whether any underground transformer vaults or electrical vaults requiring manhole access are part of the design; if so, show manhole locations on site plan (Sheet 9), wet utilities, and landscape sheets
- Whether the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) identifies any existing utility poles or driveways conflicting with proposed electrical routing or transformer locations; if relocations are required, show on Sheet 21 and coordinate with Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should determine applicability of each sub-item based on applicant's written response before requiring plan revisions.

perRunFindings.comment: If pull boxes are required by Austin Energy electrical service design specifications, confirm their locations are shown on all utility plan sheets. If not required, this item is not applicable. Clarify in the electrical specifications whether pull boxes are required or optional for this installation.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' positioned throughout the site on the underground electric routing. However, the vision analysis determined that these are likely pull boxes for the electrical service routing (standard for underground utility systems) but the plans do not explicitly state whether pull boxes are 'required by electrical service design' or whether they are only being provided as standard practice. The distinction matters for this checklist item: if pull boxes are required per Austin Energy design specifications, then showing them is required; if they're optional, then omitting them would not be a deficiency.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The applicability note for EL-15.37 states 'Only when pull boxes required by electrical service design.' This checklist item is conditional. Pull boxes are standard in underground electrical systems for drawing cable and navigation, but they must be explicitly required by Austin Energy or electrical specifications to trigger this checklist requirement. Without clear indication that pull boxes are required by design, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

perRunFindings.comment: Clarify whether this project includes any underground electrical vaults or transformer vaults requiring manhole access. If only pull boxes are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable. If underground vaults are required, show manhole locations on all required plan sheets (site, wet utilities, landscape).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box' but does not explicitly show any separate manhole locations distinct from pull boxes. Pull boxes and manholes are different - pull boxes are small access points for drawing cable, while manholes are larger access points for vault-like underground utility infrastructure (such as underground transformer vaults or junction points). The plans do not indicate whether any true underground vaults or transformer vaults are required. The applicability note states 'Only when manholes required for electrical service,' which is a conditional applicability requirement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Manhole locations are only relevant if the electrical service design includes underground vaults, transformer vaults, or other vault-like installations. The current design shows pad-mounted surface transformers and pull boxes, not underground vaults. Without explicit indication that underground vaults requiring manhole access are part of the design, this item may not be applicable.

perRunFindings.comment: Review the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4 or external survey document) to confirm whether existing poles or driveways conflict with proposed transformer, electrical routing, or access route locations. If relocations are required, show this on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and coordinate with Site Plan (Sheet 9) for driveway relocation scope. If no conflicts exist, this item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: The applicability note states: 'Only when pole or driveway relocation required. Check: survey for existing poles/driveways in conflict with proposed development.' The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4 per README) and the site plan show the site is cleared following demolition of the prior assisted living facility. The site plan shows proposed driveways and parking in locations consistent with site topography and building locations. The survey references (CDS Survey noted in facts.md from 2018) would need to be examined to confirm whether existing poles or driveways remain in the proposed improvement area.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item is conditional on whether relocation of poles or driveways is required. Without explicit indication in the plan notes that relocations are necessary, or survey evidence of conflicts, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

comments.title: Conditional Electrical Requirements Appear Inapplicable — Reviewer Should Confirm
comments.comment: Three conditional electrical checklist requirements appear not to apply to this project based on its characteristics, but reviewer confirmation is needed before closing.
comments.issue:
The following conditional requirements were evaluated and appear inapplicable:
- Niche service requirements (UCM § 1.10.4, footnote 3): Sheet 21 shows only surface pad-mounted transformer pads; no niche service configuration (transformer installed within a building footprint, exterior-accessible) is indicated anywhere in the design
- Per-site transformer requirement for multi-site developments (UCM § 1.16.0): The project is a single-site development on a single parcel (Lot 1, Mecey Subdivision, Parcel ID 0406100252, 2.16 acres); multi-site provisions do not apply
- Minimum flood elevation for meters (UCM § 1.9.3.1.G): The site is confirmed in FEMA Flood Zone X, outside both the 100-year and 500-year floodplain, with no COA floodplain intersection; the 100-Year Reference Flood Datum elevation requirement is not triggered
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations and meter locations throughout the site
comments.resolution: Reviewer should confirm: (1) no niche-type transformer installations are proposed or required by AE design, (2) the project is a single-site development with no distinct separately-served parcels, and (3) the FEMA Zone X designation is current and no portion of the site intersects the 100-year or 500-year floodplain. If any of these conditions differ, the applicant must provide documentation per the applicable UCM section.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify all three conditional items are indeed inapplicable before closing; niche service and flood zone determinations should be confirmed against AE records.

perRunFindings.comment: If niche service is required or proposed for any transformer, provide: (1) niche plan showing equipment location within building footprint, (2) profile showing niche dimensions and exterior access, (3) evidence of AE Design consultation and approval. If only pad-mounted transformers are used (as currently shown), this item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 pad-mounted transformer pads, all positioned outside buildings on the site surface. There is no indication of any niche service (specialized transformer installation within building footprint, accessible from exterior). The applicability note states this item applies 'only when transformer service via specialized niche' and requires 'transformer service via specialized niche (equipment within building footprint, accessible from exterior, site outside Network Area).' The site plan shows all transformers as surface pad-mounted equipment, not niches.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Niche service is a specialized configuration where transformer equipment is installed within a building's footprint but remains accessible from the exterior for Austin Energy access. This is fundamentally different from the pad-mounted transformers shown on the plans. Without indication of niche service in the design, this item does not apply.

perRunFindings.comment: If this is a multi-site development (multiple distinct sites, each potentially serving independent customer groups), verify that each site has its own transformer. If this is a single-site development (as currently described), this item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows a single development with 8 buildings and 39 units served by 5 transformers. The applicability note states: 'Only for multi-site developments. Check: project description or site plan for number of distinct sites.' The site plan (Sheet 9) describes the project as a single site: 'Valley View Townhomes' on 'Lot 1, Mecey Subdivision.' The facts.md confirms a single parcel (Parcel ID 0406100252, 2.16 acres). There is no indication this is a multi-site development.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item is conditional on the project being a multi-site development where each site should have its own transformer. The Valley View Townhomes project is a single development on a single lot. Therefore, this item does not apply.

perRunFindings.comment: Since the site is in FEMA Flood Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), minimum flood elevation requirements for meters do not apply. This item is not applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: The facts.md confirms the site is in 'FEMA Flood Zone: Zone X (outside 100-year and 500-year floodplain)' and 'COA Flood Zone: Zone X' with 'Floodplain intersection: None.' Sheet 21 does not indicate meter elevations relative to flood levels because the site is not subject to the 100-Year Reference Flood Datum requirement. The applicability note states: 'Only when site is subject to 100-Year Reference Flood Datum ordinance.' Since the site is in Zone X (no floodplain), this requirement does not apply.
perRunFindings.reasoning: This item applies only to sites within a 100-year floodplain subject to elevation requirements. The Valley View Townhomes site is outside the floodplain in Zone X, so flood elevation requirements do not apply.

comments.title: Trees Near Overhead Electric Line — UC Status and Clearances Undocumented
comments.comment: The landscape plan proposes large trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm) adjacent to the overhead electric line along the southern and western boundaries without documenting utility-compatible (UC) species status per ECM Appendix F or dimensioning clearances from the conductor, and the OHE line voltage is not classified.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only UC-designated species be planted within 15 ft of distribution conductors, that large trees (mature height ≥40 ft) maintain 25 ft from distribution and 50 ft from transmission conductors, and that all clearances and species designations be verifiable on submitted plans. The following deficiencies prevent compliance verification:
- ECM Appendix F is not included in the plan set; no UC column cross-reference is provided for proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) on Sheets 31 or 35.
- Three mitigation trees (labeled "M") in the SE corner near the southern OHE line are not identified by species on Sheet 31, making individual UC and clearance determination impossible.
- No clearance dimensions are annotated on Sheet 31 from tree trunk centers to the OHE outside conductor; visual analysis confirms at least three tree canopy circles overlap or are directly tangent to the southern OHE line.
- Cedar Elm (10 proposed) and Live Oak (2 proposed) are large trees (mature height ≥40 ft per standard horticultural references), but plant schedule (Sheet 35) documents only container heights at planting, not ECM Appendix F mature heights, and does not identify which species are "large trees."
- The OHE line along the southern boundary is not classified as distribution or transmission on Sheet 21 or 31; if transmission (≥60 kV), large trees must maintain 50-ft clearance.
comments.sheets: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Landscape Calculations (Sheet 35); Tree List (Sheet 32); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line (SE corner mitigation trees); western site boundary along overhead electric line
comments.resolution:
Revise the plan set to address all of the following:
- Include ECM Appendix F (or an exhibit excerpting the UC column) and mark the UC designation for each proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) on Sheet 35.
- Add species labels on Sheet 31 for the three unlabeled mitigation trees in the SE corner near the southern OHE line.
- Annotate clearance dimensions on Sheet 31 from tree trunk centers to the outside OHE conductor for all trees within the applicable clearance zone (25 ft for large-tree/distribution; 50 ft for large-tree/transmission).
- Label the OHE line on Sheet 21 and Sheet 31 as distribution or transmission (with voltage class if known); if transmission, verify all large trees are ≥50 ft from conductor.
- Add ECM Appendix F mature height values to the plant schedule on Sheet 35 and identify each species that qualifies as a "large tree" (≥40 ft). Relocate or substitute any large trees that cannot meet the applicable setback.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs per constituent finding); reviewer should field-measure or scale clearances from OHE line to nearest tree symbols on Sheet 31 and confirm OHE voltage classification with Austin Energy.

perRunFindings.comment: Three mitigation trees shown on landscape plan less than 15 feet from overhead electric line lack species identification, preventing verification of utility-compatibility per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide species identification for all trees proposed near overhead electric facilities and verify utility-compatible (UC) designation from ECM Appendix F for non-UC tree species.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows three mitigation trees (marked 'M') positioned in the southeast corner with canopy edges less than 15 feet from the existing OHE (overhead electric) line running along the southern property boundary (per vision analysis). Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) provides the plant schedule identifying four tree species proposed: Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud. However, the landscape plan does not identify which species corresponds to the three trees shown near the OHE line. The plans show no clearance measurements or documentation of utility-compatibility verification.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The grouping requires that non-utility-compatible trees must be at least 15 feet from distribution conductors. The vision analysis clearly shows tree canopy symbols less than 15 feet from the OHE line. The plant schedule lists multiple proposed tree species, some of which (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud) are not identified in the grouping guidance as utility-compatible species. The critical issue is that the three specific trees shown near the OHE line on the landscape plan are not identified by species, making it impossible to determine their utility-compatibility status.

perRunFindings.comment: Three mitigation trees shown less than 15 feet from overhead electric line lack species identification and mature height confirmation, preventing verification of large-tree clearance requirement (minimum 25 feet from distribution conductors). Identify tree species and provide mature heights per ECM Appendix F for all trees proposed near overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line, southeast corner
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 shows three mitigation trees in the southeast corner with tree canopy edges positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line. Sheet 35 plant schedule lists proposed trees including 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana) and 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia), both of which typically have mature heights of 40 feet or greater. However, the landscape plan does not identify which species the three trees near the OHE line represent. The specification on Sheet 35 lists only container heights at planting (16' minimum for Live Oak and Cedar Elm containers), not mature heights.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) must be more than 25 feet from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. If the three trees positioned less than 15 feet from the OHE line are Live Oak or Cedar Elm (both likely 40+ ft mature height), they would violate this requirement. Without confirmed species identification and mature height designations from ECM Appendix F, a definitive determination cannot be made.

perRunFindings.comment: Plant schedule lists tree species proposed near overhead electric line, but does not document utility-compatible (UC) status per ECM Appendix F required by UCM § 1.10.10.4. Clearance distances from tree trunks to outside conductors are not dimensioned on landscape plan, preventing verification of compliance with 15-foot minimum distance for non-utility-compatible species near distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: western site boundary where overhead electric line is present
areas within 15 feet of overhead distribution conductor

Sheet 31 shows the OHE line and depicts trees positioned along the site boundary near this overhead line. Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule listing proposed tree species: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus Crassifolia), 2 Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana), 6 Mexican Redbud (Cercis Canadensis var. Mexicana), and 2 Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora Secundiflora). The plant schedule does not indicate the UC status of any species per ECM Appendix F, and no clearance dimensions are provided on the landscape plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only utility-compatible trees (marked UC in ECM Appendix F) be proposed within 15 feet of distribution conductors. The voltage classification of the OHE line (distribution vs. transmission) is not documented; the plant schedule provides species names but does not reference ECM Appendix F or identify UC status; no clearance dimensions are shown.

perRunFindings.comment: Large trees (Live Oak and Cedar Elm) with typical mature heights of 40-50 feet are shown on landscape plan and tree survey adjacent to overhead distribution conductors. Plans do not document mature heights to identify large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F), and no clearance dimensions are provided to verify compliance with 25-foot minimum setback from distribution conductor.

areas within 25 feet of overhead distribution conductor
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 (landscape plan) shows overhead electric lines (OHE) running along site boundaries with utility poles, and trees positioned along these boundaries. Sheet 32 (tree inventory) documents surveyed trees on site including large native species: Live Oak specimens with DBH of 32 inches (Tree 4018), 36 inches (Tree 4026), 27 inches (Tree 4027), and 24 inches (Tree 4038), all marked as Appendix F species; Cedar Elm 17 inches DBH (Tree 4010); Pecan 24 inches DBH (Tree 4015). Sheet 35 specifies proposed planting of 10 Cedar Elm and 2 Live Oak. The landscape plan shows multiple tree symbols positioned directly adjacent to or overlapping the OHE line along the southern boundary (per vision analysis: '3+ trees positioned directly underneath or extremely close to the OHE line'). The landscape plan provides NO clearance dimensions from tree trunks to the outside conductor, and the plant schedule does NOT specify mature heights.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that large trees (mature height 40 feet or greater per ECM Appendix F) be positioned at least 25 feet from the outside conductor of overhead distribution facilities. The site has documented large native trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm) and proposed plantings of the same large species positioned adjacent to or overlapping the OHE line, with no clearance dimensions to verify the 25-foot minimum.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed tree species appear to be Utility Compatible, but clearance verification is incomplete due to unclear distribution vs. transmission designation and lack of dimensioned clearances from proposed trees to overhead electric line.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line '- OHE -' along southern boundary. Proposed species are all Utility Compatible (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud). Landscape Plan does not indicate whether line is distribution or transmission or dimension clearance distances from proposed trees.
perRunFindings.reasoning: All proposed species are UC-designated, which satisfies this requirement if within clearance zones. However, line voltage classification and clearance distances not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.

perRunFindings.observation: Proposed 2 Live Oaks and 10 Cedar Elms appear to qualify as 'large trees' (mature height >= 40 feet). Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line but does not dimension distances from proposed large trees to this line. Landscape Plan does not explicitly identify which trees are large trees or their proximity to OHE line.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Large trees within 25 feet of distribution line prohibited, but clearance distances not dimensioned on Landscape Plan. Cannot verify compliance without distance specifications.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed tree species are Utility Compatible, which would satisfy transmission clearance requirements if overhead electric line is transmission (>= 60kV). However, overhead line voltage classification and clearance distances are not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.
perRunFindings.observation: All proposed species are Utility Compatible (UC). Overhead electric line shown on Sheet 31 but line voltage classification (distribution vs. transmission) not clearly indicated. Distance to proposed trees not dimensioned.
perRunFindings.reasoning: All UC species would satisfy requirement even if line were transmission. However, line voltage and clearance distances not clearly specified on Landscape Plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed large trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm - mature height >= 40 feet) may be planted within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric line. Transmission facility classification and clearance distances are not clearly indicated on Landscape Plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Two Live Oaks and 10 Cedar Elms qualify as 'large trees' (mature height >= 40 feet). Landscape Plan shows overhead electric line but does not dimension clearances or identify which trees are large. Line voltage classification not specified.

perRunFindings.comment: Trees proposed near overhead electric line (southern boundary) have not been verified as utility-compatible species against ECM Appendix F. Verify all species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) in ECM Appendix F UC column and provide documentation. For any non-UC species within 15 feet of OHE, provide written Austin Energy approval.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line runs and trees are proposed within 15 lateral feet
perRunFindings.observation: Vision analysis of landscape plan Sheet 31 identified multiple trees (marked 'M' for mitigation trees) positioned along the southern property boundary. The sheet clearly shows the OHE (Overhead Electric) line labeled running the entire length of the southern boundary. Several proposed tree canopy circles visually overlap or are immediately tangent to the OHE line, with at least three 'M' trees having canopy circles crossing directly over the OHE line and utility pole symbols. ECM Appendix F (the definitive reference for Utility-Compatible species identification) is not provided in the site plan documentation. No Austin Energy approval letter, coordination note, or design stamp indicating approval for non-UC species placement is visible on the landscape plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that only utility-compatible (UC) trees be planted within 15 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment. UC status is definitive — only species with 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F qualify. Because Appendix F is not provided in the site plan, UC status cannot be determined from available evidence. The trees are positioned directly under the OHE line (southern boundary), which is within the 15-foot zone. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak both with mature heights ≥40 feet) are proposed along the southern property boundary within the overhead electric line corridor. These species must be maintained at least 25 lateral feet from the OHE line per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Revise landscape plan to show either: (1) relocation of large trees to maintain 25-foot clearance from OHE line, or (2) substitution with smaller species (mature height <40 feet).
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric distribution line runs
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) specifies proposed shade trees: 10 Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia) and 2 Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), both specified as 100 GAL. container grown with 4' caliper and 16' height minimum. Cedar Elm and Live Oak have mature heights in the range of 40-50 feet or greater, placing both species in the 'large tree' category (≥40 feet mature height). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows mitigation trees (M) positioned along the southern boundary where the OHE line is located. Vision analysis confirms at least three trees with canopy circles overlapping or directly tangent to the OHE line. No ECM Appendix F reference is provided in the site plan to definitively confirm mature height specifications.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states: 'Large trees (mature height ≥40 feet) may not be planted within 25 lateral feet of overhead electric distribution conductor or equipment.' The proposed large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak) are positioned directly along the OHE line at the southern boundary, well within 25 feet. The landscape plan does not show distance annotations or clearance verification.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed tree species cannot be verified as utility-compatible without ECM Appendix F. Provide either: (1) a copy of ECM Appendix F with UC column marked for all proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud), or (2) a letter from City forester confirming UC status of each species. Species shown near overhead electric facilities (southern boundary) must be verified as having 'x' in the UC column of ECM Appendix F per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: All areas where proposed trees are within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution or 50 feet of overhead transmission
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 35 lists proposed tree species: Live Oak (Quercus virginiana), Cedar Elm (Ulmus crassifolia), Texas Mountain Laurel (Sophora secundiflora), and Mexican Redbud (Cercis canadensis var. mexicana). Both common names and scientific names are provided, which allows cross-reference against ECM Appendix F. However, the site plan documentation does NOT include ECM Appendix F itself.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The applicant must provide proof that species used near electric facilities comply with the UC requirement. Proof consists of either (a) ECM Appendix F included in the site plan documentation with UC column marked for each species, or (b) a reference letter from the City's urban forester or landscape code reviewer confirming UC status. The site plan provides species names but not the definitive Appendix F verification.

comments.title: Trees Near Transformer Pads — UC Species Verification Incomplete
comments.comment: Trees near pad-mounted transformer locations are identified only by functional category (M, PL, SY) on the Tree List, with no species names or ECM Appendix F cross-reference, and the Landscape Plan provides no distance dimensions from tree symbols to transformer pads.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.4 and ECM Appendix F require that trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted transformer equipment be utility-compatible (UC) species. Sheet 32 (Tree List) categorizes trees by function (M=Mitigation, PL=Parking Lot, SY=Street Yard) but does not list species names, making UC verification impossible. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree symbols throughout the site, including in proximity to the three transformer pads shown on Sheet 21, but provides no dimensioned distances from tree trunk locations to pad edges. Neither species-to-pad distance nor UC status is documented.
comments.sheets: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Tree List (Sheet 32); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Areas within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted transformer equipment throughout site interior
comments.resolution: Add species names (common and scientific) to each entry on Sheet 32 (Tree List) and provide an exhibit or table on Sheet 31 or 32 that: (1) identifies each tree within 10 lateral feet of a transformer pad by species, (2) cross-references each species against ECM Appendix F UC designation, and (3) annotates dimensioned distances from each such tree trunk to the nearest transformer pad edge.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs per finding); reviewer should overlay Sheet 21 transformer pad locations against Sheet 31 tree symbols to identify which trees fall within 10 ft.

perRunFindings.comment: Landscape plan shows trees throughout the site but lacks dimensioned distances to transformer pads and species cross-reference to ECM Appendix F utility compatibility column. Sheet 32 (Tree List) is referenced but not examined in detail. Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads positioned within the development interior. However, the landscape plan does not include dimensioned measurements documenting distances between the proposed trees and transformer pad locations, and no cross-reference is provided between the landscape plant list and ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) column.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The landscape plan identifies tree locations and provides symbols indicating tree types and mitigation counts, but does not measure distances to transformer pad locations or confirm species utility compatibility. perRunFindings.comment: Tree species planted or retained within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads are not identified by scientific/common name on the landscape or tree list sheets. Provide a cross-referenced list showing each tree's species and confirmation of utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for all trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment.

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 32 (Tree List) provides tree inventory with functional categories (M=Mitigation, PL=Parking Lot, SY=Street Yard) but does NOT list specific tree species names. Without species identification, utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) column cannot be verified. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols distributed across the site but does not cross-reference species against ECM Appendix F. Trees are present in the vicinity of transformer pads and electrical easements, but species-specific verification of utility compatibility is not documented on the plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 and ECM Appendix F require verification that trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment are utility-compatible species. The plans identify trees only by functional category (M, PL, SY), not by species name. This is particularly important because the plans do not document whether trees identified as 'M' (mitigation trees) planted specifically for the development are utility-compatible, or whether existing trees within 10 feet of pads meet the requirement.

comments.title: Landscape Plan Not Coordinated with Underground Electric Infrastructure
comments.comment: The Landscape Plan does not depict underground electric duct bank or conduit routing, and the Landscape Details sheet omits tree well details, preventing verification that proposed trees and tree wells are not placed on top of underground electric utilities.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees from being planted on top of underground electric duct banks and requires coordination of tree well placement with utility infrastructure. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines ('- E -') routed throughout the site with tree canopy symbols overlapping in multiple locations, but Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not depict underground duct banks or conduits, making it impossible to correlate proposed tree planting locations with underground utility routing. comments.title: Dimensioned Clearance Exhibits Missing for Electric Easement Boundaries
comments.comment: Plans show electric easement locations but provide no dimensioned clearances between easement boundaries and proposed structures, driveways, or parking areas.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.16.0 require clearance verification exhibits with explicit dimensions from recorded electric easement boundaries to all nearby improvements. The site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) depict buildings, driveways, and parking areas in proximity to recorded easements (5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76; 5' P.U.E.) but provide only property-line dimensions (e.g., Bldg 4 at 27.3' from east property line), not easement-boundary dimensions. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) similarly shows transformer pad locations and underground lines without clearance callouts. Additionally, two easements not depicted on the site plan — a Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 ac., NE interior) and a City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 ac., NE corner) — create further gaps in clearance verification. Without dimensioned clearance exhibits, compliance with minimum required clearances cannot be confirmed.
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Grading plan (Sheet 11); Electrical design plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All structures and improvements within 15 feet of electric easement boundaries; site perimeter along eastern and southern property boundaries where 5' electric easements are recorded; northeast corner where Greenbelt Access & Use Easement and City of Austin Drainage Easement are undepicted
comments.resolution: Provide a clearance verification exhibit — on the site plan or a dedicated sheet — showing dimensioned separations from all recorded electric easement boundaries to every proposed structure, driveway, parking area, and site improvement within 15 feet. For overhead distribution facilities confirm minimum 15-foot radius clearance; for underground facilities confirm minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance per UCM § 1.10.5. Additionally, depict and dimension clearances for the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement and City of Austin Drainage Easement in the northeast area of the site.

comments.title: 24/7 Vehicular Access to Electric Facilities Not Shown or Dimensioned
comments.comment: No formal 24/7 vehicular access routes are designated or dimensioned from the public right-of-way to electric easements and transformer pads.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.3.16 requires permanent, unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access from public ROW to all electric facilities for installation, operation, and maintenance. The following deficiencies are present:
- No access routes labeled or dimensioned from Valley View Road to any transformer pad or electric easement on Sheets 9, 11, or 21; access is assumed via adjacent internal driveways
- A continuous concrete retaining wall along the north, east, and south perimeter physically separates easement areas from public ROW, requiring routing through private internal drives and bypassing residential buildings
- Transformer pad detail on Sheet 21 contains a note reading "need to look up approp. detail," indicating the design is incomplete
- Existing retaining wall (to be replaced) and wood fence along the eastern boundary may obstruct access to the eastern easement areas
- No gates, removable fencing sections, or AE-keyed lock provisions are noted for off-hours access on any sheet
- Sheet 3 general notes state that 24-hour access shall be maintained, but no plan shows how this requirement is satisfied
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Electrical design plan (Sheet 21); Grading plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: All electric easements and transformer pad locations on site; electric easements along east and south property boundaries; Valley View Road frontage
comments.resolution: Show and dimension explicit vehicular access routes from Valley View Road (public ROW) to all transformer pads and electric easement areas, meeting minimum 12-foot horizontal width and 16-foot vertical clearance on an all-weather surface (HMAC or PCC). For eastern and southern easement areas separated from public ROW by the perimeter retaining wall, demonstrate how Austin Energy maintenance vehicles gain access. Note all 24/7 access provisions including any gate or lock arrangements providing AE personnel access at any hour. Complete the incomplete transformer pad detail on Sheet 21.

- Multiple tree symbols (Mitigation trees, Parking Lot trees, and Buffer Point trees per Sheet 31 legend) are drawn directly on or overlapping the dashed southern and eastern 5' easement boundaries on Sheets 9 and 31
- A concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is located within the 5' electric easement along the eastern boundary; Sheet 16 shows the retaining wall top elevation at 681.00
