Remove or relocate the concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond from within the 5' electric easement along the eastern boundary, or obtain documented written Austin Energy approval for this encroachment.

perRunFindings.comment: Multiple trees and vegetation (site amenities) are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the electric easement boundaries to comply with UCM § 1.10.10.2.

Easement" without the "aerial" designation. UCM § 1.16.0 requires construction details and profile plan drawings of fences and existing utility facilities when fencing is proposed near AE facilities, to be submitted for AE Design review and preliminary approval. comments.title: Underground Electric Line Crosses Southern Property Boundary Without Documented Easement
comments.comment: An underground electric line shown on Sheet 21 extends from a pull box south of Building 7 across the property boundary onto the adjacent southern property without a documented easement or unified development designation.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.8 and Code § 15-9-123(B) permit electrical facilities to cross property lines only when: (1) easements are obtained from the adjacent property owner, or (2) properties qualify as a unified development per Austin Energy's criteria (physical adjacency, common ownership, unified operation, and AE determination). Sheet 21 shows a blue underground electric line extending southward from the pull box south of Building 7, explicitly crossing the heavy dashed main property line into the adjacent southern property toward an off-site electric easement. No easement instrument referencing the southern adjacent property is labeled or recorded on the plans, and no unified development designation is documented. The Master Comment Report references UCM § 1.3.8 as under review but no resolution is evident in the submitted materials.
comments.sheets: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Southern property boundary; cross-property underground electric line from pull box south of Building 7 onto adjacent southern property
comments.resolution: Either (1) provide documentation of an executed easement from the adjacent southern property owner for the underground electric line crossing, recorded and referenced on Sheet 21; or (2) provide written confirmation from Austin Energy that the subject lot and the adjacent southern property qualify as a unified development under UCM § 1.3.8 criteria.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify on Sheet 21 that the underground line south of Building 7 crosses the property boundary and confirm that no easement documentation was submitted with the application.

comments.title: Transmission Easement Landscaping Non-Compliant and Not Approved by AE Transmission Reviewer
comments.comment: The landscape plan proposes trees and shrubs within and immediately adjacent to transmission easements without overlaying easement boundaries on Sheet 31, and no Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval is documented.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.10.4, § 1.14.0, and § 1.14.6 require: (1) transmission easement boundaries shown on landscape plans for compliance verification; (2) no trees within transmission easements or within 25 feet of any transmission structure base; (3) shrubbery must not obstruct walking or vehicle access to transmission structure bases; and (4) AE transmission reviewer approval of the landscape plan. Sheet 31 shows multiple tree planting symbols (coded SY, PL, P, and M) directly on or overlapping easement boundary lines along the north, east, and south property lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 explicitly states "No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement" and "No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure," but compliance cannot be verified because transmission easement boundaries are not overlaid on Sheet 31. comments.title: Transformer Pad Locations and Clearance Zones Missing from Landscape Plan
comments.comment: The landscape plan omits all 5 transformer pad locations shown on the electrical design plan, making it impossible to verify that proposed trees, shrubs, and access corridors comply with Austin Energy minimum clearance requirements.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees and shrubs from being planted within specified clearance zones around pad-mounted electric equipment, and requires that landscape plans show transformer routing to enable verification. None of the following clearance requirements can be confirmed because transformer pads are not depicted on Sheet 31:
- No trees within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted equipment (5 transformer pads identified on Sheet 21 near Bldg. 1 entrance, Bldg. 2, Bldg. 4/5 courtyard, Bldg. 6/7 courtyard, and Bldg. 8)
- No shrubs within 10 lateral feet of the access door (hot-stick-use/pad-locked) side of each transformer pad
- No shrubs within 5 lateral feet of the non-access sides of each transformer pad
- No trees positioned between any transformer access door and the nearest drivable surface (street, alley, or parking area) required for bucket truck access
- Dimension callouts confirming measured clearances at all pad locations are absent
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Landscape Calculations (Sheet 35)
comments.applicableArea: All 5 transformer pad locations throughout site: adjacent to Bldg. 1 near entrance, adjacent to Bldg. 2, courtyard between Bldgs. 4 and 5, courtyard between Bldgs. 6 and 7, and adjacent to Bldg. 8; all proposed trees and shrubs (Dwarf Palmetto, Big Muhly, Gulf Muhly, Texas Sage, Dwarf Wax Myrtle per Sheet 35) in proximity to those pads
comments.resolution:
Overlay all 5 transformer pad locations and underground electric routing from Sheet 21 onto the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and annotate the following for each pad:
- 10-foot lateral clearance zone around all sides of the pad, with confirmation that no trees fall within this zone
- Access door side labeled with a 10-foot shrub-free zone; non-access sides labeled with a 5-foot shrub-free zone
- Tree-free corridor shown from each transformer access door to the nearest drivable surface (street, alley, or parking area)
- Dimension callouts at each pad confirming measured clearances meet the requirements above
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy — transformer pad locations, access door orientations, and underground routing from Sheet 21 must be confirmed with the electrical engineer before overlay onto the landscape plan.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Several runs returned 'unclear' rather than 'fail' because transformer locations are not shown on Sheet 31; reviewer should confirm pad locations from Sheet 21 match proposed landscape context before approving the overlay.

comments.title: Root Barrier Construction Details Absent from Landscape Plans
comments.comment: No root barrier details or specifications appear anywhere in the landscape documentation for trees proposed within 5–20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers for all trees planted within 5–20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, with minimum installation depth of 4 feet and positioning exactly 5 feet from the equipment edge. The following deficiencies are present:
- Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) contains standard tree planting and protection details (Standard 610S-4 tree protection, tree planting pit, shrub planting) but no root barrier construction detail with depth or placement specifications
- Sheet 31 contains no callouts, notes, or detail references identifying trees that require root barriers
- Sheet 21 shows multiple transformer pads and 8+ pull boxes (underground electric equipment) with significant overlap with existing tree canopy zones; the proposed planting of 20 trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) and shrubs per Sheet 35 is not assessed against these locations
- Mitigation trees ('M' designation) on Sheet 32, including those near electrical easements, have no root barrier documentation
- Without root barrier specifications on plan documents, there is no standard for contractors to follow during construction
comments.sheets: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Landscape Details (Sheet 37); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Calculations (Sheet 35); Tree List (Sheet 32)
comments.applicableArea: All proposed and existing trees within 5–20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment (transformer pads and pull boxes) throughout site; 20 proposed trees including Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel; mitigation trees ('M' designation) near electrical easements per Sheet 32
comments.resolution: Add a root barrier construction detail to Sheet 37 that includes: minimum 4-foot installation depth, positioning exactly 5 feet from underground equipment edge, barrier material specification, and a cross-section view. On Sheet 31, once transformer pad locations and underground routing from Sheet 21 are overlaid (per companion comment), add callouts identifying all trees within the 5–20 foot zone of underground equipment and reference the new root barrier detail for each.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: The specific trees requiring root barriers cannot be confirmed until transformer pad locations are overlaid on Sheet 31 (see companion comment on transformer clearances); this comment should be re-evaluated after that coordination is complete.

comments.title: Electric Easement Labels Incomplete — Nomenclature, Type, and Recording
comments.comment: Electric easement labels throughout the plan set use abbreviated forms, omit required aerial/underground type designation, and carry inconsistent or missing recording information across sheets.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0 and § 1.16.0(1)(i) require complete proper nomenclature, aerial/underground designation, and recording references on all electric easement labels. Three compounding deficiencies are present across Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 21:
- **Abbreviated nomenclature**: Labels read "Elec. Easement," "Elec. & Tele. Easement," "P.U.E.," and "Esm't." rather than the required complete form (e.g., "Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement").
- **No aerial/underground designation**: No label specifies whether the easement serves aerial facilities (overhead poles, conductors, guy wires) or underground facilities (conduit, pad-mounted equipment), despite both types being present on-site per Sheet 21 (OHE and underground conduit shown).
- **Missing/inconsistent recording information**: Sheet 2 (Plat) easement labels carry no volume/page citations; volume/page references differ between sheets (Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 on Sheet 21 vs. Pg. 883 on Sheet 9), preventing verification against recorded documents.

comments.applicableArea: All electric easement labels along property boundaries on Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 21, including: 5' Elec. Ease. (north boundary of Lot 2); 5' Elec. Ease. (south boundary of Lot 1); 5' Electric Easement Vol. 69/73; 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468; 5' P.U.E.
comments.resolution: Revise all easement labels on Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 21 to: (1) use complete proper nomenclature (e.g., "5' Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement"); (2) add "Aerial" or "Underground" designation to each easement per the facility type it serves (reference UCM §§ 1.10.3–1.10.4 for applicable clearance requirements); and (3) include consistent volume/page or instrument number citations matching recorded documents across all sheets (e.g., "Vol. 73, Pg. 76, Case C8S-75-160" and "Vol. 5468, Pg. 385, D.R.T.C.Tx.").

comments.title: Transmission Facility Presence Unresolved — Cascading Documentation Deficiencies
comments.comment: Sheet 3 contains 16 detailed Electric Transmission Notes (Block 20) but no transmission structures, transmission easements, or 60kV+ infrastructure are depicted on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), or Site Plan (Sheet 9), creating an unresolved ambiguity that triggers multiple mandatory corrections.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(8) and § 1.14.0 require that transmission notes and documentation appear on specific sheets when transmission facilities (60kV+) are present; these notes must be removed when no such facilities exist. The contradiction between comprehensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 and their complete absence from working plan sheets produces the following deficiencies:
- **Transmission notes not propagated to required sheets**: The 16-item Block 20 transmission notes on Sheet 3 do not appear on Grading Plan (Sheet 11) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) as required by UCM § 1.16.0(8); contractors reviewing those sheets have no awareness of 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction safety meetings, or barricading requirements.
- **Transmission easement boundary absent from all working plans**: The transmission easement boundary, dimensions, coordinates, and 25-foot clearance zones are not depicted on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Grading Plan (Sheet 11), or Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) as required by UCM § 1.14.0; all existing electric easements shown on these sheets are only 5–10 feet wide.
- **No 25-foot all-weather access corridor shown or dimensioned**: UCM § 1.14.4.A requires a minimum 25-foot-wide all-weather vehicle access route with 16-foot minimum vertical clearance to transmission easements; no such corridor is labeled or dimensioned on any plan sheet.
- **No pavement design for tandem axle loads**: Sheet 3 notes and UCM § 1.14.4 require pavement within the transmission easement to support 48,000 lb tandem axle loads (5-foot spacing); no engineering calculations, pavement design, or certification is provided on Sheets 9, 11, 22, 23, or 24.
- **No building elevations showing transmission lines**: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations showing transmission line locations and clearances when transmission facilities are present; none are provided.
- **No CAD overlay of building footprints on transmission easement**: UCM § 1.14.0 requires a CAD plan view showing all building footprints overlaid on the transmission easement boundary with clearance dimensions; no transmission easement boundary is depicted on Sheets 9 or 21.
comments.sheets: Cover Sheet (Sheet 1); General Notes (Sheet 3); Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Construction Details (Sheets 22–24); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site if transmission facilities (60kV+) are present on or adjacent to the property; pavement and structures within 5-foot easement areas along north and south property boundaries; all building footprints relative to any transmission easement
comments.resolution: Applicant must first confirm whether transmission facilities (60kV+ voltage, large structures) are present on or immediately adjacent to the site. If NO transmission facilities exist: remove Block 20 Electric Transmission Notes from Sheet 3 and document the absence of transmission infrastructure on Sheet 4. If transmission facilities DO exist: (1) add all transmission notes to Sheets 11 and 31; (2) depict the transmission easement boundary with dimensions, coordinates, and 25-foot clearance zones on Sheets 9, 11, and 21; (3) show and dimension the 25-foot all-weather access corridor with 16-foot vertical clearance, including gate, grade, curb, and drainage specifications; (4) provide pavement design sealed by a registered engineer demonstrating 48,000 lb tandem axle (5-foot spacing) capacity for all pavement within the easement; (5) provide building elevations showing proposed structures in relation to transmission lines; and (6) provide a CAD overlay showing all building footprints dimensioned to the transmission easement boundary.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Core transmission ambiguity (EL-12.44) is high confidence (3/3 runs); the six cascading sub-items (access corridor, pavement design, CAD overlay, building elevations, easement depiction, sheet propagation) are each low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm transmission facility presence before requiring all corrective actions.

comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(3) and Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) require new electric easements to be dedicated by separate instrument with surveyor-sealed metes and bounds descriptions when no new plat is filed. Three related deficiencies are present:
- **Existing easement dimensions not shown on electrical plan**: Sheet 21 shows proposed underground infrastructure but does not depict the boundary dimensions of existing 5' electric easements from the 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) in relation to proposed improvements, preventing verification of whether new facilities fit within recorded easements.
- **Transformer vault easements not formally depicted**: Three transformer pads on Sheet 21 carry a 'Vault Easement' leader-line label but no formal boundary dimensions, area callouts, metes and bounds, or recording references are provided; vault easements are entirely absent from Sheet 11 (Grading Plan).
- **No surveyor-sealed field notes for new easement dedications**: Proposed underground electrical lines route extensively through the site interior — well beyond the historic 5' perimeter easements — requiring new easement areas dedicated by separate instrument; no surveyor-executed, signed, and sealed field notes or metes and bounds descriptions are included in the submittal. comments.title: Transformer Pad Proximity Clearances Not Dimensioned on Plans
comments.comment: The electrical plan shows all three transformer pads positioned near buildings, sidewalks, and one another, but no dimensional annotations document compliance with the UCM-required minimum proximity clearances.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires documented minimum clearances for pad-mounted transformers. The following are missing from the submitted plans:
- **5-ft clearance to buildings:** Pads 1 and 2 (west side near Buildings 2 and 8) lack dimensions from pad edges to building foundations and exterior walls
- **2-ft clearance to back of sidewalk:** Pads 1 and 2 (near sidewalk easements on western boundary) lack dimensions from pad edges to back of sidewalk
- **10-ft clearance on access door side (15-ft if confined space):** No pad shows access door orientation on any plan sheet; without this, the applicable use-area clearance (10 ft to open area; 15 ft if access door faces an area enclosed on 3+ sides) cannot be verified — Pad 3 is surrounded by Buildings 4, 5, and 6, raising the possibility of the 15-ft confined-space standard
- **5-ft clearance between transformer pads:** Edge-to-edge or center-to-center distances between all three pads are not dimensioned
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer Pad 1 (west side near Building 2 and sidewalk easement); Transformer Pad 2 (west side near Building 8 and sidewalk easement); Transformer Pad 3 (central courtyard between Buildings 4, 5, and 6); all three transformer pad locations
comments.resolution:
Revise Sheet 21 to add dimension callouts addressing each of the following:
- Clearance from Pad 1 and Pad 2 edges to exterior walls/foundations of Buildings 2 and 8 (minimum 5 ft)
- Clearance from back of sidewalk to Pad 1 and Pad 2 edges (minimum 2 ft)
- Access door orientation symbol on all three pads, with annotated clear zone on the access door side (minimum 10 ft to open area; minimum 15 ft if the access door faces an area enclosed on 3 or more sides — provide cross-section for Pad 3 to document whether confined-space standard applies)
- Edge-to-edge or center-to-center distances between all three transformer pads (minimum 5 ft)

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads shown on electrical design plan lack documented clearance measurements to adjacent buildings. Provide dimensioned drawings or calculations demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance from edge of transformer pad to building foundations and exterior walls.

Transformer Pad 2 west side near Building 8
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads as dotted rectangles. Pads 1 and 2 are positioned on the west side of the site near Buildings 2 and 8 respectively, in proximity to the property line and sidewalk easement areas. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout but does not include dimensional clearance measurements between the transformer pads and building facades. Vision analysis confirms Pad 1 is positioned between Building 2 and the western property boundary (sidewalk area), and Pad 2 is positioned similarly near Building 8. However, no numerical measurements (e.g., "5 feet minimum") are provided on any submitted plan sheets to document actual clearances from building foundations or structures.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires a minimum 5-foot clearance from pad-mounted equipment to buildings, structures, and building foundations. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating compliance through documented measurements or calculations on the plans. While the plans show transformer pad locations and building positions, the absence of explicit clearance measurements between the pad edges and building walls prevents verification of compliance. This constitutes failure to document the required clearances, not merely unclear positioning. However, since the pads are shown at some distance from the buildings (not touching), the deficiency cannot be definitively proven as a pass or fail without actual measurements. This requires clarification through submission of dimensional drawings showing clearances.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pads 1 and 2 shown near sidewalk easements on electrical plan lack documented clearance measurements. Provide dimensioned drawings demonstrating minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to edge of transformer pad.

Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms sidewalk easement marking near both western pads. However, no explicit measurements are provided documenting the distance from the back of the sidewalk to the transformer pad edges.

Sidewalk easements are clearly depicted on the electrical plan in proximity to Pads 1 and 2, but without dimensional documentation (measurements in feet) on the plans, the actual clearance cannot be verified. The pads appear to be positioned nearby the sidewalk area, but confirmation of the specific 2-foot minimum requires dimensioned drawings.

Provide documentation showing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door and demonstrating minimum 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent structure.
perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads as dotted rectangles but provides no indication of access door orientation or hot-stick use area boundaries. Site plan (Sheet 9) does not include transformer pad detail orientation information. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms that pad access door orientation is not visible/marked on the submitted plans for any of the three pads.

Without knowing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door, it is impossible to verify whether the required 10-foot clearance exists in the appropriate direction. The plans must indicate access door orientation and the associated 10-foot use area to demonstrate compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 located between multiple buildings in central courtyard area. Provide documentation clarifying whether the pad access door faces a confined space (3+ sides enclosed). If confined space applies, provide dimensioned drawings or cross-sections demonstrating minimum 15-foot clearance from access door.

perRunFindings.observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows Transformer Pad 3 positioned centrally within the site, surrounded by Buildings 4 (north), 5 (east), and 6 (south) within a parking/circulation area. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows these buildings in close proximity to each other. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes that the central pad is "located within an open paved/drive area surrounded by three aforementioned buildings." No cross-section drawings are provided showing whether the pad access door faces any of these surrounding buildings or is within a confined space (niche, vault, or enclosed area on 3+ sides).

Transformer Pad 3's location between three buildings suggests it may face a confined space orientation on one or more sides. However, without access door orientation documentation and no cross-section drawings demonstrating the configuration, it cannot be determined whether the 15-foot confined space threshold applies or whether the applicable clearance requirement has been met.

comments.title: Overhead Conductor Clearances From Transformer Pads Not Documented
comments.comment: Plans show transformer pads near existing overhead electric lines but provide no section views or dimensional annotations documenting the required vertical and horizontal clearances from overhead distribution conductors.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 establishes minimum clearances from overhead distribution conductors to pad-mounted transformer equipment. Sheet 21 shows overhead electric lines (-OHE-) along the southern and western property boundaries, and Sheet 3 general notes reference electric transmission clearance requirements. The following are absent from the submitted plans:
- **7.5-ft vertical clearance:** No section views or elevation drawings show the relationship between surveyed overhead conductor elevation and the top of transformer equipment; vertical clearance from the lowest conductor to the highest point of any transformer cannot be verified
- **7.5-ft horizontal sky-to-ground clearance:** No dimension callouts on Sheet 21 document the horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from each transformer pad to the overhead distribution primary, neutral, and secondary conductor envelope
- **15-ft radial clearance from primary/neutral conductors:** No dimension callouts document the radial clearance from each transformer pad to the nearest primary and neutral conductor centerline (measured from conductor centerline, not pole centerline)
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pad locations relative to overhead electric lines (-OHE-) on southern and western property boundaries
comments.resolution:
On Sheet 21 and/or supplemental electrical detail sheets, provide the following:
- Cross-section drawing(s) showing surveyed overhead conductor elevation(s) and transformer pad height with annotation verifying minimum 7.5-ft vertical clearance from the lowest conductor to the top of transformer equipment
- Dimension callouts on the plan view verifying minimum 7.5-ft horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from each transformer pad edge to the overhead conductor envelope
- Dimension callouts verifying minimum 15-ft radial clearance from each transformer pad to the nearest primary and neutral conductor centerline (measured from conductor centerline, not pole); if any transformer pad is within the 15-ft radius, provide relocation notes or AE Design written approval
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs per sub-item) — reviewer should confirm which transformer pads fall within the overhead line clearance zones shown on Sheet 21 and whether section views have been submitted elsewhere.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide section views of proposed transformer pads showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum 7.5-foot vertical clearance from the lowest point of overhead conductors to the highest point of transformer equipment. If transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines, provide specific clearance verification or relocation notes.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple transformer pad locations throughout the site (labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' at several locations). However, the electrical plan is a plan view showing horizontal placement only. NO section views or elevation drawings accompany the electrical plan showing the vertical relationship between transformer pad height and the surveyed elevation of overhead electric conductors above the site. No vertical clearance dimension annotations are present. Overhead electric lines are shown on the plan as existing 'OHE' lines on the western and southern boundaries, but no section showing the clearance from these conductors to the tops of transformer pads is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformers (whether pole-mounted or pad-mounted) to maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a vertical clearance requirement, requiring knowledge of both the transformer height and the conductor height. The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but does not provide the surveyed conductor elevation or section views demonstrating that the 7.5-foot clearance is maintained. This is particularly important if any transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines or where overhead conductors pass over transformer equipment.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts and/or cross-section drawings on the electrical plan showing the clearance from each transformer pad to the nearest overhead distribution line conductor, verifying the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) designated on the southern property boundary. The general notes (Sheet 3) reference electric transmission clearance requirements, specifying '25 feet of transmission structures; 20-foot clearance for aerial equipment/staging.' However, no dimension callouts or cross-section drawings are provided on Sheet 21 to document the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pad locations to the overhead conductors. The plans do not indicate whether transformer pads are located within the clearance zone of the overhead lines.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution primary, neutral, and secondary conductors extending from ground to sky. Without dimensional annotation or cross-section drawings showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this clearance envelope, compliance cannot be verified. The presence of overhead lines on the property adjacent to transformer locations requires explicit clearance documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Minimum 15-foot radius clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan showing the radial distance (measured from conductor centerline, not pole) from each transformer pad to the nearest primary and neutral conductor, verifying the minimum 15-foot radius clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. The code requires minimum 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured from the conductor centerline (not pole centerline). No dimension callouts are provided on the electrical plan to document the 15-foot radius clearance from transformers to the primary/neutral conductors. The distance from transformer pads to the overhead line location is not dimensionally verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes a 15-foot radius clearance requirement from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. This is a radial clearance measured from the conductor itself, not from the pole. Without specific dimension callouts showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this 15-foot radius from the conductor location, compliance cannot be confirmed. The overhead line is present on the property adjacent to transformer locations, requiring explicit clearance documentation.

comments.title: Transformer Pad Positions Not Verified Against Recorded Easements
comments.comment: Transformer Pads 1, 2, and 3 are shown near sidewalk and vault easement callouts on the electrical plan, but the spatial relationship between pad boundaries and recorded easement boundaries has not been dimensionally documented.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 prohibits placement of transformer pads within drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements under overhead lines without written Austin Energy Design approval. Sheet 21 shows Pad 1 near a 'Sidewalk Easement' callout, Pad 2 near a 'Vault Easement' callout, and Pad 3 (southwest location) immediately adjacent to a 'Vault Easement' callout. No plan sheet documents whether any pad is within or outside the boundary of these or other recorded easements. Additionally, facts.md identifies multiple plat-dedicated easements — including a 7.5' Public Utility Easement and two 5' electric easements from Case C8S-75-160 — whose precise boundaries relative to transformer pad locations have not been confirmed on any submitted plan sheet.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Plat (Sheet 2); Site Plan (Sheet 9)

For the plat-dedicated 7.5' PUE and 5' electric easements (Case C8S-75-160), confirm in writing whether these qualify as 'electrical easements' under UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4.

comments.title: Building Elevations and Profile Drawings Lack Overhead Clearance Dimensions
comments.comment: The plan set contains no building elevation sheets or profile/cross-section drawings with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension callouts from the outside conductor to proposed buildings and building projections.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 and AEDC § 1.10.3 require building elevation sheets and profile/cross-section drawings with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimensioned clearances from the outside (outermost) conductor — not pole centerline — to all building faces and projections. No building elevation sheets appear anywhere in the 39-sheet plan set. The following are missing:
- Building elevation sheets showing surveyed elevations of overhead conductors overlaid on proposed building profiles
- Horizontal clearance dimension callouts from the outside conductor to all building faces on site plan and elevation sheets — minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance for Buildings 1–8
- Section and plan view exhibits (e.g., Section A-A, B-B) with dimension lines originating at the outer conductor and extending to the outermost edges of all buildings and site features
- Profile/cross-section drawings showing clearances from the outer conductor to all building projections including overhangs, balconies, awnings, and canopies, with dimensions labeled in feet and inches
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 20); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Construction Details 1 (Sheet 22); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31); Wall Plan (Sheet 38); Wall Plan Details And Notes (Sheet 39); General Notes (Sheet 3); Cover (Sheet 1)
comments.applicableArea: Buildings 1–8 at 3759 Valley View Road; Buildings 1 and 8 (closest to overhead utility lines along Valley View Road/western boundary); Buildings 7 and 8 (closest to OHE line on southern boundary); all proposed structures within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities on western and southern property boundaries
comments.resolution: Submit building elevation sheets and profile/cross-section drawings for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. Drawings must: (1) show surveyed elevations of overhead conductors on each elevation view (including mid-span conductor height); (2) include dimension callouts showing horizontal clearance measured from the outside (outermost) conductor — not pole centerline — to all building faces and the outermost edge of any projections, as horizontal distance only; (3) include section and plan view exhibits with labelled section lines (A-A, B-B, etc.) and dimension lines originating at the outer conductor extending to building edges; and (4) show clearances to all building elements including overhangs, balconies, awnings, and canopies, labeled in feet and inches, demonstrating 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: EL-1.1 returned 'unclear' in two of three runs — reviewer should confirm no clearance dimension annotations exist on any plan sheet.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor locations and clearance dimensions are required to demonstrate that buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No such documentation is present on the site plan.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, particularly Building 1 and Building 8 (closest to overhead electric lines on western and southern boundaries)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms overhead electric utility lines (O.H.U.L.) with utility poles exist along Valley View Road (western boundary) and southern property boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1-8 with Building 1 dimensioned at 26.1' and Building 8 at 26.6' from the western property line. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) references existing OHE lines. However, NO building elevation sheets are provided in the 39-sheet set. NO dimension annotations show horizontal clearances from buildings to the outside conductor of overhead lines. NO surveyed conductor elevations are shown on any drawings.
perRunFindings.reasoning: While buildings are set back approximately 26+ feet from the property line, the requirement is to maintain a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of overhead electric conductors. Without surveyed conductor elevation data, clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to building faces, and no building elevation drawings showing the vertical relationship, it is impossible to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. The code requires clearance measured from the outside conductor (which may be offset several feet from the pole center on multi-conductor installations), not from the pole or property line. Applicant has acknowledged responsibility for maintaining clearances (Sheet 3, Block 8), but has not provided the necessary documentation to demonstrate compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: No building elevation sheets or dimension callouts showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to Buildings 7 and 8. Provide registered surveyor elevation data and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an overhead electric line (OHE) routing along and crossing the site. Sheet 9 (Proposed Site Plan) shows this OHE line running along the southern boundary of the property. Buildings 7 and 8 are positioned closest to this southern boundary. However, no clearance dimension lines or annotations are provided on either the site plan or any building elevation sheets showing the horizontal distance from the buildings' exterior walls or projections to the OHE conductor. No profile/section views are provided showing vertical clearances. The plans do not identify whether the OHE line is a primary, secondary, or neutral conductor, nor is there a surveyed elevation of the conductor provided. No dimension callouts originate from the conductor location itself—the critical measurement baseline required by code.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric conductors. This measurement must be from the outside conductor, not from the pole. The applicant has not provided evidence that this clearance is maintained. Without (1) building elevation sheets showing surveyed conductor elevations, (2) dimension annotations from the outside conductor to the building face, or (3) a registered surveyor's proximity survey per UCM § 1.10.3, the reviewer cannot determine whether the requirement is met.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed buildings do not show measured clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. All buildings with potential clearance concerns require clearance dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets, measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Buildings and permanent structures throughout the site
perRunFindings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) clearly shows overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) running along Valley View Road (western boundary) and the northern property boundary, with utility poles marked. The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows eight multi-story residential buildings (ranging from 33'-5" to 36'-1" in height) positioned on the site. The overhead electric utility line is labeled '----OHE----' on the site plan running along the Valley View Road frontage (southern boundary). However, NO clearance dimensions are annotated anywhere on Sheet 9 showing the horizontal distance from the outside conductor of the overhead line to any building face or structure. No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions were found in the submitted plans.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires buildings to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors. The regulation defines this as a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet from the conductor. The site plan shows buildings within reasonable proximity to the overhead lines along Valley View Road, but the applicant has provided no dimensional evidence that the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal clearance is maintained. The absence of clearance annotations and dimensions constitutes a failure to demonstrate compliance. Per the grouping documentation, clearance dimensions must be labeled on plans with dimension lines originating from the actual outside conductor location (not pole centerline).

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevation sheets prepared by the architect/engineer are required, showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations from the conductor to building faces, roofs, parapets, and all projections, for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All buildings proposed within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: The 39-sheet site plan set does not include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 9 shows building footprints and FFEs but is a plan view only. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors to be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The absence of building elevation sheets constitutes a failure to provide the required documentation. The code requirement is specific: 'Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors not included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met' is identified as a deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are missing. Provide building elevation drawings showing surveyed conductor locations and clearance dimensions to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern OHE line; entire site with overhead facilities
perRunFindings.observation: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires that surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The applicant has not submitted any building elevation sheets. This is a mandatory documentation requirement for any site with buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities. The absence of this required documentation constitutes a deficiency regardless of actual clearances that might exist on the ground.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevation sheets do not show surveyed elevations of existing overhead electric conductors. Sealed building elevation exhibits are required for all buildings with potential proximity to overhead lines, showing the surveyed elevation of the outside conductor and dimensioned clearances from the conductor to building faces and projections.
perRunFindings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents existing overhead utility lines running along the property boundary and service drop. The proposed buildings range from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1" in height. While general notes on Sheet 3 reference benchmarks (B.M. #1 at 678.52' and B.M. #2 at 681.08' NAVD 88), these are general site control points, not surveyed overhead conductor elevations. No building elevation exhibits were found that show the actual conductor elevation overlaid with the building profile to verify vertical clearances.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Documentation Requirements section, 'Profile plans: Engineered, sealed profile drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and building features, including overhangs, balconies, and canopies, with dimensioned clearances' are required. The grouping cites UCM § 1.10.3 as requiring permanent clearances and explicitly states that clearance verification requires 'surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors included on building elevation sheets.' Without surveyed conductor elevation data on building elevation sheets, the applicant cannot demonstrate that the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance or other required clearances are met.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide section view exhibits (with title callouts such as Section A-A, B-B) on site plan or separate detail sheets showing dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of each building and all building projections, clearly labeling clearances in feet and inches.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings in plan view only with no section line callouts (A-A, B-B, etc.) that would reference section views showing clearances. Sheet 22 shows standard construction details for curbs, sidewalks, and driveways but contains no section views specifically showing clearances from outer electric conductor to building edges. Sheets 38-39 show wall construction details and sections but not clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to wall faces. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'Section and plan view exhibits [that] show dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections for clearance verification.' This is a specific documentation requirement. The absence of any section views with dimension lines from the outer conductor to building edges or wall faces constitutes non-compliance. The requirement applies when buildings or structures are proposed within potential clearance distance, which is the case here.

perRunFindings.comment: No section/profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to buildings and site features. Provide detailed section and plan views with dimension callouts from outside conductor to building edges and site improvements.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking areas; all structures within clearance distance of OHE line

These dimension annotations are mandatory and must originate from the actual conductor location, not from the pole. perRunFindings.comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outside electric conductor to the outermost edges of proposed buildings, building projections, and other site features. perRunFindings.reasoning: The grouping explicitly states: 'Common Violation Patterns: Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor... perRunFindings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings are not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities/easements. perRunFindings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities. comments.title: Dual Clearance Envelope Verification Exhibits Not Provided
comments.comment: No engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits are provided demonstrating that proposed structures satisfy both of Austin Energy's required clearance envelopes from overhead distribution conductors.
comments.issue: AEDC § 1.16.0(2) and AEDC § 1.10.3 require engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits, drawn to scale and included in the permitted plan set, demonstrating two concurrent clearance envelopes: (1) the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance — a vertical plane extending infinitely upward from a point 7.5 feet horizontally from the outside conductor — and (2) the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance extending infinitely in all directions from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. These are geometrically distinct envelopes; satisfying one does not satisfy the other, and both must be met simultaneously. No exhibits of either type appear in the 39-sheet plan set.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site where overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors are present; OHE line along Valley View Road (western boundary) and along the southern property boundary
comments.resolution: Prepare engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits (drawn to scale) and include them in the permitted plan set. Each exhibit must graphically depict both clearance envelopes simultaneously: (1) the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance plane extending infinitely upward from 7.5 feet horizontal distance from the outside conductor, and (2) the 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance envelope extending in all directions from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. All measurements must originate from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from pole centerline. Both envelopes must appear on the same exhibit(s).

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits are not provided, not engineered and sealed, or not included in the permitted plan set. No exhibits demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor per AEDC § 1.10.3) are visible on the submitted site plan. applicableAreas: Entire site where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities

Neither sheet shows calculated clearance zones, clearance dimensions measured from outer conductors, or exhibits demonstrating that the dual clearance envelope requirements (7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance) are satisfied. No profile or cross-section views with clearance dimensions are provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.10.3 require clearance verification exhibits when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones of existing electric facilities. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes that BOTH clearance envelopes must be satisfied simultaneously and that clearances must be measured from the outer conductor, not pole centerline. Without engineered exhibits demonstrating these calculations, the applicant has not provided evidence of compliance.

perRunFindings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits not provided. perRunFindings.comment: No clearance verification exhibits provided demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius cylindrical clearance requirements from overhead distribution conductors as required by AEDC § 1.10.3. comments.title: Driveway Vertical Clearance to Overhead Line at Valley View Road Not Documented
comments.comment: No vertical clearance documentation is provided for the proposed driveway that crosses under the existing overhead electric line at the Valley View Road frontage.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (areas without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities — including telecommunications attachments — to the finished driveway grade. The proposed driveway at the Valley View Road frontage crosses directly under the OHE line, but no section views, surveyed conductor heights, mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided on any sheet. Truck traffic classification is unspecified, so the applicable minimum (16 ft vs. 18 ft) cannot be determined.
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Construction Details 1 (Sheet 22)
comments.applicableArea: Proposed Type II and Type III driveways at Valley View Road frontage crossing under OHE line; internal driveways and parking areas on the southern portion of the site adjacent to the OHE line
comments.resolution: Provide grading profile section views at each driveway/OHE crossing showing: (1) finished driveway grade elevations at the conductor crossing location; (2) surveyed overhead conductor height at mid-span above the driveway; (3) vertical clearance dimension annotation from the lowest point of the conductor — including any telecommunications attachments — to the finished driveway grade; and (4) truck traffic classification for each driveway. Clearance must meet 16 feet minimum (no truck traffic) or 18 feet minimum (truck traffic). If clearance appears marginal, provide a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurement.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Two of three runs returned 'unclear' — reviewer should confirm the proposed driveway directly crosses beneath the OHE line on the current site plan.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide grading profile sections for proposed driveways showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations at the low point and dimension annotations verifying minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance (depending on truck traffic designation) from the lowest point of all overhead conductors and attached equipment to the finished driveway surface.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing or passing under or adjacent to overhead electric facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows driveways marked 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway' on the western and internal portions of the site. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows existing and proposed contours with driveway grades and spot elevations, but contains NO profile sections showing the vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached telecommunications lines) to the driveway surface. Sheet 22 shows standard driveway construction details (thickness, reinforcement, grades) but NO sections showing vertical clearance to overhead lines. The FFE elevations of buildings are provided (ranging from 683' to 687.5' NAVD 88), but overhead conductor elevations are not given.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires driveways to maintain minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (for parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (for areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments. This requires (1) surveyed conductor height data, (2) profile or section views showing clearance calculations, and (3) mid-span clearance verification if the clearance appears marginal. None of these are provided. Applicant has not verified mid-span clearances with registered surveyor data, and no vertical clearance dimensions are shown on grading or profile sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: No documented vertical clearance from finished driveway grades to overhead electric line. Provide grading plan section views with finished elevations at OHE line crossing and surveyed conductor height; specify truck traffic classification.
applicableAreas: Internal driveways and parking areas on southern portion of site where OHE line is routed
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows finished floor elevations and site contours but does not provide finished driveway grade elevations at specific locations relative to the OHE line shown on Sheet 9. No section views are provided showing the vertical relationship between the lowest point of the overhead electric line and the finished grade of parking/drive areas. Truck traffic classification (which determines 16-foot vs. 18-foot clearance requirement) is not specified on the plans. No mid-span clearance measurements from a registered surveyor are provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for parking without truck traffic, or 18-foot with truck traffic, from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including service drops and telecommunications attachments). Without (1) documented finished grade elevations at driveway locations, (2) surveyed overhead line heights, and (3) specification of truck traffic usage, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant must provide site/utility profile views with documented vertical clearances.

perRunFindings.comment: The proposed driveway crosses the existing overhead electric line at Valley View Road. No section views, surveyed mid-span clearance measurements, or vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided to demonstrate the minimum 16-foot (or 18-foot for truck traffic areas) vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead line to the finished driveway grade. A registered surveyor's survey showing mid-span clearance is required, with results documented on section views and profile sheets.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveway intersection with overhead utility line at Valley View Road frontage
perRunFindings.observation: The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows an overhead utility line labeled 'O.H.U.L.' running along Valley View Road (western boundary). The proposed site plan (Sheet 9) shows a proposed driveway at the bottom left (Valley View Road frontage) area. Per the vision analysis of Sheet 9, the proposed driveway 'crosses directly under the horizontal ----OHE---- line' along Valley View Road. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows the finished floor elevations and site grades but does not annotate the vertical clearance dimensions at the driveway location where the overhead line crosses. No registered surveyor data showing mid-span clearance measurements is provided. The roadway grade elevations are not dimensioned relative to the overhead line height.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 specifies: 'Driveway and parking without truck traffic: 16 feet minimum vertical clearance; Roads, streets, alleys, and areas with truck traffic: 18 feet minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments.' The grouping documentation notes this is a 'Common Violation Pattern: Inadequate service-drop clearances: Driveway grade shown within 15-16 feet of overhead service drop without mid-span clearance verification; service drop sag at maximum load/temperature may contact vehicles.' Since the proposed driveway crosses under the overhead line, vertical clearance must be verified through surveyed mid-span clearance data showing the lowest point of the conductor at maximum sag.

comments.title: Registered Surveyor Mid-Span Clearance Survey Not Submitted
comments.comment: No registered surveyor field survey data documenting mid-span overhead conductor heights and calculated clearances to proposed structures and site features has been submitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's survey showing pole locations and mid-span clearances when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements. Buildings 7 and 8 and adjacent parking and driveway areas are positioned immediately adjacent to the OHE line on the southern boundary; all buildings are approximately 26–30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western (Valley View Road) boundary. Overhead conductor elevations are not documented anywhere in the 39-sheet plan set, making it impossible to calculate clearances to proposed structures (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground minimum for buildings; 16–18 feet for driveways and parking).
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Buildings 7 and 8 and adjacent parking and driveway areas on southern boundary adjacent to OHE line; all proposed buildings, driveways, parking areas, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
comments.resolution: Submit a registered surveyor's field survey documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above all buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including telecommunications attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with applicable minimum clearance thresholds; and (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements bearing the registered surveyor's certification and seal.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Flagged by 2 of 3 runs — reviewer should confirm that no surveyor mid-span clearance data is present in the submittal and that building and driveway proximity to OHE lines is within the marginal clearance range requiring this survey.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide registered surveyor field survey data documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with minimum clearance thresholds (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground for buildings, 16-18 feet for driveways/parking, others as applicable); (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements with registered surveyor certification.
applicableAreas: All proposed driveways, parking areas, buildings, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
perRunFindings.observation: Overhead electric lines (O.H.U.L.) are shown on existing survey (Sheet 4) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but NO surveyed conductor elevation data is provided anywhere on the 39-sheet site plan set. Buildings have FFEs ranging from 683' to 687.5' (Sheet 9, 11), but overhead conductor heights are not documented. Driveways and parking pads have grading elevations shown (Sheet 11), but no profile sections with surveyed mid-span clearance data verify vertical clearances meet requirements. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that buildings are approximately 26-30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western boundary—this distance is close enough that vertical clearance verification (mid-span clearance) should be provided per UCM § 1.10.3 guidance for situations where 'clearance appears marginal or insufficient.' No registered surveyor data confirming mid-span clearance is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'survey by registered surveyor showing pole locations and mid-span clearances not provided when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements.' The grouping guidance states that when vertical clearance 'appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data,' registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required. The site plan does not provide surveyed conductor elevations, making it impossible to calculate vertical clearances from building FFEs and driveway grades to conductor height. Furthermore, the presence of structures within approximately 26-30 feet horizontally of overhead lines, combined with the absence of conductor elevation data, suggests that clearance verification is required but not provided.

perRunFindings.comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements provided despite buildings and parking areas being positioned adjacent to overhead electric line. Provide licensed surveyor measurements of overhead conductor heights and clearances to all proposed structures and site features.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8; parking and driveway areas adjacent to southern OHE line
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 shows an existing OHE line with utility poles routed across the property. Sheet 9 shows Buildings 7 and 8 and parking/driveway areas positioned immediately adjacent to this overhead line (on southern boundary). Without seeing surveyed conductor elevations or documented clearance measurements, the vertical clearance appears potentially marginal—the minimum required clearances (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18-foot for driveways, 7.5-foot for parking) cannot be visually confirmed from plan-view drawings alone. No mid-span clearance survey data from a registered surveyor is provided to document actual measured clearances.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance measurements when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements or when visual determination is insufficient. Given the close proximity of buildings and parking to the OHE line shown on the plans, and the complete absence of vertical clearance documentation, a registered surveyor's measurement is required to verify compliance. The applicant has not provided this required survey work.

comments.title: Building Elevation Sheets Missing Street, Pole, and Easement Context

- Front and side elevations showing the relationship of all 8 buildings to Valley View Road and existing distribution poles with overhead utility lines along western and southern property boundaries
- Elevation views showing overhead line conductors, cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide per standard distribution pole design), and property boundaries
- Elevation views depicting the spatial relationship between Buildings 1–8 and the documented 5-foot electric easements and 15-foot electric and telephone easements on multiple property boundaries
comments.sheets: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All proposed buildings (Buildings 1–8) in relationship to Valley View Road and distribution poles/overhead utility lines along western and southern property boundaries; 5-foot electric easements and 15-foot electric and telephone easements on multiple property boundaries
comments.resolution: Provide building elevation sheets for all proposed buildings showing: (1) front and side elevations depicting Valley View Road, existing distribution poles, overhead lines, conductors, and cross arms (include cross arm dimension of approximately 8 feet) relative to building faces; (2) property boundary lines on each elevation view; and (3) elevation views oriented from the direction of each electric easement showing the spatial relationship between building faces and the 5-foot and 15-foot electric easement areas documented on the property.

applicableAreas: Locations of existing utility poles and streetlights adjacent to proposed buildings
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) documents existing distribution poles with power lines along Valley View Road (western and southern property boundaries) and shows the overhead utility line (O.H.U.L.) symbols. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing proposed structures with streets, streetlights, and electric poles.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when electric poles or streetlights exist on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has not provided any building elevation sheets. This deficiency directly prevents verification of clearance compliance between proposed structures and existing overhead electric facilities.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing proposed structures with adjacent streets (Valley View Road), streetlights, and electric poles. Provide front and side elevations for all buildings showing the relationship to Valley View Road, existing poles, and overhead/underground facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(2).
applicableAreas: Relationship to existing Valley View Road, poles, and streetlights
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan submittal (39 sheets total) contains detailed site plans, grading plans, utility plans, and landscape plans, but does NOT include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing site features and property context, but no building elevation views have been identified in the submittal. UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires building elevations showing the relationship between proposed structures and existing public infrastructure including streets, streetlights, and electric poles. The absence of building elevation sheets representing the buildings' relationship to Valley View Road and any adjacent utility poles/streetlights is a clear deficiency in the required documentation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires building elevations to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing streets, streetlights, and electric poles. These elevation views are essential for demonstrating clearance compliance and understanding site context. comments.title: Detention Pond Retaining Wall Encroaches into Electric Easement

comments.issue:

- Sheet 9 confirms the concrete retaining wall enclosing the pond is drawn within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern property boundary (plat-dedicated per Sheet 2, Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160); a detention pond with retaining walls, biofiltration media, and required vegetation constitutes a drainage structure prohibited within an electric easement
- Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 16) explicitly prohibit drainage, filtration, or detention ponds that impair Austin Energy's access to transmission easements; no documentation demonstrates the pond design preserves the required 25-ft maintenance vehicle turnaround clearance from structure base at the northeast corner transmission easement boundary

- Provide dimensioned site plan documentation or an Austin Energy letter confirming that the pond design preserves required transmission easement access, including the 25-ft clearance from structure base for 80,000-lb maintenance vehicle turnaround

The site plan does not provide documentation that the pond design has been reviewed for impact on transmission facility access or that the pond can be maintained while preserving Austin Energy's turnaround and maintenance vehicle access requirements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: While water quality features (detention ponds) may be allowable outside transmission easements with appropriate setbacks, the proposed pond's immediate adjacency to the transmission easement boundary raises questions about whether it impairs Austin Energy access as prohibited. The transmission facility access requirements (including 25-foot clearance from structure base for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles) must be verified.
