comments.title: Recorded Easements Missing from Site Plan; Overhead Clearance Unverified
comments.comment: Multiple recorded easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan, and no proximity survey has been provided to verify that proposed customer facilities comply with Austin Energy overhead clearance requirements.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition on customer facilities installed under or over AE overhead distribution facilities and requires all facilities within electric easements to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The following easements are either not depicted or not verified on the submitted site plans:
- Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 ac NE interior) — recorded and perpetual, not depicted on site plan, not in COA GIS
- City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 ac NE corner) — recorded and perpetual, not depicted on site plan, not in COA GIS
- 5' Electric Easements (×2) and 7.5' Public Utility Easement (plat-dedicated, Vol. 73/Pg. 76) — boundaries not verified relative to proposed improvements
Without accurate easement boundaries shown, neither the absolute prohibition on facilities under/over overhead distribution lines nor the 7.5-foot clearance requirement can be confirmed.
comments.sheets: Plat (Sheet 2); Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All proposed customer facilities, building structures, and site features relative to existing electric easements and overhead distribution facilities; specifically the NE interior (Greenbelt Access easement), NE corner (City of Austin Drainage easement), and eastern boundary (5' Electric Easements ×2 and 7.5' PUE)
comments.resolution: Add all recorded easements — including the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731), City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137), 5' Electric Easements (×2), and 7.5' Public Utility Easement — to the site plan with accurate boundary dimensions and recording references. Provide a registered surveyor proximity survey confirming: (1) no customer facilities are located under or over AE overhead distribution lines (absolute prohibition); (2) all facilities within electric easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor; and (3) all facilities comply with easement use restrictions.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should independently verify all easement boundaries against Travis County recorder documents and COA GIS; the Greenbelt and Drainage easements are confirmed recorded but absent from submitted plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide comprehensive easement exhibit on site plan showing all recorded easements (Greenbelt Access, City Drainage, 5' Electric Easements ×2, 7.5' Public Utility Easement, and any others per county records) with accurate boundary dimensions. Provide registered surveyor proximity survey confirming: (1) no customer facilities are located under or over overhead distribution lines (absolute prohibition); (2) all facilities within electric easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor; (3) all facilities comply with easement use restrictions.
applicableAreas: All proposed customer facilities, building structures, and site features relative to existing electric easements and overhead distribution facilities
perRunFindings.observation: Facts.md identifies two perpetual easements with NO development permitted: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres) in NE interior—explicitly marked as 'strict no-build zone'; (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres) in NE corner with unlimited City access rights. Both are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (facts.md: 'NOT depicted on the submitted site plan and NOT in the COA GIS easement layer'). Additionally, a 5' Electric Easement (×2) and 7.5' Public Utility Easement are plat-dedicated per facts.md but locations relative to proposed improvements are not verified on site plans. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show all easements, but facts.md notes these are not shown. Sheet 9 shows the general site layout and street easements, but does not clearly depict all recorded electric easement boundaries or verify that proposed features maintain adequate clearance from easement areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: 'customer facilities proposed to be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities' is prohibited 'regardless of clearance distances.' Additionally, items within electric easements must maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The facts.md documentation reveals that critical easements (Greenbelt, Drainage, Electric, PUE) are either not depicted or not verified on the site plan. Without accurate easement boundaries shown on plans, applicant cannot demonstrate that (1) no facilities are placed under/over overhead distribution lines in violation of the absolute prohibition, or (2) items within easements maintain required 7.5-foot clearances. A proximity survey by registered surveyor is required to confirm easement boundaries and facility compliance.

comments.title: Non-Electric Utility Equipment and Crossing Angles in Electric Easements Not Documented
comments.comment: The utility plans do not explicitly confirm that all non-electric utility equipment is located outside the electric easements or that any utility crossings of easements occur at perpendicular angles.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.3.24 prohibits water, wastewater, and gas utility facilities, meters, vaults, backflow preventers, valves, tanks, and equipment from being located within electric easements where only electric facilities are permitted, and requires non-electric utility lines to cross easements perpendicularly rather than running parallel or longitudinally. UCM § 1.14.7 similarly restricts non-electric utility installations within easements. The submitted plans show utility infrastructure locations but:
- Provide no explicit confirmation or dimension callouts showing that water meters, wastewater connection points, and backflow preventers are located outside the 5' Electric Easement boundaries
- Do not document the routing alignments or crossing angles of water and wastewater utilities relative to the electric easements
- Contain no detail sheets, notes, or utility coordination table specifying perpendicular crossing compliance
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 20); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Electric easement boundaries throughout the site; utility connections on the western side of the property; 5' Electric Easement along the eastern property boundary
comments.resolution: Provide a utility coordination plan that: (1) explicitly confirms through dimension callouts that all water meters, wastewater connection points, backflow preventers, and other non-electric utility equipment are located outside all electric easement boundaries; and (2) documents the routing alignment and crossing angles of all non-electric utilities relative to electric easements, confirming perpendicular (or near-perpendicular) crossing angles and the absence of parallel runs within any electric easement.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — visual inspection suggests water/wastewater connections are on the western side away from the eastern electric easement, but explicit dimensional confirmation is absent from the plan set.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide utility plan with explicit confirmation and dimensions showing that all water meters, wastewater connection points, backflow preventers, and other utility equipment are located outside all electric easements and crossing utility lines cross only perpendicularly.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis identified multiple utility easements: wastewater easement, drainage easements, public utility easement, and electric easements. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water meter and wastewater connection points on the western side of the property. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric transformers at locations: NW corner Bldg. 1, SW corner Bldg. 8, SE corner Bldg. 6, and between Bldgs. 4-5. The utility tap locations (water meter) do not appear to be within the 5' electric easement on the eastern boundary based on their western-side positioning. However, no explicit statement is provided on the plans confirming that all utility equipment (water meters, backflow preventers, wastewater connection points) are located outside the electric easements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-5.13 requires: 'Water, wastewater, or gas utility facilities, meters, vaults, backflow preventers, valves, tanks, or equipment located within electric easements where only electric facilities are permitted.' The plans show utility infrastructure locations but do not explicitly confirm that all non-electric utility equipment is outside the electric easement boundaries. While visual inspection suggests water/wastewater connections are on the western side away from the eastern electric easement, explicit clearance confirmation with dimension callouts is absent. Marked 'unclear' because the issue cannot be definitively confirmed from available plan evidence.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide utility coordination plan documenting that all non-electric utilities (water, wastewater) cross electric easements at perpendicular or near-perpendicular angles. Confirm no utility lines run parallel or longitudinally within electric easements and no utility vaults or equipment are located within easement boundaries.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple easements including drainage, wastewater, utility, and electric. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water and wastewater service connections. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing. The utility plans indicate water service connection on the western side and wastewater connection points, suggesting these utilities may cross the site. However, the plans do not show explicit routing alignments or crossing angles for utilities relative to the electric easements. No detail sheets or notes specify the crossing angles or confirm perpendicular crossings of non-electric utilities through electric easements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-5.16 requires: 'Non-electric utility lines (water, wastewater, gas, private utilities) running parallel or longitudinally within electric easements rather than crossing perpendicularly.' The code allows perpendicular utility crossings but prohibits parallel runs or utility equipment/vaults within easements. The submitted plans do not explicitly document the routing angles and crossing methodologies for water and wastewater utilities relative to electric easements. Without these details, compliance with the perpendicular crossing requirement cannot be confirmed.

comments.title: Fire Hydrant Location Intersects 5' Electric Easement Boundary
comments.comment: Fire Hydrant 1 appears to be located with its center directly on the inner boundary of the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern property line, potentially placing the hydrant partially within the easement.

This site has distribution easements and distribution-level infrastructure, not transmission. The cited code (UCM § 1.14.7) is transmission-specific. While fire hydrants should not be located in electric easements generally (per basic access principles), this specific checklist item is transmission-focused. The fire hydrant proximity to the distribution easement boundary is problematic for access but is not captured by EL-5.23's transmission-specific criteria. Marked 'unclear' because the fire hydrant location relative to distribution easements is a potential issue not specifically addressed by EL-5.23.

comments.title: Separate-Instrument Easement Dedications for Vault and Cross-Property Facilities Undocumented
comments.comment: It is unclear whether new separate-instrument easement dedications are required for the transformer vault and cross-property underground electric line shown on Sheet 21, and no metes and bounds descriptions or surveyor-sealed field notes have been provided for those facilities.

perRunFindings.comment: It is unclear whether applicant is relying solely on 1975 plat-dedicated easements or proposing new separate-instrument easement dedications for vault and cross-property electric facilities. No separate-instrument exhibits are visible on site plan.

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Site Plan Review

perRunFindings.observation: This is a site plan filing without concurrent subdivision plat. Existing electric easements from 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat are shown on Sheet 2 (5-foot E&T easement, 7.5-foot P.U.E.) with plat-recorded status. However, additional infrastructure shown on Sheet 21 includes a transformer vault easement (labeled as 'Vault Easement' on the drawing) and an underground electric line that extends across the southern property boundary to an adjacent property. No explicit separate-instrument easement exhibits or dedications are visible on the site plan for these new/modified facilities. The Site Plan Release Notes (Sheet 3, Block 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' suggesting potential future dedications but no current dedicated separate instruments are evident. It is unclear whether the applicant intends to rely solely on the existing 1975 plat easements for all proposed facilities, or whether new separate-instrument dedications are being made for the vault and cross-property facilities.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code §§ 14-1-11, 14-1-21, and 14-1-22 establish that when a site plan is filed without a concurrent platting activity, electric easements must be dedicated by separate recordable document (deed or easement agreement) with metes and bounds and surveyor certification. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site plan is filed without concurrent subdivision plat or when additional easements are needed after plat recordation.' This site IS filed without concurrent plat, AND there ARE additional facilities (vault, cross-property line) shown that may require additional easement dedications beyond what the 1975 plat provides. However, the plans do not clearly indicate whether separate-instrument dedications are being made. The presence of the Bluebeam coordination link with Austin Energy (per master comment report) suggests some coordination occurred, but the visible site plan documents do not show explicit separate-instrument dedications with proper documentation. This ambiguity warrants an 'unclear' determination pending clarification of the applicant's intent regarding separate-instrument dedication.

perRunFindings.comment: If new easement dedications are required for vault and cross-property facilities, metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes must be provided to Austin Energy; none are visible on site plan
applicableAreas: Vault easement for transformers; cross-property easement for southern electric line extension
perRunFindings.observation: No metes and bounds descriptions, surveyor-sealed field notes, or surveyor exhibits are visible on the site plan for the vault easement (labeled on Sheet 21) or the cross-property electric line extension (shown extending south from the site across property boundary on Sheet 21 vision analysis). The 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat (Sheet 2) shows plat-dedicated easements with surveyor certification dated August 20, 1975, but contains no metes and bounds narrative for those easements—only visual boundary depictions and recording references. If new easement dedications are required (per EL-7.1 determination), Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) mandates that metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes be provided. No such documentation is evident on the submitted site plan sheets.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) specifies that easement dedications by separate instrument require metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor. UCM § 1.16.0(3) similarly requires that metes and bounds descriptions be provided to Austin Energy for easement dedication. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site requiring electric easement dedication by separate instrument.' If the determination of EL-7.1 is that new separate-instrument dedications ARE required, then metes and bounds are a mandatory component that must be present. The absence of metes and bounds on the visible site plan is a deficiency. However, this determination is contingent on EL-7.1 being clarified as requiring new dedications rather than relying on existing plat easements. Hence, 'unclear' is warranted pending that clarification. If new dedications are required and metes and bounds are absent, this would be a 'fail.'

comments.title: Public Utility Easement Width Adequacy for Proposed Utilities Not Verified

comments.title: Overhead Electric Clearance Zones May Extend Across Property Boundaries
comments.comment: No clearance verification exhibits have been provided to determine whether the required horizontal and radial clearance zones from the existing overhead electric line extend across the southern property boundary onto the subject site.

comments.resolution: Provide clearance verification exhibits (per EL-11.1 requirements) depicting the 7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance zones around the existing overhead electric line on the southern boundary, confirming whether those envelopes extend across the property line onto the subject site and that no proposed structures or improvements encroach into those zones.
