perRunFindings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether required clearance zones from overhead electric facilities extend across property lines. This determination depends on the clearance verification exhibits referenced in deficiency EL-11.1. Please provide clearance verification exhibits that clearly show whether required clearance envelopes extend beyond the subject property boundary.
applicableAreas: Property boundaries where clearance zones extend across lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show property lines and existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary near Valley View Road. The sheets show that the existing overhead line is located outside the subject property (on the street side). However, without clearance verification exhibits (as noted in deficiency EL-11.1), it is impossible to determine whether required clearance zones extend across the property line boundary. No clearance radius is drawn or calculated on the available sheets. The applicability of this item depends on whether clearances extend beyond property boundaries, which cannot be verified from the submitted evidence.
perRunFindings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 specifies dual clearance zones (7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radius) that may extend across property boundaries if structures are sufficiently close to the property line. However, without the clearance verification exhibits that should be provided in response to EL-11.1, this specific requirement cannot be evaluated. The determination of whether clearance lines should extend across property boundaries is dependent on the clearance exhibit analysis, which has not been provided.

comments.title: Parkland Designation Overlap with Transmission Easement Not Confirmed
comments.comment: It cannot be confirmed from the submitted plans whether any parkland designation or parkland dedication area overlaps with the transmission easement boundaries documented on the site.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits designation of land within transmission easements as parkland or for parkland dedication. Transmission easements with strict restrictions — prohibiting habitable structures, storage sheds, detention/drainage ponds, and other uses that would impair AE access — are documented on Sheet 3 (Electric Transmission Notes, Item 16 and throughout). The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) and Plat (Sheet 2) do not provide a spatial overlay of the transmission easement footprint against any parkland designations. Facts.md confirms the site is within a Parkland Deficient Area (two polygon features intersect the parcel), indicating parkland fee-in-lieu requirements will apply per unit, but the plans do not depict the transmission easement boundaries in relation to any proposed parkland credit or dedication area.
comments.sheets: Plat (Sheet 2); General Notes (Sheet 3); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Transmission easement areas throughout the site; any proposed parkland dedication or parkland credit areas
comments.resolution: Depict the transmission easement boundaries on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) and Plat/General Notes (Sheets 2–3) with explicit notation confirming that no parkland designation, parkland dedication, or permanent structures are located within the transmission easement area. If the project relies solely on parkland fee-in-lieu, confirm in writing to Austin Energy that no parkland credit is proposed within the transmission easement footprint.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Parkland designation and dedication determinations typically require coordination with the Parks and Recreation Department; Austin Energy must also confirm transmission easement boundaries to enable a spatial compliance check.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs) — spatial comparison of transmission easement and parkland boundaries cannot be confirmed from submitted plan evidence; reviewer should obtain AE transmission easement boundary data for overlay check.

perRunFindings.comment: Parkland designation within transmission easement areas not verified. Review Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) to confirm that no parkland is designated or proposed within transmission easement areas per UCM § 1.16.0(9).
perRunFindings.observation: The facts.md notes transmission easement restrictions on the property. Sheet 31 is the Landscape Plan. However, without detailed examination of Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), the presence or absence of parkland designations overlapping with transmission easement areas cannot be definitively determined. The facts.md indicates transmission easement areas exist, but does not specifically indicate whether parkland is proposed within those areas. The plat designations would show any parkland areas.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits designation of land within transmission easements as parkland or for parkland dedication. If the project includes parkland dedication and any of the dedicated area overlaps with transmission easements, this is a deficiency. The review of available materials does not provide sufficient detail to confirm or deny parkland designation compliance. Additional examination of the plat and landscape plan would be needed.

perRunFindings.comment: Cannot definitively verify from available evidence whether land within transmission easement is correctly excluded from parkland designation or reserved for parkland dedication. Provide explicit identification of transmission easement boundaries on landscape and plat plans with clear notation that no parkland or permanent structures are located within easement areas.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes (item 16 and throughout the section) establish that transmission easements exist on the property with strict restrictions prohibiting habitable structures, storage sheds, drainage/detention ponds, and other structures that would impair AE access. Sheet 31 shows a landscape plan. Facts.md identifies transmission easement existence on the property but does not specify exact boundaries. Vision analysis of Sheet 3 confirmed the transmission easement requirements are documented but cannot visually confirm the exact spatial footprint of the transmission easement relative to proposed parkland designations on the landscape plan without additional detailed examination. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) cannot be fully evaluated for parkland designation conflicts with transmission easement location without comparative spatial analysis.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits land within transmission easements from being labeled as parkland or proposed for parkland dedication. This is a critical restriction violation if transmission easements overlap with landscape/parkland areas. The facts and Electric Transmission Notes confirm transmission easements exist; however, without access to the specific transmission easement boundary overlay and detailed landscape plan parkland designation boundaries, a definitive determination cannot be made. The requirement necessitates visual confirmation of coordinate/spatial relationships.

comments.title: Fire Lane Routing Relative to Transmission Easement Not Documented
comments.comment: The transmission easement boundary is not depicted on the fire protection plan or site plan, making it impossible to verify whether internal fire lanes or drive aisles cross or encroach into the Austin Energy transmission easement.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.0 requires that any fire lane or driveway crossing AE property be relocated within the limits of construction with all required clearances maintained. Sheet 3 (Electric Transmission Notes) specifies a 25-foot clearance from transmission structures and a 46,000 lb pavement design requirement for paving within the transmission easement. Neither Sheet 9 (Site Plan) nor Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) depict the transmission easement boundary, making it impossible to verify whether internal fire lanes/drive aisles pass through the easement or merely run adjacent to it.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10)
comments.applicableArea: Internal drive aisles and fire lanes; areas potentially within or adjacent to the Austin Energy transmission easement
comments.resolution: Depict the Austin Energy transmission easement boundary on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10). Verify that internal fire lanes do not cross the transmission easement; if any fire lane must cross the easement, provide documentation confirming: (1) the crossing is within limits of construction; (2) all UCM § 1.10.0 clearances from transmission structures are met; and (3) pavement design within the easement is designed for 46,000 lb loading per Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Fire lane routing changes may require coordination with Austin Fire Department to confirm continued compliance with fire access requirements.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — transmission easement boundary is absent from submitted plan sheets; reviewer should independently confirm easement location against Austin Energy records before requiring plan revision.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed fire lane routing relative to AE transmission easement not clearly documented. Depict transmission easement boundary on site plan and verify that fire lane routing does not cross the easement or, if it must cross, confirm it is relocated within construction limits and maintains all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.0 and Sheet 3 transmission easement requirements (25-foot clearance from structures, 46,000 lb pavement design in easement).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) shows internal drive aisles serving the eight buildings with fire lanes, but does not explicitly label any routes as passing through an Austin Energy transmission easement. Sheet 9 shows internal driveways but the transmission easement is not depicted, making it unclear whether fire lanes/driveways technically pass through the transmission easement area or merely adjacent to it. The site plan lacks clear visualization of the transmission easement boundary relative to fire lane routing.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.0 requires that if a fire lane routing crosses AE property, it must be relocated within limits of construction and necessary clearances must be met. Without the transmission easement boundary depicted on the site plan, it cannot be verified whether fire lanes pass through the easement or maintain required clearances. Sheet 3 transmission notes indicate 25-foot clearances are required from transmission structures, but the actual easement boundaries are not shown for comparison against fire lane locations.

comments.title: Projected Electrical Load Calculations Missing from Plans
comments.comment: No projected electrical load, demand projections, or capacity analysis have been documented on the electrical plans or submitted to Austin Energy Design for this 39-unit development.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that projected electrical load be shown on plans and that load calculations, demand projections, and capacity analysis be provided to Austin Energy Design. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows infrastructure routing, transformer pads, pull boxes, and meter locations but contains no load data in any form—no kW or kVA figures, no service amperage, no demand tables, and no load calculation documentation. Without load documentation, Austin Energy cannot verify transformer sizing, service amperage adequacy, conduit capacity, or determine whether line extension or infrastructure upgrades are required to serve the development.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site; all transformer pad locations and service points; electrical design plan documentation
comments.resolution: Calculate and document the total projected electrical demand for all 39 units and 8 buildings (in kW or kVA) per NEC/IEEE standards and show on Sheet 21 in a load calculations table including: (1) total project demand load; (2) per-building load breakdown with square footage basis; (3) kVA rating for each transformer pad; (4) service amperage per building; (5) demand factors applied. Submit the load calculations to Austin Energy Design for review and approval.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires submission to and approval by Austin Energy Design, which must verify adequacy of the proposed service configuration based on calculated load.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical load calculations, demand projections, and capacity analysis not provided to Austin Energy Design. Provide detailed electrical load calculations showing peak demand projections and capacity analysis for the proposed 39-unit development to AE Design for review and approval.
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and general notes (Sheet 3) with electric transmission requirements. However, after review of Sheet 21 blocks and guides, Sheet 3 electric notes, the Engineer's Summary Letter, and all supplementary documents, no electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis documents were located in the submittal. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows routing and equipment placement but does not include load calculations or capacity analysis documentation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that electrical load calculations, demand projections, and capacity analysis be provided to AE Design. These are essential technical documents needed for AE to evaluate whether existing service is adequate or whether upgrades are required. The absence of these calculations from the submitted documents represents a gap in required electrical design documentation. Load calculations are typically the basis for determining transformer size, service requirements, and capacity adequacy.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical load calculations and demand projections not provided to Austin Energy. Sheet 21 shows preliminary layout only without load analysis, demand calculations, or capacity specifications. Submit detailed electrical load calculations for all 39 units and buildings, including peak demand, connected load, demand factors per NEC standards, and capacity analysis to support service requirements determination.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows spatial routing of underground electric lines, transformer pads, pull boxes, and meters. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: NO load calculations or capacity analysis visible anywhere on the sheet. No tables, schedules, or numerical load data present. Engineer's Summary Letter covers only water and wastewater utilities, not electrical. No supplementary document containing load calculations identified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires 'electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis' be provided to AE Design. The preliminary nature of Sheet 21's design (no service specifications, no voltage/phase/amperage shown) indicates load analysis has not been performed or submitted. For a 39-unit development with 8 buildings, electrical demand calculations are fundamental to determining service requirements. The absence of this documentation is a clear deficiency.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis not provided to AE Design. Submit electrical load calculations for the 39-unit development, including peak demand projections and justification for transformer sizing and service specifications shown on the site plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical layout with transformer pads, pull boxes, and service routing, but no supporting electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis documented. No calculations provided verifying that the proposed transformer capacity is adequate for 39 units or substantiating the specific equipment sizing shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires load calculations and demand projections be provided to AE Design during land development review. These calculations justify the service specifications and allow AE Design to verify adequacy. Absence of these calculations prevents AE Design review of electrical system adequacy.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load for the 39-unit multifamily project not shown on plans. Calculate and document total electrical demand (peak load in kW or kVA) required for the project based on unit types, occupancy, and expected usage patterns per IEEE, NEC, or AE load calculation standards. Show demand on electrical design plan.
applicableAreas: All service locations and transformer pad locations
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer locations and service infrastructure but does not specify the projected electrical load (in kW, kVA, or amperage) for the facility. No load calculations, demand estimates, or power requirement specifications are documented on the electrical sheets. Sheet 3 General Notes do not specify electrical load. The project description (39 multifamily units) is known, but the electrical demand calculation required by UCM is not shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that plans show 'Approximate location and space for electric facilities, desired service point, projected load shown.' Projected electrical load is a fundamental requirement for Austin Energy to determine transformer sizing, service entrance capacity, line extension requirements, and overall system adequacy. Without load documentation, Austin Energy cannot verify that the proposed service configuration is adequate for the project's electrical demand.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load for proposed service is not shown on plans. Please provide: (1) load calculation for the 39-unit residential development (in watts or kVA); (2) transformer kVA ratings on all transformer pads; (3) service panel amperage (e.g., 200A, 400A, 600A per building); (4) one-line electrical diagram showing load distribution; (5) verification that transformer size is adequate for projected demand.
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for projected load documentation. The sheet shows transformer pads and meters but does not include: (1) kVA ratings for the transformers, (2) amperage capacity of service, (3) load calculations for the 39-unit residential project, (4) notes indicating projected electrical load, (5) equipment schedules with load data. No load analysis or calculations are shown on the electrical plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires 'Projected electrical load required for electric service [to be] shown on plans.' This information is critical for AE Design to verify: (1) transformer size is adequate for the load, (2) service amperage is appropriate, (3) no load-related issues exist. Without this documentation, AE Design cannot verify the design is code-compliant and adequate to serve the 39 units.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load not shown on plans. Calculate and show the total electrical load for the project (in kW or kVA) and identify the load for each building or service point, based on building size, occupancy classification, and code-required minimum loads.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of projected electrical load information. Vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No, projected electrical loads (kW, kVA, or amperage) are not shown anywhere on this sheet.' The sheet contains building square footage and finished floor elevations (e.g., 'Bldg. 1: 3,290 sf, FFE = 687.50'), but there is no statement of total project electrical load, load per building, service amperage, or any other load specification.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires that plans show 'Projected electrical load required for electric service' as part of the application requirements. Projected load is essential information for Austin Energy to determine service requirements, transformer sizing, and capacity. Without projected load, AE cannot verify that the proposed transformer(s) are adequately sized, that conduit sizing is appropriate, or that the overall service design meets load demands.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected load for electric service is not provided on electrical plans. Please provide the calculated electrical load for the proposed development (in kVA or kW) based on the 39 residential townhome units and any common area electrical requirements, and submit for Austin Energy capacity verification.
perRunFindings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 3 (General Notes), and facts.md project summary. No electrical load information is shown on any sheet. Sheet 21 shows facility locations and routing but no load calculations, service amperage, or projected demand information. Sheet 3 contains Austin Water capacity letters for water and wastewater service but no corresponding electrical load letter or documentation from Austin Energy. Facts.md describes the project as 39 townhome units but provides no electrical load requirements.
perRunFindings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that 'Projected load [be] required for electric service' for projects with new or upgraded electric service. This project is clearly a new development with 39 units requiring new electric service. The applicant must provide electrical load calculations showing the total demand (in kVA or kW) for the project based on the 39-unit residential load and any common area requirements.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected load required for electrical service not clearly provided. If new service is being provided, submit load calculations and electrical demand projections in kVA or kW with service voltage, transformer size (kVA), and amperage rating specifications. Confirm with Austin Energy whether load calculations are required in site plan or deferred to building permit design.
perRunFindings.observation: Searched Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and related sheets for projected electrical load information. Sheet 21 shows utility notes mentioning water and wastewater specifications but NO electrical load information. No kW or kVA load calculations are shown. No service amperage or voltage specifications are documented. No electrical one-line diagram or load calculation documentation exists. Master Comment Report lists UCM § 1.9.3 (Installation of Metering Equipment) as a preliminary design requirement, suggesting service design details should be provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires projected load for electric service. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan and routing of new underground electric service indicate new service is provided. If new service is proposed, load must be documented. However, applicability is UNCLEAR because whether this qualifies as 'new service' requiring load documentation in site plan versus preliminary routing subject to later building permit design is ambiguous. Master Comment Report's inclusion of metering equipment requirements suggests loads should be specified.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load not provided on electrical plans. Estimated demand load in amperes (or kVA) must be calculated and shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to demonstrate adequate service sizing.
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) for projected load information. The sheet contains: building unit counts (e.g., Bldg. 1: 3 units, Bldg. 2: 6 units), square footage per building, and FFE data. No projected electrical load (in kW, amperage, or kVA) is labeled on the sheet. No demand calculation is shown. No specification of service amperage or phases is documented. No load table is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires 'Projected load' to be 'provided on electrical plans' for projects with 'new or upgraded electric service.' This 39-unit multi-family project requires new electric service, triggering the requirement. The electrical design plan shows physical layout of distribution infrastructure but does not quantify the electrical load that infrastructure must serve. Without projected load documentation, reviewers cannot verify that the service size, transformer capacity, and distribution infrastructure are adequate for the intended use.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load is not shown on any plan sheets. UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires documentation of the projected electrical load for the development. Add load calculations and clearly indicate the total projected load and individual building loads on the electrical site plan and other required sheets.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows building identifications, unit counts, and floor areas, but does not include any notation of projected electrical load (in kW, kVA, amps, or other standard electrical load units) for the development or individual buildings. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show projected electrical load. No other sheets reference electrical load calculations or projections. The supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report) do not mention electrical load.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that the 'projected electrical load' be shown on plan sheets submitted for Austin Energy land development review. This is a fundamental requirement to demonstrate the adequacy of service and determine whether line extension or other infrastructure upgrades are needed.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load is not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or any other plan sheet. Add projected electrical service amperage, estimated demand (kW or kVA), or connected load to the electrical design plan. Include load calculations for all buildings and identify the service voltage and amperage for the development.
perRunFindings.observation: Examination of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows detailed electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground routing, benchmarks, utility notes) but contains NO indication of projected electrical load in any form. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 lists 'Utility Notes' that address contractor requirements and material specifications, but no load information. The 'Key values' section lists building sizes and floor areas but no electrical load figures (kW, kVA, Amps, or service amperage). No supplementary documents reviewed contain electrical load information.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires 'projected electrical load' to be shown on plan sheets. This is distinguished from infrastructure location — load information must be documented to allow Austin Energy to verify adequate service capacity and equipment sizing. Without projected load documentation, Austin Energy cannot make an informed determination of line extension requirements, duct bank requirements, vault vs. pedestal service selection, or service point location per UCM § 1.3.12 and § 1.5.2.1.

perRunFindings.comment: Projected electrical load must be shown on plan sheets. Add load calculations table to the electrical design plan showing total projected electrical demand in kW and/or amperes, and breakdown by building if applicable, per UCM § 1.16.0(6).
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). No electrical load calculations, demand summaries, amperage requirements, voltage specifications, or load data appear on any of these sheets. No tables or callouts showing projected electrical load for the development (e.g., total kW, total amps, demand load per building) are present. The sheets show physical infrastructure (transformers, meters, lines) but do not quantify the electrical service demand.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires the projected electrical load to be shown on plan sheets. The grouping's common violation patterns list 'Missing projected load: No indication of projected electrical load for the development' as a violation. The absence of load data on any plan sheet prevents verification of service adequacy and AE Design determination of infrastructure requirements.

comments.title: Service Voltage and Size Specifications Require Austin Energy Design Approval
comments.comment: The electrical plans show service infrastructure without voltage, phase, or capacity specifications, and no Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics has been submitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications to be provided to AE Design; UCM § 1.3.2 establishes that AE Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity)—applicants cannot self-certify these parameters. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads, underground service lines, and meter banks but includes no service voltage (e.g., 120/208V, 277/480V), phase designation, or amperage specifications. No AE Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics for this location is on file.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site; all transformer pad and service connection locations; electrical service design documentation
comments.resolution: Submit an Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming the service characteristics available and approved for this site, specifying: (1) service voltage (e.g., 120/208V, 277/480V); (2) phase configuration (single-phase or 3-phase); (3) service capacity in amps. Do not show service specifications on the plans until AE Design provides written determination, then update Sheet 21 to reflect AE-approved parameters.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires Austin Energy Design to issue a written service determination; AE Design holds exclusive authority to specify voltage, phase, and capacity parameters for this location.

perRunFindings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications not documented on site plan or provided to Austin Energy Design. Provide specifications for service voltage (e.g., 120/240V or three-phase voltage) and service size (e.g., amperage and transformer kVA ratings) to AE Design and document AE Design approval on site plan.
perRunFindings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows general routing of electrical infrastructure, transformers, and meters but does not include voltage and service size specifications. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 provides utility notes about water and wastewater specifications but does not document electrical service voltage (e.g., 120/240V, 277/480V, 12.47kV) or service size (e.g., 200A, 400A, transformer capacity in kVA). No voltage and service size specifications were found in supplementary documents or correspondence.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that voltage and service size specifications required for service be provided to AE Design. This is a fundamental technical specification that AE Design must evaluate and approve. Service voltage and size determinations cannot be made by the applicant; they must be determined and approved by AE Design based on the calculated load and available infrastructure.

perRunFindings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications not provided. Sheet 21 shows preliminary layout without service voltage, phase requirements, or amperage specifications. Submit Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity in amps) for this site, or indicate which specifications will be determined during detailed design phase per AE direction.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis found: NO voltage specifications visible, NO phase requirements labeled, NO service capacity/amperage shown. The sheet shows proposed transformer pad and pull box locations with labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Underground Electric Line') but no technical parameters. No service characteristics specified anywhere on the sheet or in supplementary documents.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications necessary for service be provided to AE Design. These are critical parameters that must be determined by Austin Energy Design based on customer load requirements. The absence of voltage (e.g., 120/240V, 480V), phase (single-phase, 3-phase), and service amperage on the drawings indicates Austin Energy has not yet provided these determinations.

perRunFindings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications required for service not provided to AE Design with AE approval documentation. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming service voltage, phase configuration, and capacity specifications for the development.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with transformer and service routing but does not document voltage, phase, capacity specifications in a format submitted to AE Design. No documentation of AE Design approval for the service voltage and size specifications shown on the electrical plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications be provided to AE Design during review. Per regulatory overview, applicants cannot self-certify service specifications — AE Design must determine and approve what voltage, phases, and capacity are available and adequate at the specific location. Showing service specifications without AE Design approval documentation violates UCM § 1.3.2.

perRunFindings.comment: Service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) not shown with Austin Energy Design approval documentation. Either remove service specifications from the plans, or provide an AE Design approval letter confirming the voltage, phases, service size, and transformer capacity shown are available and approved for this location.
perRunFindings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and electrical equipment placement and routing. However, the blocks.md and guide.md for Sheet 21 do not document specific service voltage or service characteristics (single-phase vs. three-phase, service amperage, transformer capacity in kVA) with documentation of AE Design determination and approval. The preliminary design shows equipment placement but does not include voltage and capacity specifications with AE Design approval letters or correspondence.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Plans showing service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) require documentation of AE Design determination and approval per UCM § 1.3.2. Applicants cannot self-determine service specifications; these are determined and approved by AE Design based on load analysis and available infrastructure. Evidence of AE Design approval must accompany any service specifications shown on plans.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans show preliminary electrical design without Austin Energy Design approval of service characteristics. Provide Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming the service characteristics available and approved for this site, specifying: (1) service voltage available (e.g., 120/240V, 480V), (2) phase configuration (single-phase or 3-phase), and (3) service capacity in amps. Do not show service specifications on plans until AE Design provides written determination.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis found: NO service voltage shown, NO phase designation (single-phase or 3-phase), NO service capacity/amperage specified. The sheet shows infrastructure locations but no electrical parameters. No corresponding Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics for this location is present in supplementary documents.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.2 establishes that Austin Energy Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity). Plans cannot show self-determined service specifications; they must be confirmed by AE Design based on site evaluation and customer needs. Sheet 21 lacks these determinations entirely, and no AE Design approval letter providing the determinations is available.

perRunFindings.comment: Plans show service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) without documentation of AE Design determination and approval. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming the service voltage, phases, and capacity shown on Sheet 21 have been determined as available and approved for the site's location and load requirements.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) displays electrical service infrastructure with transformer pads, pull boxes, and service routing. However, no documentation is evident that the service characteristics shown (voltage, phases, capacity) have been determined and approved by AE Design. The plan appears to be applicant-prepared preliminary design rather than responsive to AE Design determinations. No AE Design approval letter confirming the service specifications are available and appropriate for the location is submitted.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.2, AE Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) available at any location. Applicants cannot self-certify service specifications. Plans showing service specifications without documentation of AE Design determination and approval directly violate this code section. The regulatory overview emphasizes this as a common violation pattern (violation #1).

comments.title: Electrical Service Not Identified as Primary or Secondary Voltage
comments.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan does not identify whether the electrical service is primary voltage (AE distribution, ~12.47kV) or secondary voltage (utilization voltage via step-down transformer), and no voltage designations appear on any service lines or equipment.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.3 (One Point of Service and One Service Voltage) requires that plans identify service as primary or secondary. Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad,' overhead existing lines labeled 'OHE,' and proposed underground lines labeled 'Underground Electric Line'—none with voltage designations or primary/secondary identification. Without this designation, Austin Energy cannot determine the service demarcation point (AE responsibility vs. customer responsibility), verify that equipment specifications and clearances are appropriate for the service voltage, or confirm whether the design meets the one-service-voltage requirement.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pads, service connection points, overhead electric lines (OHE), and underground electric line locations on site
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, label each transformer pad as primary or secondary voltage service and identify ownership (AE-owned or customer-owned). Provide a transformer pad schedule specifying kVA ratings and voltage configurations (primary input voltage / secondary output voltage) for each pad. Label the voltage level on all service lines (overhead and underground). Add a one-line diagram or plan note showing voltage levels throughout the distribution system and clarifying AE/customer demarcation.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical service voltage not identified on plans. Specify service voltage (e.g., 120/208V single-phase, 277/480V three-phase) and identify service as primary or secondary to establish regulatory compliance framework and equipment specifications.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 and associated plans show proposed transformer pads and service connection points but do not indicate service voltage or identify the service as primary or secondary. No voltage specification (e.g., 208/120V, 277/480V, primary vs secondary) is labeled anywhere on the electrical design sheets. The existing service connection point on west side is marked as 'Underground Electric Line' without voltage designation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 (One Point of Service and One Service Voltage) is a fundamental requirement for electric service documentation. Service voltage designation determines equipment specifications, clearance requirements, accessibility standards, and regulatory compliance pathways. Without explicit designation of primary or secondary service, the regulatory applicability and compliance path cannot be determined.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical service is not identified as primary or secondary voltage. Please provide: (1) transformer pad schedules identifying kVA ratings and voltage configurations (primary/secondary); (2) service voltage identification on site plan (e.g., '120/208V, 3-phase, 4-wire secondary'); (3) clarification of whether transformers are Austin Energy-owned (customer side) or customer-owned equipment; (4) one-line diagram showing voltage levels throughout the system.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 proposed transformer pads with labels 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but no voltage designation is provided. The transformers are not labeled as serving primary (distribution voltage, typically 12.47kV in Austin) or secondary (service voltage, typically 120/208V or 240/480V) voltage. No notes indicate whether these are primary service transformers or secondary distribution/step-down units. Vision analysis found: 'The Electrical Transformer Pad labels do not include the kVA rating or voltage configurations of the transformers.'
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 specifies that electrical service must be identified with 'one service voltage' and references understanding the service as primary or secondary. The plans must identify whether the shown transformers are AE-owned primary-to-secondary step-down transformers (most typical for residential service) or customer-owned equipment. This distinction is critical for understanding the service point demarcation and compliance with one-service-voltage requirement.

perRunFindings.comment: Service voltage not identified as primary or secondary. Specify on the electrical design plan whether the service is primary voltage (AE-supplied) or secondary voltage (customer-owned transformer), and label the service voltage on all applicable facilities and lines.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground electric lines. Vision analysis indicates that transformers are labeled generically as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' and meters are labeled as 'Electrical Meters' with no additional designation. There are no notes, labels, or callouts indicating whether the service is primary (supplied directly from AE distribution), secondary (from a customer transformer), or specifying the voltage level of the service. The overhead electric lines shown as existing ('OHE') and the proposed underground service have no voltage designations. UCM § 1.3.3 requires that service be identified as primary or secondary, and no such designation appears on the electrical design plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.3 'One Point of Service and One Service Voltage' establishes that plans must identify whether the service is primary (customer receives service at AE's distribution voltage, typically 12.47kV) or secondary (customer receives service at utilization voltage, typically 120/208V or 277/480V via a customer-owned transformer). This designation is fundamental to understanding the service configuration and AE's scope of work vs. customer responsibility. Without this identification, AE cannot determine whether proposed equipment (transformers, metering) is correctly specified, whether clearances are adequate for the service voltage, and whether the service aligns with AE policy.

comments.title: Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual Compliance Not Demonstrated on Electrical Plans
comments.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan contains no UCM compliance notes, undimensioned transformer clearances, and no references to applicable Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual sections, making it impossible to verify that the proposed service routing and equipment placement meet UCM Section 1 requirements.
comments.issue:
LDC § 25-4-200 and UCM Section 1 require that sites connecting to Austin Energy's system demonstrate compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The Master Comment Report identifies eight applicable UCM sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4) plus ECM Appendix F, none of which are referenced on Sheet 21. Specifically missing from the electrical plans:
- No UCM compliance notes or code section references of any kind on Sheet 21
- No dimensioned clearances from transformer pads to buildings, windows/doors, parking areas, or sidewalks per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (required minimums: 10 ft hot-stick use area on padlocked sides; 15 ft facing confined space; 20 ft oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs; 5 ft adjacent brick/masonry building; 12 ft from windows if lateral clearance < 5 ft; 2 ft from back of sidewalk)
- No transformer pad dimensions or equipment specifications (kVA rating, insulation type)
- No bollard specifications for pads within 4 ft of parking or traffic areas (UCM § 1.10.4)
- No conduit sizing or routing documentation meeting UCM standards
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site; all transformer pad locations, pull box locations, underground electric routing, and service connection points
comments.resolution: Revise Sheet 21 to include: (1) UCM compliance notes referencing all applicable sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4, and ECM Appendix F); (2) dimensioned clearances from all transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4; (3) bollard specifications for pads within 4 ft of parking or traffic areas; (4) transformer pad dimensions and kVA/equipment specifications for each pad. Coordinate with Austin Energy Design lead to confirm routing compliance prior to plan approval.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy Design lead to confirm that the proposed routing and equipment placement comply with UCM Section 1 prior to plan approval.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electrical service routing shown on Sheet 21 does not demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). Add UCM compliance notes, dimensioned clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment specifications, and pad details to demonstrate that service routing and equipment placement meet all applicable UCM standards.
applicableAreas: electrical service routing on site plan
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and underground electric lines routed across the site. However, the plan contains no notes, callouts, or documentation referencing Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual requirements or UCM Section 1 compliance. The plan lacks any notation of design compliance with specific UCM standards such as clearances (UCM § 1.10.4), truck access (UCM § 1.3.16), or metering equipment installation (UCM § 1.9.3). Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains general electric notes from Austin Energy but does not address the specific UCM Section 1 routing requirements for the proposed electrical service design shown on Sheet 21.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.13 requires demonstration that 'Proposed electric service routing not shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual' and applies to all sites. The grouping instruction states this requires 'Electrical site plan includes UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment placement meets UCM standards, transformer locations comply with Table 1.10.4 requirements.' The preliminary electrical plan shows the general routing layout but fails to demonstrate compliance through dimensioned clearances, compliance notes, or reference to specific UCM sections.

perRunFindings.comment: Proposed electric service routing not documented as complying with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Verify that the underground service configuration (loop system, clearances, conduit sizing, pull box spacing) meets UCM Section 1 standards and obtain Austin Energy Design lead approval. Include Design Criteria compliance notes on the electrical site plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts the routing of underground electric lines entering the site from Valley View Road on the west and forming an apparent continuous loop around the interior driveways, connecting to four transformer pads and eight meter banks. However, the plan contains no explicit notes or documentation stating that the proposed routing complies with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual specifications (UCM Section 1). The electrical service configuration (whether it is a loop system, radial feed, or dual feed) is not explicitly labeled, though the visual configuration suggests a loop system.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist item EL-19.13 applies to 'All sites' and requires that 'Proposed electric service routing [be] shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual.' The electrical site plan shows the physical routing but does not explicitly document that this routing was designed in accordance with Design Criteria standards. The preliminary design stage and the Master Comment Report indicating ongoing Austin Energy coordination suggest the design may not yet be finalized against these standards.

perRunFindings.comment: Add notes to the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan referencing compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1) and specifically identify which UCM sections govern the proposed service routing (e.g., UCM § 1.3.12 Line Extension Policy, UCM § 1.9.3 Metering Equipment, UCM § 1.10.3 Overhead Line Clearances, UCM § 1.10.4 Padmount Equipment Clearances). Demonstrate that proposed service routing is designed in accordance with these standards.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts proposed electric service routing including four transformer pad locations, underground electric lines connecting to buildings, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the electrical design plan contains zero references to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM), no compliance statements with specific UCM sections (such as § 1.3.12, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4), and no notation of design standard compliance. The Master Comment Report lists required Austin Energy Design Criteria sections (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4) but these standards are not referenced on the electrical sheets themselves.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist deficiency states 'Proposed electric service routing not shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual.' The site plan documents show routing (transformer locations, line paths, connections), but this routing is not explicitly documented as compliant with or designed according to UCM standards. Professional practice requires that electrical service design reference and comply with the applicable design manual. The grouping specifies this is required for 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system,' which applies here.

perRunFindings.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan does not demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). Add to the electrical site plan: (1) dimensioned clearances from all transformer pads to buildings, doors, windows, parking areas, and sidewalks per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4; (2) transformer pad dimensions and specifications; (3) truck access dimensions and bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking; (4) conduit sizing and routing specifications; (5) explicit UCM compliance notes confirming adherence to all applicable sections of UCM Section 1.
applicableAreas: electrical site plan design and specifications
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical infrastructure layout including three transformer pads, underground service lines, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the plan lacks all documentation required to demonstrate compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual: (1) Clearances are not dimensioned; (2) Transformer pad dimensions are not specified; (3) No UCM compliance notes or callouts appear on the electrical plan; (4) No reference to Table 1.10.4 clearance requirements (10 ft hot-stick use area, 15 ft facing confined space, 20 ft from oil-filled equipment to fire escape, 5 ft from windows/doors, 12 ft from windows if lateral <5 ft); (5) No equipment specifications (kVA ratings, voltage, insulation type) are provided; (6) No truck access dimensions or bollard requirements are shown.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.16 specifies 'Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated' and applies to 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system.' The grouping instruction requires 'Electrical site plan includes UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment placement meets UCM standards, transformer locations comply with Table 1.10.4 requirements.' Per LDC § 25-4-200, compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual, UCM Section 1) must be demonstrated.

perRunFindings.comment: Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated on electrical site plan. Add notes to the electrical site plan referencing applicable UCM sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4, Appendix F), dimension clearances per UCM § 1.10.4, and verify all equipment placement meets UCM standards. Coordinate with Austin Energy Design lead to confirm compliance prior to approval.
perRunFindings.observation: The electrical site plan (Sheet 21, labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan') depicts four transformer pads, eight electrical meter locations, pull boxes, and underground electrical lines forming an apparent loop configuration. However, the plan contains no notes or callouts referencing compliance with specific sections of the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). The 'Utility Notes' block on Sheet 21 contains only generic contractor directives. No clearance dimensions are shown for transformer pads relative to buildings or structures. No transformer pad details or specifications are referenced. The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) lists preliminary design requirements including eight specific UCM sections (§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4) plus Appendix F of the Environmental Criteria Manual, but these requirements do not appear to be explicitly addressed on the electrical site plan.
perRunFindings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that sites requiring connection to Austin Energy must demonstrate compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1). The electrical site plan is required to include UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, and equipment placement meeting UCM standards. The preliminary site plan shows electrical infrastructure but lacks documented references to specific Design Criteria Manual sections or evidence that the design has been evaluated against those standards.

perRunFindings.comment: Revise the electrical site plan to include compliance notes referencing specific UCM sections. Dimension clearances around transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4, specifying: (1) hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) = 10 feet minimum clearance, (2) facing confined space (niche/vault) = 15 feet, (3) oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs = 20 feet, (4) adjacent brick/masonry building = 5 feet minimum, (5) adjacent non-brick/masonry building = 12 feet from oil-filled equipment. Add notes confirming equipment pad placement within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck access and specifying bollard requirements if within 4 feet. Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks.
applicableAreas: Electrical service design and equipment placement
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts transformer pad locations, underground electric service routing, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the sheet contains no notes, callouts, or references demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM). No clearances are dimensioned according to UCM § 1.10.4 tables. No equipment placement notes reference specific UCM standards. The transformer pads are shown as generic rectangular symbols with no detail references or specification callouts.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The deficiency states 'Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated.' The electrical design plan shows the proposed infrastructure layout but provides no evidence that this design was created with reference to UCM standards or that it meets those standards. Specificity is required: the sheet must show which UCM sections apply, what the requirements are, and how the proposed design meets them (dimensioned clearances and compliance notes). The absence of all this documentation is the deficiency.

comments.title: Transformer kVA Ratings and Capacity Adequacy Not Documented
comments.comment: Transformer pads on Sheet 21 bear no kVA ratings, and no documentation confirms that total transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units and 8 buildings.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0 requires adequate transformer documentation for Austin Energy coordination. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads (quantity varies between 4 and 5 across review runs) labeled only as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' with no kVA ratings, no assignment of buildings or units to each transformer, and no load distribution analysis confirming that combined capacity meets or exceeds electrical demand. Note: this deficiency overlaps with and is partially addressed by the missing projected load calculations comment; both issues may be resolved concurrently.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: All transformer pads on Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.resolution: Add kVA ratings to each transformer pad symbol on Sheet 21 and include a transformer schedule showing: (1) each transformer's kVA rating; (2) the buildings and units served by each transformer; (3) the load assigned to each transformer; (4) confirmation that combined transformer capacity meets or exceeds calculated electrical demand with appropriate safety margin. This may be resolved concurrently with the load calculations requirement.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (2/3 runs flagged, one as unclear) — verify transformer kVA ratings are absent from Sheet 21 and that the number of transformer pads (4 vs. 5) is consistent across plan sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: Confirm that transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units and 8 buildings. Provide electrical load calculations showing: (1) total electrical demand for the development, (2) the kVA rating of each of the 5 transformers, (3) the total combined capacity, and (4) confirmation that capacity exceeds demand with appropriate safety margin. Show this information on Sheet 21 in a specifications table or notes section.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings with 39 units total. The buildings are described as 4-plexes, 5-plexes, and 6-plexes with gross floor areas ranging from 3,290 sf to 4,997 sf per building. The electrical plan shows 5 transformers but provides no specification indicating: (1) the total capacity of all transformers combined, (2) the electrical demand of all 39 units and 8 buildings, (3) the load distribution among the 5 transformers, or (4) whether the total transformer capacity is adequate to serve all buildings. No transformer sizing analysis or electrical load calculation is provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Transformer capacity must be adequate to serve all buildings in the development. This is a fundamental design requirement. Without showing transformer sizes and confirming that total capacity meets or exceeds the calculated electrical demand for 39 residential units, the adequacy of the electrical service cannot be verified. Austin Energy design review typically requires load calculations demonstrating adequate capacity.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide electrical load calculations showing total connected load and demand for all buildings, and confirm that the proposed four transformers with specified kVA ratings are adequate to serve this load per Austin Energy requirements.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers serving 39 units across 8 buildings. The plan does not include a load calculation or documentation showing that four transformers are adequate to serve all buildings and units. No calculations, Austin Energy requirements letter, or specifications document is provided that confirms transformer capacity (kVA) is sufficient for the project's electrical load.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer documentation must be adequate to support Austin Energy coordination. Without documented electrical load calculations and transformer capacity specifications, it cannot be verified that the proposed transformers are adequate to serve the project. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer quantity not adequate to serve all buildings in development' as a potential deficiency. While four transformers appear reasonable for 39 units, this must be documented with engineering calculations or Austin Energy requirements confirmation.

comments.title: Austin Energy Line Extension Determination and Developer Cost Responsibility Undocumented
comments.comment: Austin Energy's formal determination of whether a line extension is required to serve this development—and the developer's corresponding acknowledgment of financial responsibility for line extension costs—have not been documented in the submitted application.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.12 requires two distinct steps: (1) Austin Energy must formally determine line extension applicability during the ESPA review based on whether adequate AE facilities exist at the proposed service point (this cannot be determined from distance alone), and (2) if a line extension is required, the developer must acknowledge in writing their financial responsibility for all associated costs. The preliminary electrical design (Sheet 21) shows service routing entering from Valley View Road ROW, and Sheet 3 references UCM § 1.3.12, but no ESPA determination letter and no developer cost acknowledgment are present in the submitted documents. The Master Comment Report references AE review via an inaccessible Bluebeam link; the Engineer's Summary Letter does not address electric service planning.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Entire site; Valley View Road service connection point; potential line extension route
comments.resolution: Submit: (1) Austin Energy correspondence (ESPA determination letter or equivalent) confirming whether a line extension is required to serve the proposed 39-unit development; and (2) if a line extension is required, a signed developer acknowledgment of financial responsibility for all line extension costs per UCM § 1.3.12. If AE confirms service is available from existing infrastructure without a line extension, submit that written confirmation.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires Austin Energy Design to make the line extension applicability determination through the ESPA process; AE evaluates based on existing infrastructure capacity and location relative to the proposed service point.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: ESPA review comments are referenced in the Master Comment Report but are only accessible via an inaccessible Bluebeam link — reviewer should obtain and review those AE comments directly.

perRunFindings.comment: AE Design determination of line extension requirements must be documented in ESPA correspondence and referenced on site plans or in approval correspondence.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows service routing with blue line entering from Valley View Road right-of-way on west side, suggesting connection to existing AE infrastructure. However, no explicit documentation found regarding whether line extension is required or not. Master Comment Report references AE Design review via Bluebeam but no ESPA correspondence discussing line extension applicability was located. Engineer's Summary Letter does not address electric service planning. No evidence of AE determination of whether adequate existing facilities exist at proposed service location.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.12 requires discussion of line extension requirements with AE Design. The applicability checklist note specifically states 'Note: Line extension applicability cannot be determined from distance alone—requires Austin Energy determination during ESPA review.' Without access to ESPA correspondence or AE Design approval letters discussing whether line extension is required, cannot verify this item was properly addressed. The preliminary plan routing suggests possible service from existing infrastructure, but without formal AE determination document, status remains unclear.

perRunFindings.comment: Line extension requirements not documented in available correspondence. ESPA determination and line extension decision from Austin Energy Design not visible on site plan or in accessible project correspondence.
applicableAreas: entire site - potential line extension determination
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan shows underground electric lines routing from Valley View Road to the property, and Sheet 3 references Austin Energy Design Criteria including 'UCM § 1.3.12 - AE Line Extension Policy.' However, no specific documentation of ESPA (Electric Service Planning Application) review results, line extension determination, or discussion with Austin Energy Design regarding line extension requirements/fees is visible on the site plan, cover sheet, or in the available correspondence.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The checklist item requires discussion of line extension requirements with Austin Energy Design. The preliminary electrical design assumes service is available from Valley View Road, and the Austin Energy Design Criteria are referenced, but there is no explicit documentation that line extension applicability was discussed with Austin Energy or what determination was made. Per the grouping's Regulatory Overview, 'Line extension determination: Made by Austin Energy during ESPA review based on whether adequate AE facilities exist.' Without access to the ESPA determination or correspondence documenting this discussion, the status cannot be confirmed.

perRunFindings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for line extension not documented. Provide documentation from Austin Energy indicating whether line extension to the site is required and acknowledge developer responsibility for all line extension costs per UCM § 1.3.12.
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan shows new electric service infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground routing on Sheet 21) for a new 39-unit development. This is a new site requiring electric service extension. However, no documentation confirming developer financial responsibility for line extension costs was located. The facts.md does not mention existing electric service at the site, and the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows new infrastructure routing, suggesting line extension is required. No cost responsibility acknowledgment or work order from Austin Energy indicating line extension fees was found.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When line extension is required to provide electric service to a site, the developer must acknowledge financial responsibility for line extension costs per UCM § 1.3.12 (the AE Line Extension Policy). The project shows new electric service infrastructure, which strongly suggests line extension is necessary. Without documentation of cost responsibility acknowledgment or AE correspondence indicating whether line extension is required and who is responsible, this requirement cannot be verified as met. A formal acknowledgment of line extension cost responsibility may be required before site plan approval.

perRunFindings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for line extension not confirmed. Austin Energy must determine whether line extension is required to serve the proposed 39-unit development and provide written determination. If line extension is required, developer must acknowledge financial responsibility in writing. Submit Austin Energy correspondence confirming line extension requirement (or service-only status) and developer's signed acknowledgment of cost responsibility if applicable.
perRunFindings.observation: No correspondence from Austin Energy indicating whether line extension is required or whether service can be provided via existing infrastructure is present in supplementary documents. Master Comment Report Electric Review section references AE site comments on Bluebeam (inaccessible) but contains no summary of line extension determination. No cost responsibility acknowledgment from developer regarding line extension fees is visible. Facts.md notes existing 5-foot electric easements on property suggesting some AE infrastructure may already be present.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.12 requires developer financial responsibility acknowledgment for line extension when required. The determination of whether line extension is necessary requires Austin Energy Design evaluation based on existing infrastructure capacity and location relative to proposed service point. Without correspondence from AE Design confirming line extension necessity (or confirming service can be provided from existing infrastructure), this item cannot be definitively evaluated. The Bluebeam comments may address this but are inaccessible.

comments.title: Developer Cost Responsibility for AE Facility Relocation and System Upgrades Not Documented
comments.comment: No Austin Energy correspondence has been located confirming whether existing AE facilities must be relocated or whether system upgrades are required for this development, and no developer cost responsibility acknowledgment for either scenario has been submitted.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.13 (Excess Facilities/Excess Cost Policy) requires the developer to acknowledge financial responsibility prior to site plan approval for: (1) relocation or removal of existing AE facilities where required by the development — Sheet 3 documents transmission easement requirements and notes existing AE transmission facilities on or near the property, but no AE correspondence identifying relocation scope or costs has been located; and (2) system upgrades (beyond standard line extension) required due to grid overload or capacity limitations — no AE correspondence indicating upgrade requirements was found. If neither applies, AE correspondence confirming this should be on record.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Transmission easement areas along property boundaries; entire site (system capacity assessment)
comments.resolution: Submit the following from Austin Energy Design: (1) If existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed — AE correspondence identifying relocation scope and costs, and developer's signed cost responsibility acknowledgment per UCM § 1.3.13. (2) If system upgrades are required due to grid overload or capacity limitations — AE determination letter and developer's signed upgrade cost acknowledgment per UCM § 1.3.13. (3) If neither relocation nor upgrades are required — AE written confirmation to that effect.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires Austin Energy Design to make formal determinations regarding facility relocation needs and system upgrade requirements; determinations typically originate during the ESPA or service request process.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each) — verify whether existing transmission facilities visible on Sheet 4 along Valley View Road require relocation as part of this development.

perRunFindings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for electric facility relocation or removal not documented. If existing Austin Energy facilities must be relocated or removed for the development, provide cost responsibility acknowledgment per UCM § 1.3.13 and documentation from Austin Energy indicating relocation scope and costs.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents transmission easement requirements and notes that existing electric transmission facilities are on or near the property. However, no documentation confirms whether existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed as part of the development. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed new infrastructure routing but does not document conflicts with existing AE facilities or required relocations. No cost responsibility acknowledgment for facility relocation was located.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When existing AE facilities must be relocated or removed, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13 (Excess Facilities/Excess Cost Policy). Without documentation of existing facility conflicts, relocation requirements, or cost responsibility, the applicability of this item cannot be fully determined. If facility relocation is required, the acknowledgment document is missing.

perRunFindings.comment: No correspondence from Austin Energy identifying required system upgrades found. If Austin Energy has determined that electric system upgrades are required for this development, provide documentation and acknowledge developer financial responsibility for these costs per UCM § 1.3.13.
perRunFindings.observation: No documentation from Austin Energy indicating that system upgrades are required due to area grid overload, capacity limitations, or infrastructure improvements was located in the submitted documents. The facts.md and project documents do not reference any correspondence about substation capacity concerns or required system improvements. Austin Energy's completeness check is marked complete, but no specific indication of required system upgrades was noted.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When AE indicates that system upgrades (beyond standard line extension) are required due to grid overload or capacity limitations, developer financial responsibility must be acknowledged prior to site plan approval per UCM § 1.3.13. This typically comes from Austin Energy as a formal determination during the ESPA or service request process. Without such correspondence from AE, it cannot be determined if upgrades are required or if developer financial responsibility acknowledgment is needed.

comments.title: Electrical Infrastructure Clearances from Detention Pond Not Documented or Verified
comments.comment: The site plan does not document required separation distances between electrical facilities (pull boxes, underground lines) and the biofiltration/detention pond, and no Austin Energy approval of the pond design relative to electrical facility protection is on record.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.0 requires electric facility conflicts with proposed ponds and water features to be resolved per AE criteria. The biofiltration/detention pond is located in the NE corner of the site (Sheet 15), adjacent to electrical easements and drainage easements. Sheet 21 shows pull boxes and underground electric lines routed through the eastern portion of the site in the same area as the pond; Sheet 9 shows drainage easements in the NE area. No documentation shows AE has reviewed and approved the pond design for impacts on electrical facility access, maintenance access, or facility protection. No specific clearance dimensions between electrical pull boxes, underground lines, the pond structure, retaining walls, perimeter fence, or water surface are called out on any sheet.
comments.sheets: Site Plan (Sheet 9); Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations (Sheet 15); Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles (Sheet 16); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Northeast corner — biofiltration/detention pond; eastern site area with underground electrical pull boxes and conduit routing
comments.resolution: Submit Austin Energy Design written approval of the detention pond design relative to protection of, and maintenance access to, electrical facilities per UCM § 1.10.0. Add specific clearance dimensions to Sheet 21 showing measured separation between all pull boxes and underground electric lines and the pond basin edge, retaining walls, perimeter fence, and water surface; confirm all clearances meet AE design criteria.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires Austin Energy Design to confirm required clearance standards and review the pond design for compliance with UCM § 1.10.0 electrical facility protection criteria.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Vision analysis could not definitively measure distance between pull boxes and pond edge on Sheet 21 — reviewer should verify physical clearances on the plan sheet.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facilities conflicts with proposed ponds and water features not resolved per AE criteria. Submit documentation showing Austin Energy Design review and approval of detention pond design relative to protection of electrical facilities and easement access. Address any required clearances, protective measures, or operational constraints related to electrical utilities adjacent to the pond.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheets 15 and 16 show a biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast portion of the site. Sheet 9 shows the pond adjacent to the eastern property boundary where electric easements are located. Sheets 15-16 contain engineering details for the pond including stage-storage calculations, material specifications, and drainage infrastructure. However, there is no documentation showing that Austin Energy has been consulted or has approved the pond design relative to impacts on electrical facilities, easement access, or utility protection.
