comments.title: AE Vehicle Access Routes and Transformer Pad Coordination Details Missing from Plans
comments.comment: Plans do not document Austin Energy vehicle access routes, truck access path specifications, or required transformer pad coordination details, preventing verification that AE personnel can access and maintain all electrical facilities.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(4) requires plans to demonstrate that development preserves Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed facilities; no access routes, widths, turning radii, or clearance zones are marked on the site plan or electrical plan. The following specific deficiencies exist across Sheets 9, 21, 11, and 31:
- Truck access paths are not delineated with required 12-foot horizontal width, 16-foot vertical clearance, and 72,180 lb total vehicle weight capacity from the public right-of-way to each transformer pad
- 20'×35' minimum horizontal clear zones with 35-foot vertical clearance in front of each transformer pad are not shown per UCM § 1.3.16
- Per UCM § 1.16.0(2), AE Design coordination details are absent: measured clearances to existing overhead lines on the west boundary; transformer pad clearances (10-foot minimum on access door side, 5-foot minimum on operator sides); disconnect location and distance from each transformer; bollard and protective barrier details; and mountable curb specifications
- Grading and landscape plans do not confirm that grade changes, retaining walls, fencing, or landscaping will not obstruct AE access routes
- Transmission easement roads are not confirmed to support 46,000 lb tandem axle loading as required by Sheet 3 Block 20 notes
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Grading plan (Sheet 11); Landscape plan (Sheet 31); General Notes (Sheet 3)

comments.resolution:
On Sheet 21 (and cross-referenced on Sheets 9, 11, and 31):
- Delineate truck access paths from the public right-of-way to each transformer pad, dimensioned with 12-foot horizontal width and 16-foot vertical clearance; add a note specifying pavement supports 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight
- Draw and dimension a 20'×35' clear staging zone with 35-foot vertical clearance in front of each transformer pad
- Add the following AE Design coordination callouts to Sheet 21: measured clearances from proposed facilities to existing overhead lines on the west boundary; disconnect location with distance from each transformer; transformer pad clearance dimensions (10-foot minimum on access door side, 5-foot minimum on operator sides); bollard and protective barrier details; and mountable curb specifications
- On Sheets 11 and 31, add notes confirming no grade changes, landscaping, or barriers obstruct AE access routes; confirm transmission easement road pavement supports 46,000 lb tandem axle loading

comments.title: Point of Service Connection to Existing AE Infrastructure Not Labeled on Plans
comments.comment: The electrical design plan does not identify the specific point where the proposed electrical system connects to existing Austin Energy infrastructure, and the demarcation between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities is not shown.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(5) requires the point of service to be identified with one service voltage; UCM § 1.3.3 defines the point of service as the demarcation between AE-owned and customer-owned facilities. comments.title: Transmission Easement Not Depicted and AE Transmission Engineering Review Not Documented
comments.comment: The transmission easement boundary is not drawn on the site plan or electrical design plan, and there is no evidence in the submitted materials that Austin Energy Transmission engineering review has been completed.
comments.issue:

Sheet 3 (Block 20) documents extensive transmission easement coordination requirements — including 25-foot structure clearances, grading coordination, fencing requirements, and mandatory pre-construction safety meetings with Andrew Perez (512-505-7153) — confirming the applicability threshold is met. Despite this:

- No AE Transmission engineering review approval letter, stamp, or documentation is present in the submitted site plan materials

comments.title: Transformer Pads 2 and 3 Inside Gated Perimeter Prevent Unrestricted 24/7 AE Access
comments.comment: Transformers 2 and 3 are located inside the gated property perimeter, preventing Austin Energy from having the unrestricted 24/7 emergency and maintenance access required by code.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.11.1 require all AE electrical equipment to be accessible 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Sheet 9 shows an entrance gate and exit gate on the western boundary at Valley View Road; Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Buildings 4 and 5) and Transformer 3 (southeastern corner, south of Building 6) are situated deep within the gated residential perimeter. AE personnel would require gate access codes or keys to reach these units during emergencies or for routine maintenance, violating the unrestricted access requirement. No easement, exception, or emergency access procedure is documented in the submitted plans to address this condition.

comments.applicableArea: Transformer pads 2 and 3 within gated perimeter; entrance and exit gates on western property boundary at Valley View Road
comments.resolution: Provide one of the following to resolve the 24/7 access requirement for Transformer 2 and Transformer 3: (1) relocate both transformers outside the gated perimeter with direct, unrestricted truck access from Valley View Road; (2) record and submit a permanent easement document granting Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 property access regardless of gate status; or (3) obtain and submit documented written approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing the gated configuration with specific emergency access procedures.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify gate and transformer locations on Sheet 9 and confirm whether Transformers 1 and 4 at or near the gate line have adequate unrestricted access before determining scope of required correction.

comments.title: Meter Sight-Line to Transformer Not Documented on Plans

The "within sight" standard in UCM § 1.9.3.1.B does not specify a maximum distance, but direct visual contact is required. Building walls and structures between meters and transformers may obstruct sightlines for some of the eight meter locations.

comments.title: Austin Energy ESPA Documentation for Line Extension Determination Not Provided
comments.comment: No Austin Energy ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service has been submitted to confirm whether a line extension is required to serve the site.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.3.12 and UCM § 1.16.0(6) require documentation of Austin Energy's determination of whether the proposed electric service requires a line extension (customer-funded infrastructure extension, with associated Contributions in Aid of Construction / CIAC) versus a service-only connection to existing nearby infrastructure. Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing from the existing right-of-way at Valley View Road to transformer pads and building meter locations, but contains no line extension notation, CIAC reference, or service classification. Whether a line extension is required cannot be determined from plan analysis alone — this determination is made exclusively by Austin Energy Design during ESPA review based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. The Master Comment Report references AE completeness check as complete, but the actual ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement is not present in the project file.

If a line extension is required, show its full extent on Sheet 21 and document any associated CIAC or line extension fees. If the service qualifies as a service-only connection, note this determination on Sheet 21.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires coordination with Austin Energy Design and Distribution — line extension determination is made exclusively by Austin Energy during ESPA review and cannot be verified from submitted plan documents.

comments.title: Austin Energy Service Territory and Dual-Service Area Not Confirmed
comments.comment: The project file does not include explicit written confirmation that the site at 3759 Valley View Road is within Austin Energy's electrical service territory, and no documentation addresses whether the site falls in a dual-service area shared with another utility provider.
comments.issue: Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 establishes Austin Energy's service territory boundaries; plans referencing Austin Energy standards must be within that territory, and plans outside AE territory must remove all AE references. Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act (state law) requires a PUC Service Area Exception Application when a customer in a dual-service area requests service from the non-territorial provider. While the site is in City of Austin full-purpose jurisdiction and the submission references Austin Energy design criteria throughout (Sheet 3 transmission clearances, electric review in Master Comment Report), explicit service territory confirmation and dual-service area determination are absent from the submission. No service territory map, provider selection documentation, or PUC application is present in the project file.

comments.applicableArea: 3759 Valley View Road site; service territory boundary determination for electrical service provider
comments.resolution: Provide written documentation confirming the site at 3759 Valley View Road is within Austin Energy's exclusive electrical service territory. If the site is located in a dual-service area where both Austin Energy and another provider operate, provide either (a) documentation of service provider selection, or (b) a completed PUC Service Area Exception Application if non-territorial service is requested under the Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act. If within AE's exclusive territory, a brief written confirmation from Austin Energy or notation on the plans is sufficient.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: May involve Austin Energy Customer Service for territory confirmation; PUC Service Area Exception Applications are a state-level process under the Texas Public Utility Commission.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — full-purpose City of Austin jurisdiction and pervasive AE references on plans make non-AE territory unlikely, but reviewer should confirm service territory status formally.

comments.issue: Code of Ordinances § 15-9-123 establishes that customer-owned conduit and cable on the load side of the meter are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy jurisdiction, and should not be submitted for Austin Energy approval. The preliminary electrical design on Sheet 21 shows high-level service routing including transformer locations, underground lines, pull boxes, and eight meter locations, but does not label or distinguish the AE-to-customer ownership transition point at any meter location. This ambiguity may result in improper submittal routing during building permit review.

Carry this delineation forward into building electrical plans during the building permit stage.

comments.title: Austin Energy Notes Section Missing Three Required Notes
comments.comment: The Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3 is missing three required notes: a conceptual-design disclaimer, a plan-change notification requirement, and a developer conduit responsibility statement.
comments.issue:
AEDC 1.16.0 and AEDC 1.3.0 require the following notes, none of which appear in the current Electric Notes sections on Sheets 3 or 21:
- **Conceptual disclaimer (AEDC 1.16.0):** A statement that electric facilities shown are conceptual only, should not be used for bidding purposes, and that final electric design by Austin Energy may vary and may require changes to the site plan. Sheet 21's title includes the word 'Preliminary' but this alone does not satisfy the required disclaimer note.
- **Plan-change notification (AEDC 1.16.0):** A statement that Austin Energy must review any changes to plans that may affect electric requirements, including changes in building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, and spoil site locations. Transmission Note #2 (grading coordination near transmission facilities) is insufficient — it covers only transmission coordination and omits all other required change types.
- **Developer conduit responsibility (AEDC 1.3.0):** A statement that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, including conductor installation if applicable, coordination with other utilities to resolve conflicts, and that all costs are the applicant's responsibility. Sheet 21 shows developer-designed underground electric routing, transformer pads, pull boxes, and connections to eight buildings, making this note directly applicable.
comments.sheets: General Notes (Sheet 3); Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21)
comments.applicableArea: Sheet 3, Austin Energy Notes section (Blocks 8 and 14); Sheet 21, Utility Notes (Block 6) and all sheets showing Austin Energy service
comments.resolution:
Add the following three notes to the Austin Energy Notes section on Sheet 3 (and reference on Sheet 21 as applicable):
- **Conceptual disclaimer:** 'Electric facilities shown are conceptual in nature and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown and may require changes to the site plan.'
- **Plan-change notification:** 'Austin Energy must review any changes to plans that may affect electric requirements, including changes in building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, and spoil site locations.'
- **Developer conduit responsibility:** 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet the current Austin Energy (AE) Design Criteria Manual, including the installation of conductors if determined during the design process (prior to the issuance of the building permit) that the developer will fund the installation cost of the conductors. The Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve all conflicts. All costs associated with these improvements will be the responsibility of the applicant.'

The Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve all conflicts. All costs associated with these improvements will be the responsibility of the applicant.'

comments.title: Electric Transmission Notes Included Without Transmission Infrastructure on Site
comments.comment: Sheet 3 includes 16 Electric Transmission Notes, but the site plan shows no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements that would make these notes applicable.

The site plan (Sheet 9) shows only 5-foot distribution electric easements and standard overhead distribution lines (OHE notation); no transmission towers, structures, poles, or transmission easements are present per visual analysis and facts on record. Including 16 detailed transmission notes addressing 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 25-foot clearance zones, transmission easement road requirements, and OSHA transmission safety when no transmission infrastructure is shown constitutes inclusion of inapplicable requirements that may confuse contractors.

comments.resolution: Remove the 16 Electric Transmission Notes (Block 20 on Sheet 3) unless transmission infrastructure or a transmission easement is confirmed to be present on or within 100 feet of the site. If transmission facilities are nearby, provide a specific Austin Energy coordination letter confirming transmission proximity before retaining the notes.

comments.title: Buildings 1–8 Missing Overhead Electric Clearance Documentation
comments.comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey, conductor type identification, or building elevation/section views have been provided to verify that Buildings 1–8 and their projections maintain required clearances from overhead electric lines on the western (Valley View Road ROW) and southern boundaries.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities to maintain 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from the outside conductor of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The following documentation is absent:
- Conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not identified on any plan sheet; this distinction is required to determine which clearance standard applies
- No registered surveyor proximity survey documents radial distances from outside conductor to buildings, site features, parking areas, or driveways along the western or southern boundaries
- No building elevation or section views demonstrate 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances for building faces and projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs, HVAC penetrations) for any of Buildings 1–8
- No surveyed conductor elevation data is included anywhere in the 39-sheet set
comments.sheets: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4); Site plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Buildings 1–8 and all building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs); western boundary OHE along Valley View Road ROW (Buildings 1, 2, 8 at approximately 26.1–26.6 ft from western property line); southern boundary OHE line (Buildings 7, 8 and adjacent parking, driveways, site improvements)
comments.resolution:
Submit the following to verify compliance:
- Label conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on all plan sheets depicting overhead electric lines
- Provide a registered surveyor proximity survey documenting surveyed conductor elevations and radial distances from the outside conductor to all proposed building faces, projections, and site improvements along both the western (Valley View Road ROW) and southern OHE boundaries
- Provide building elevation or cross-section views for all buildings within proximity of OHE lines with dimension annotations confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor to all outermost projections
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Surveyed conductor elevation data typically requires coordination with Austin Energy to obtain existing conductor height and location information for the registered surveyor proximity survey.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Unclear status; verify whether a registered surveyor proximity survey or conductor elevation data was submitted separately outside the 39-sheet plan set.

perRunFindings.comment: Plan documentation required: (1) identification of existing conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on overhead lines; (2) dimension annotations showing minimum 15-foot radial clearance from buildings and other customer facilities to the outside conductor of distribution primary and neutral conductors; (3) clarification of whether existing lines are distribution or transmission voltage.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 in relation to distribution primary and neutral conductors on western and southern boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Sheets 4, 9, and 21 confirm existing overhead electric (O.H.U.L.) facilities adjacent to the property. However, the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not labeled or identified on any plans. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies specifically to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No dimension annotations show radial clearances from any building or customer facility to these conductors. No plan notes identify whether the existing lines are distribution (voltage <60kV) or transmission (voltage ≥60kV), and no conductor types are labeled.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (including buildings) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of distribution primary and neutral conductors. Without identification of conductor types and without dimension annotations showing radial clearances from buildings to the conductors, compliance cannot be verified. The 15-foot clearance measurement requires identification of which conductors are primary/neutral vs. secondary, and this distinction is absent from the plans.

perRunFindings.comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey provided showing distances from proposed parking areas and site features to outside conductor of OHE line. Provide proximity survey documenting radial clearances from all customer facilities.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and site features on southern portion near OHE line
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 shows existing OHE line with associated utility poles. Sheet 9 shows the same OHE line routing along the southern boundary with parking areas, driveways, and site improvements in close proximity. The plans do not specify whether the overhead line serves distribution or transmission function, nor are the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) identified. No dimension annotations are provided showing distances from site facilities (parking, driveways, retaining walls) to the outside conductor. A registered surveyor proximity survey documenting existing and proposed facility locations relative to the OHE line is not provided.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (parking, driveways, site improvements) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The distinction between distribution and transmission affects the applicable clearance standard. Without a registered surveyor proximity survey showing the conductor type, voltage level, and radial distances from all proposed facilities, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant has not submitted this required documentation.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevation or section exhibits are required showing all projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) with dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of projections, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs) for Buildings 1-8
perRunFindings.observation: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows buildings 1-8 with footprints and general layout, but no section views or elevation drawings depicting building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead electric conductors. No surveyed conductor elevations are provided. Building architectural details or elevations showing projection dimensions are not included in the 39-sheet set.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires building projections to maintain both (1) 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors. Without section views or elevation drawings showing the vertical and horizontal relationships between building projections and the overhead conductors, and without surveyed conductor elevation data, compliance with these requirements cannot be verified. Buildings can only be shown in plan view without cross-sections showing their height relative to conductor height.

perRunFindings.comment: No building elevation or profile sheets provided showing vertical clearances from Building 8 roof and overhangs to overhead electric line. Provide engineered building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Building 8 roof and overhang areas adjacent to southern OHE line
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 shows Building 8 positioned adjacent to the southern boundary where the OHE line is routed. However, no building elevation or section views are provided on the site plan set that show the roof elevation of Building 8, any rooftop projections (overhangs, canopies, HVAC penetrations, vents), or their vertical clearance from the overhead line. No profile sections are provided showing the relationship between building projections and the conductor location. Building height is specified as 36'-1" but the finished floor and roof elevations are not dimensioned relative to the OHE line.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance (horizontal) and implies vertical clearance verification for any building projections. Without profile or elevation sheets showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the building roof/overhang elevation dimensioned relative to that conductor, compliance cannot be determined. The applicant must provide elevation views with clearance dimensions for all building projections near the overhead line.

perRunFindings.comment: Surveyed elevations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations from the outside conductor to building faces are required, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from electric facilities in the adjacent Valley View Road right-of-way.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, 8 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead utility lines and utility poles along Valley View Road (western boundary). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1, 2, and 8 positioned near the western property line adjacent to Valley View Road ROW. Building 1 is dimensioned at 26.1' from the western property line; Building 8 at 26.6'. However, NO surveyed conductor elevation data is shown, NO dimension annotations show clearances from buildings to the outside conductor, and NO section views demonstrate that permanent 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from electric facilities in the adjacent ROW.
perRunFindings.reasoning: No surveyed elevation data or clearance dimensions provided showing that buildings adjacent to Valley View Road maintain required permanent clearances from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities in ROW. Proximity survey data by registered surveyor is needed.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed structures and overhead electric conductors. Provide building elevation sheets showing electric poles, cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide), and overhead conductors with dimensions confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities along western property boundary
Overhead electric facilities along southern property boundary
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line running along the southern boundary. Sheets 9 and 31 show the building footprints and layouts throughout the site. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal to verify the three-dimensional clearance between the proposed buildings and the overhead conductors. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that overhead electric facilities are shown along boundaries but no elevation views or clearance exhibits are provided. The buildings shown on the site plan and landscape plan would need elevation drawings to verify they maintain the required 7.5-foot horizontal clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes permanent clearance requirements from AE overhead distribution lines (7.5 feet horizontal, 15-foot radius). To verify compliance with these clearance requirements, building elevations must be provided showing the position of overhead conductors, poles, and cross arms relative to the proposed structures. The site plan shows the overhead facilities and building locations in plan view, but without elevation views and clearance exhibits, the three-dimensional clearance relationships cannot be determined. The 'Preliminary' designation of the electrical design may indicate coordination with Austin Energy is ongoing, but the site plan should include the necessary views to verify this critical clearance requirement. Without building elevation sheets showing these facilities, the deficiency status cannot be changed from 'unclear' to 'pass'.

comments.title: Retaining Walls Missing Overhead Electric Clearance Exhibits
comments.comment: Retaining wall section exhibits (Sheets 38–39) and the grading plan (Sheet 11) do not document clearances from the outside overhead conductor to the outermost edges of the walls, and surveyed conductor elevations are absent from all wall sections.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.10.3 requires that retaining walls maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines, and that section exhibits show dimension lines from the conductor to the outermost wall edge (top and face). The following documentation is missing:
- Wall section exhibits on Sheets 38–39 show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure details; no dimension lines are shown from any overhead conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of any wall, and surveyed conductor locations are not depicted
- Grading plan (Sheet 11) shows retaining walls labeled along property boundaries near 5-foot and 15-foot electric easements but does not label wall top and bottom elevations in those areas or show toe and heel footing configuration relative to the OHE line
- Walls along the southern boundary reach up to 14 feet in height; horizontal clearance to the OHE conductor cannot be verified without conductor elevation data cross-referenced on the wall sections
comments.sheets: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4); Site plan (Sheet 9); Grading plan (Sheet 11); Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21); Wall plan (Sheet 38); Wall plan details and notes (Sheet 39)
comments.applicableArea: Retaining walls along southern property boundary (behind Buildings 7 and 8, up to 14 feet tall); retaining walls along eastern boundary (behind Buildings 5 and 6, existing wall to be replaced); retaining walls in northeast corner (adjacent to biofiltration/detention pond); areas near 5-foot and 15-foot electric easements shown on grading plan (Sheet 11)
comments.resolution: Revise retaining wall section exhibits on Sheets 38–39 to include: (1) the surveyed overhead conductor elevation shown on each section where walls are adjacent to OHE lines; (2) dimension lines from the outside conductor to the outermost edge (top and face) of the wall; and (3) a note or dimension confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. On the grading plan (Sheet 11), add wall top and bottom elevations for all walls located near electric easements and show footing configuration (toe and heel details) sufficient to verify the clearance requirement.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Surveyed conductor elevation data for the overhead line along the southern boundary may require coordination with Austin Energy to obtain existing conductor height information.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each for EL-1.14, EL-1.17, EL-12.31); however, EL-1.17 was flagged as 'fail' — verify that Sheets 38–39 contain no conductor clearance dimensions before downgrading.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide section views of retaining walls showing the surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clearance dimensions (measured horizontally) from the outside conductor location to the near face of the retaining wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls, particularly along southern property boundary where OHE line is located
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows retaining walls labeled 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall' along the southern boundary and other site perimeter locations. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) shows an overhead electric line (O.H.U.L.) running along the southern property boundary. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans) provide wall construction sections showing max 14-foot height, reinforcement details, and structural dimensions, but contain NO sections showing clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor to the wall face or top. Wall plan sheets show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure calculations, not clearances to adjacent overhead lines.
perRunFindings.reasoning: The requirement under UCM § 1.10.3 is to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. Retaining walls up to 14 feet tall are proposed along the southern boundary where overhead electric lines are present. Without section views showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the distance (measured horizontally at ground level) from the conductor to the wall face, compliance cannot be verified. The wall height is known (up to 14 feet from foundation), but the conductor height and horizontal distance from the conductor to the wall are not documented.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide section view exhibits of each retaining wall showing the surveyed outside conductor location with dimension lines to the outermost edge (top/face) of the wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the conductor to the wall.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric facilities on southern and eastern boundaries
perRunFindings.observation: Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans and Wall Details) contain section views of retaining walls showing structural reinforcement, backfill requirements, footing details, and maximum heights (14 feet). However, these section views show only internal wall construction and soil pressure relationships. NO section views include dimension lines showing clearance from an outer electric conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of the retaining wall. Sheet 9 shows OHE line along southern boundary, but Sheets 38-39 do not cross-reference or show the conductor on their wall sections.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifically requires 'Retaining walls lack section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall for clearance verification' to be addressed. This is an explicit documentation requirement. The wall construction sections present on Sheets 38-39 do not show the overhead conductor location or clearance dimensions from the conductor to the wall. The requirement is for section exhibits that include both the wall profile AND the conductor location with a dimensioned clearance.

perRunFindings.comment: Retaining wall heights and footing details near electric easements not clearly documented on grading plan. Provide wall top and bottom elevations on grading plan for walls located near overhead electric easements, with detailed cross-sections showing toe and heel footing configuration to verify clearance compliance per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls along property boundaries near electric easements
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows retaining walls labeled along property boundaries: 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall', 'Tie into existing Retaining Wall Match existing Wall Elevations', 'Existing Retaining Wall', and 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced'. The grading plan also shows electric easements ('5' Electric Easement', '15' Electric Easement') in the same boundary areas where retaining walls are located. However, the retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) are not clearly labeled on the grading plan in the areas near the electric easements. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plan Details and Notes) would contain the detailed wall cross-sections and footing details. These details must be reviewed to determine if wall elevations and footing details near overhead electric facilities are adequately documented.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that retaining wall heights and footing details be shown on grading plans when walls are proposed near overhead electric facilities to verify that the wall construction does not create clearance violations. The grouping specifies that 'Retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) not shown on grading plans or toe and heel footing details not provided for retaining walls near overhead electric facilities' is a deficiency. While walls are shown on Sheet 11 near electric easements, the specific top and bottom elevations are not clearly called out in those boundary areas. Whether detailed wall sections on Sheets 38-39 adequately document these clearances requires visual examination. The unclear status reflects uncertainty about whether the detail sheets (38-39) contain the required information.

comments.title: Parking Areas Lack Vertical Clearance Verification from Overhead Lines
comments.comment: No section views or surveyed conductor elevations are provided to verify that parking areas maintain the minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines required for the applicable parking type.

The site includes 88 parking spaces (10 surface, 78 garage). No section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to finished parking surfaces, no surveyed conductor heights are provided on the grading plan (Sheet 11), and no site plan note designates the parking areas as truck or non-truck to establish the applicable clearance standard.
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Grading plan (Sheet 11)
comments.applicableArea: Surface parking areas (10 spaces) and garage parking areas (78 spaces) beneath or within proximity of overhead electric lines along the western and southern boundaries
comments.resolution: Add a note to the site plan (Sheet 9) designating each parking area as truck or non-truck traffic and specifying the applicable minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for non-truck; 18 feet for truck). Provide section views showing surveyed conductor elevation above the finished parking surface with dimension annotations confirming the required vertical clearance is met. Include the surveyed conductor height data on the grading plan (Sheet 11) for all areas where overhead lines pass over or near parking.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Surveyed conductor elevation data for overhead lines near parking areas may require coordination with Austin Energy.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether any conductor clearance sections or a site plan note addressing parking clearance were submitted outside the 39-sheet plan set.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide section views of parking areas with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, or 18 feet for areas with truck traffic) from lowest point of conductors to finished parking surface. Add note to site plan specifying clearance requirement and designation of parking areas (truck vs. non-truck traffic).
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas beneath overhead electric lines
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces for a total of 88 spaces (per site plan data table). The parking layout is shown on the plan view, but NO section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to the parking surface. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows parking pad elevations and site topography but does not provide surveyed conductor heights or clearance verification. No note on site plan indicates the vertical clearance requirement or that parking must maintain minimum clearance from overhead lines.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires parking areas to maintain minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic). Without surveyed conductor elevations and section views showing the vertical relationship between parking pads and conductors, compliance cannot be verified. Additionally, a site plan note is required indicating the clearance requirement. No such note is present on Sheets 9 or 11.

comments.title: Exterior Lighting Plan Missing Overhead Electric Clearance Dimensions
comments.comment: No photometric or detailed lighting plan is provided showing proposed exterior fixture locations with clearance dimensions from overhead electric conductors, leaving compliance with overhead line clearance requirements unverifiable.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.3 requires decorative or exterior lighting proposed beneath or within the clearance zone of overhead electric lines to maintain 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from the outside conductor, or to be relocated. The site plan includes a lighting note on Sheet 9 addressing full cut-off shielding per Subchapter E § 2.5, but this note addresses light design standards only and does not address conductor clearances. No detailed lighting plan or photometric plan showing fixture locations with clearance dimensions from the overhead conductors is included in the 39-sheet submittal.
comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Landscape plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site, particularly those located beneath or within proximity of overhead electric lines on the western (Valley View Road ROW) and southern boundaries
comments.resolution: Provide a detailed photometric or lighting layout plan showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimension annotations from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that all fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from outside conductors; or (3) relocation notes for any fixtures that cannot meet the clearance requirements. Add a note to the site plan stating the applicable overhead line clearance requirement for exterior lighting.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — verify whether a photometric plan or lighting layout with conductor clearance dimensions was submitted as a supplementary document outside the 39-sheet plan set.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide detailed photometric plan or lighting layout showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances, OR; (3) relocation notes if fixtures cannot meet clearance requirements. Include note on site plan indicating clearance requirement for lighting.
applicableAreas: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan, Block 2) includes a 'Lighting Note' requiring all exterior lighting to be 'full cut-off and fully shielded in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5' and providing 'Figure 34: Examples of Fully-Shielded Light Fixtures.' This addresses design standards for light shielding but does NOT address clearances from overhead electric lines. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the site layout with various landscape elements but does not include dimension annotations showing horizontal or vertical clearances from proposed light fixtures to overhead electric lines. The site plan shows a general requirement for 'full cut-off' lighting compliance but does not identify where exterior lighting fixtures will be located or provide clearance verification from overhead conductors. Without a detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations and without clearance dimensions from conductors, compliance cannot be verified. If lighting is proposed beneath or within 15 feet of overhead conductors, relocation or clearance documentation is required.

comments.comment: No clearance dimensions or verification notes are provided confirming that retaining walls along the site perimeter maintain the required 5-foot minimum horizontal separation from underground electric duct banks.

comments.sheets: Site plan (Sheet 9); Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21); Wall plan (Sheet 38)

perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies multiple retaining wall segments throughout the site: a concrete retaining wall in the northeast corner along the biofiltration/detention pond, an existing retaining wall to be replaced along the entire eastern edge behind Buildings 5 and 6, and concrete retaining walls along the southern perimeter behind Buildings 7 and 8. perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that permanent structures (including retaining walls) maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric duct banks. The site plan shows both retaining walls and electric line routing in proximity to each other, but provides no documentation that this clearance requirement has been addressed. The absence of clearance dimensions or verification notes is a deficiency—required information is missing from the plans. While the general contractor verification notes reference utility coordination, they do not substitute for plan-based documentation showing that the clearance requirement has been satisfied.

comments.title: Austin Energy Formal Approval of Electrical System Plans Not Obtained
comments.comment: No formal Austin Energy approval letter or stamped electrical site plan has been submitted; the electrical design is labeled 'preliminary' with no AE approval documentation, despite the project requiring connection to the Austin Energy system.
comments.issue: LDC § 25-4-200 requires all electric system plans for sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system to obtain formal AE approval prior to site plan approval. UCM § 1.16.0 additionally requires proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electric design. Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no AE approval stamp or signature. The Master Comment Report references AE design comments via an inaccessible Bluebeam link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), and the completeness check is marked complete by Victor Givens, but neither constitutes substantive design approval — a completeness check is an administrative procedural step, not plan approval. Sheet 1 shows empty approval stamp boxes with no Austin Energy approval date recorded. The site is within Austin Energy's service territory, within 200 feet of existing AE transmission components, and proposes new electrical service to 39 units, triggering the mandatory approval requirement.
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: Electric system design and approval; entire site within Austin Energy service territory; site within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy transmission components
comments.resolution:
Obtain and submit formal Austin Energy design approval, including:
- A signed Austin Energy approval letter from AE Design (Rosemary Avila or assigned designer) confirming review and approval of the electrical design shown on Sheet 21
- A stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval seal or signature
- ESPA (Electric Service Planning Application) approval documentation

The approval must confirm compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1), including UCM §§ 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3, and 1.10.10.4 cited in the Master Comment Report's Electric Review section.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires coordination with Austin Energy's Design department (Rosemary Avila / Victor Givens). Austin Energy must formally review and approve the electrical design and issue a stamped approval letter and ESPA documentation before this deficiency can be closed.

perRunFindings.comment: Proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design not provided. Provide copies of all email or letter correspondence with AE Design confirming approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.
perRunFindings.observation: The Master Comment Report includes an Electric Review section indicating that Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements. This suggests some level of AE Design coordination. However, no formal correspondence or proof of AE Design approval of the preliminary electric design was located in the supplementary documents package. The review comments exist in an external Bluebeam link (which is not accessible in the submitted documentation), and the completeness check confirms AE completed their review, but specific design approval letters or correspondence confirming acceptance of the preliminary design are not documented.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design. This is a standard requirement when AE Design coordination is needed for infrastructure work, pole relocation, or facility modifications. The Master Comment Report suggests design coordination occurred, but the specific correspondence documenting design approval is not provided in the submittal. Completeness check completion does not constitute design approval—it is merely an administrative confirmation that AE reviewed the application.

perRunFindings.comment: Proof of correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electrical design not submitted. perRunFindings.observation: Master Comment Report (02-electric-review.md) references AE site comments on a Bluebeam link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw) but this link is inaccessible to reviewer. No direct correspondence or approval letter from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electrical design shown on Sheet 21 is present in supplementary documents. Sheet 21 itself contains no approval stamps or reference to AE correspondence.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary design for all sites requiring AE Design coordination. This project clearly requires AE Design review (new service to 39 units, transmission line crossing property). While the Master Comment Report acknowledges that AE has reviewed comments (available on Bluebeam), the formal approval correspondence itself is not available in the submitted documentation. The preliminary designation of Sheet 21 and absence of AE approval signature/stamp indicates formal approval has not been provided in documentable form.

perRunFindings.comment: Proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design not submitted. Provide written AE Design approval letter confirming review and approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.
perRunFindings.observation: Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements and completed completeness check. However, no formal correspondence or approval letter from AE Design is located in supplementary documents confirming that the preliminary electric design (Sheet 21) has been reviewed and approved by AE Design. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam link for AE site comments, but no downloaded AE Design approval letter is evident in the submittal package.
perRunFindings.reasoning: Projects requiring AE Design coordination must submit proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electric design per UCM § 1.16.0. The completion of a completeness check does not equate to design approval. Design approval documentation is required to verify that AE Design has reviewed and approved the electric design shown on Sheet 21.

perRunFindings.comment: No Austin Energy approval letter or stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval has been obtained. Submit the proposed Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to Austin Energy for formal review and approval per LDC § 25-4-200, and provide the signed approval letter and stamped electrical site plan with final application submission.
perRunFindings.observation: The site is located in Austin, TX (3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704) within Austin Energy's service territory, as confirmed by the presence of Austin Energy Electric Notes and Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3 and the identification of Austin Energy as the electrical service provider in the Master Comment Report (Rosemary Avila, Austin Energy). Sheet 21 shows a proposed electrical design with transformers, meters, and underground service lines. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy conducted a design review through Rosemary Avila with reference to a Bluebeam review link. However, no formal Austin Energy approval letter is present in the supplementary documents. No stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval seal or signature is visible. The site is within 200 feet of Austin Energy components per the transmission easement notation, triggering the approval requirement.
perRunFindings.reasoning: EL-19.15 specifies 'Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy not obtained' and applies to 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system or within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components.' LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'All electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' While the Master Comment Report documents that Austin Energy conducted a review (with comments on Bluebeam), this does not constitute formal approval. No approval letter, stamped plan, or ESPA approval documentation appears in the accessible supplementary documents. The electrical site plan is marked as preliminary, and formal Austin Energy approval is required before the design can be finalized.

perRunFindings.comment: Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy has not been obtained. Site plan is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and is in first-round comment response phase. An approved/stamped electrical site plan with documented Austin Energy approval letter must be submitted prior to site plan approval, demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan submittal is at the first-round comment response phase (SP-2025-0126C submitted 05/20/2025). The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements through a Bluebeam markup link and lists multiple UCM sections that must be addressed (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4). However, no signed Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, or formal approval documentation is visible in the supplementary documents reviewed. Sheet 1 (Cover) shows empty approval stamp boxes with no Austin Energy approval date recorded. The electrical site plan (Sheet 21) is labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no indication of Austin Energy Design sign-off.
perRunFindings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy prior to site plan approval. Evidence of preliminary design comments from Austin Energy exists (Master Comment Report references Bluebeam markup), but no formal approval letter or stamped approval documentation is visible. The site plan status indicates it is still awaiting first-round comment response, which means Austin Energy approval has not yet been obtained.

perRunFindings.comment: Obtain and submit a stamped Austin Energy approval letter for the electrical site plan and the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval per LDC § 25-4-200. The approval must address the proposed electric system design and confirm compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' (emphasis on preliminary). The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' from Victor Givens (Austin Energy), indicating completeness review has occurred. However, no stamped Austin Energy approval letter is provided in the submitted documentation. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references a Bluebeam link for Austin Energy comments (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), but the actual Austin Energy approval letter and stamped electrical site plan required by LDC § 25-4-200 are not included.
perRunFindings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' The statute mandates approval, not merely preliminary review. The submission of a 'Preliminary' electrical design plan without an accompanying Austin Energy approval letter does not satisfy this requirement. The completeness check confirmation indicates that Austin Energy has reviewed the plans for completeness (procedural conformance), but approval (substantive compliance with design standards) is a separate and more rigorous determination.

comments.title: Austin Energy Service Availability Letter Not Submitted

comments.issue: Reviewer Convention requires a letter from Austin Energy confirming utility service availability and identifying any necessary easements or service upgrades as a prerequisite to site plan approval. Water and wastewater utilities have 'Suitable and Sufficient Existing Service' approval letters documented on Sheet 3, but no equivalent AE service verification letter is present for the proposed 39-unit residential development. For a site with a transmission easement crossing and new electrical service requirements, Austin Energy must formally confirm service availability and any required infrastructure upgrades or easements.

comments.title: Proximity Survey for AE Primary Voltage Facilities Not Provided
comments.comment: No survey documenting distances between proposed customer facilities and existing Austin Energy primary voltage facilities has been submitted, despite the project's proximity to AE transmission infrastructure with documented 20–25-foot clearance requirements.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that when AE Design requests a proximity survey, one must be provided showing distances from the customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities. Sheet 21 shows proposed electrical infrastructure without proximity dimensions to existing AE primary voltage lines. Transmission easements are present on the property, and Sheet 3 (General Notes) documents 20–25-foot clearance requirements from transmission structures, suggesting AE Design may have required this survey. No proximity survey is present in the supplementary documents.

comments.applicableArea: AE primary voltage facility clearances; areas with existing or proposed AE primary voltage and transmission facilities on site
comments.resolution: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether a proximity survey has been formally requested for this project. If requested, submit a professional survey documenting clearance distances between all proposed buildings, utilities, and equipment and existing AE primary voltage transmission facilities, demonstrating compliance with the 20–25-foot clearance requirements noted on Sheet 3.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Whether this survey is required depends on a formal determination by Austin Energy Design. Applicant should confirm with AE Design whether a proximity survey has been explicitly requested during the design coordination process.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Medium confidence (2/3 runs) — this requirement is conditional on AE Design having formally requested the survey; reviewer should confirm whether AE made such a request before requiring submission.

This is typically required when development is within or near AE clearance zones. Without evidence of AE Design requesting this survey, or documentation providing it, the requirement status is unclear. The applicability depends on whether AE Design specifically requested a proximity survey.

perRunFindings.reasoning: When AE Design requires proximity surveys to document customer facilities maintain required clearances from AE primary voltage facilities, this survey must be submitted per UCM § 1.10.3. Given the presence of transmission lines and the multiple clearance requirements documented on Sheet 3, AE Design may have required such a survey. The absence of this survey prevents verification of clearance compliance.

comments.title: AE Electric Meter and Service Drop Removal from Demolished Facility Not Documented
comments.comment: No documentation confirms that Austin Energy removed the existing electric meter and service drop from the former assisted living facility prior to its demolition in June 2022.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.10.13 requires the owner to contact Austin Energy before demolition to arrange removal of the existing electric service, meter, and service drop. The previous assisted living facility on the site had existing electric service and was demolished in June 2022. The Tree Removal & Demolition Plan (Sheet 8) does not document AE removal coordination, and no work request confirmation, meter pull notice, or AE removal letter is present in the supplementary documents. While demolition is already complete, the site plan submittal should include evidence that this coordination occurred.
comments.sheets: Tree Removal & Demolition Plan (Sheet 8)
comments.applicableArea: Demolition of former assisted living facility; existing electric service connection to demolished structure; demolition completed June 2022
comments.resolution: Provide documentation confirming Austin Energy removed the electric meter and service drop from the former facility prior to the June 2022 demolition. Acceptable documentation includes: a work order or service order confirmation from Austin Energy, a meter pull notice, or a letter from Austin Energy confirming the service disconnection and equipment removal. If such records are unavailable, contact Austin Energy to obtain a historical service record confirming the disconnection.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution requires documentation from Austin Energy confirming historical meter and service drop removal; applicant may need to contact AE Records to obtain service disconnection history for the former facility.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should verify whether UCM § 1.10.13 is enforceable retroactively given demolition was completed in June 2022 before the current site plan application.

perRunFindings.comment: Provide documentation that Austin Energy removed the existing electric meter and service drop from the demolished facility before demolition. If not yet removed, submit work request to AE and document the removal per UCM § 1.10.13.
applicableAreas: Demolition of existing facility with electric service
perRunFindings.observation: Project involves demolition (facility demolished June 2022 per facts.md). Existing facility was an assisted living center that required electric service, meter, and service drop. No documentation found on current site plan or in supplementary documents confirming: (1) Austin Energy removed the electric meter and service drop before/during demolition, (2) whether site plan sheets include coordination notes for AE removal, or (3) evidence that work request was submitted to AE for removal. Sheet 8 (Demolition Plan) does not clearly document this coordination.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.13 requires that 'Existing electric service, meter, and service drop not coordinated with AE for removal before demolition may proceed.' The regulation requires: (1) written verification that utilities are suitable/sufficient (if continuing), and (2) after demolition approval but before demolition, contact AE to arrange removal. While demolition is already complete (June 2022), the current site plan submittal should document that this coordination occurred. The absence of clear documentation is a deficiency.
